3LkAAAp6uA.one_liner: Optimistic FTRL with a discounted (N+1)-th order predictor and entropic regularization over a lifted strategy space, giving constant regret.
3LkAAAp6uA.problem: Existing uncoupled learning algorithms did not guarantee horizon-independent individual regret in arbitrary N-player normal form games because large oscillations of play remained.
3LkAAAp6uA.method: Higher-order optimism with discounting (HOOD) is a variant of OptFTRL that combines a discounted (N+1)-th order predictor with entropic regularization over a suitable lifting of the strategy space, designed to dampen large oscillations of the induced play.
3LkAAAp6uA.key_idea: Pair a discounted (N+1)-th order optimistic predictor with entropic regularization on a lifted strategy space to dampen oscillations of the play sequence in a controlled manner.
3LkAAAp6uA.evidence: Theoretical regret guarantee when all players use the algorithm in arbitrary N-player normal form games; reviewers note there are no experiments.
3LkAAAp6uA.claimed_gains: Guarantees O(N^3 log^2 K) individual regret, uniformly over the horizon of play, with up to K actions per player.
3LkAAAp6uA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree this is a significant theoretical result on the open problem of constant regret in general games, with an elegant match between the predictor and the lifted regularizer.
3LkAAAp6uA.main_concern: Practicality is doubtful: the N^3 dependence, very small step size, unclear complexity of the line search over lambda, and absence of any experiments.

CacgTMv4l5.one_liner: Prunes draft tokens across the whole batch using draft confidence and a profiled runtime cost model in speculative decoding
CacgTMv4l5.problem: Under high concurrency, long drafts from parallel drafting waste compute on rejected tokens, inflating verification cost and making speculative decoding suboptimal.
CacgTMv4l5.method: D-cut selects draft tokens across the entire batch (cross-request pruning), allocating verification budget by draft confidence, and uses a runtime cost model of the deployment environment (GPU, parallelism) to set the pruning depth.
CacgTMv4l5.key_idea: Rank draft positions globally across the batch by confidence and cut at a verification budget set by a profiled runtime cost model.
CacgTMv4l5.evidence: Experiments across dense and MoE models and multiple datasets under high concurrency, reporting mean accepted tokens and output-token throughput speedup against unpruned DFlash and fixed-ratio variants.
CacgTMv4l5.claimed_gains: Improves the average speedup from 1.26× to 1.65× under high concurrency.
CacgTMv4l5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation convincing and the paper well written, with the runtime-computed verification budget as the key contribution and gains across model scales and datasets.
CacgTMv4l5.main_concern: Baselines are few and the benefit of cross-request allocation over simpler pruning at equal budget is not shown, while D-cut appears applicable only to DFlash.

MC0c6Vsq91.one_liner: Adds low-amplitude perturbations that inject simple decoy structures, exploiting diffusion models' simplicity bias to block unauthorized 3D reconstruction.
MC0c6Vsq91.problem: Diffusion-based 3D reconstruction from 2D images lets adversaries infer sensitive structures such as proprietary 3D designs or confidential physical objects.
MC0c6Vsq91.method: Flatland injects simple structures (synthesized with VLM guidance per reviews) into 2D visual signals as low-amplitude perturbations, so unauthorized 3D diffusion models reconstruct the injected simple structure instead of the original. It needs no access to the target model when generating perturbations.
MC0c6Vsq91.key_idea: Exploit the observed simplicity bias (Law of Prägnanz) of 3D diffusion models by embedding simple decoy structures as perturbations that the model reconstructs instead of the real object.
MC0c6Vsq91.evidence: 10 public diffusion models across 11 datasets and 11 proprietary models, with ablations and robustness tests against simple transformations and noise filters.
MC0c6Vsq91.claimed_gains: Prevents 10 public diffusion models from reconstructing sensitive structures across 11 datasets and is validated on 11 proprietary models; no effect-size numbers are stated.
MC0c6Vsq91.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that protecting 3D structure from unauthorized reconstruction is an important, underexplored problem, and credit black-box applicability and wide model and dataset coverage with ablations.
MC0c6Vsq91.main_concern: The simplicity-bias explanation is only correlational and not separated from learned geometric priors, and baselines are mostly 2D protection methods rather than 3D-specific ones.

k8ijbuQ0VT.one_liner: SupraTITO learns sequence-conditioned implicit transfer operators for periodic peptide assemblies, propagating configurations over long physical intervals.
k8ijbuQ0VT.problem: Peptide assembly structure and dynamics depend on sequence, but MD is too costly for the long assembly timescales and vast sequence space.
k8ijbuQ0VT.method: Learns transferable implicit transfer operators conditioned on peptide sequence, molecular topology and periodic geometry, using a periodic-boundary-consistent displacement that keeps molecules intact, to propagate configurations over intervals much longer than an MD step.
k8ijbuQ0VT.key_idea: Condition a generative transfer operator on sequence, topology and periodic geometry so configurations advance over long physical time steps while molecules stay intact.
k8ijbuQ0VT.evidence: A dipeptide benchmark with held-out sequences, comparisons against direct ensemble and observable prediction baselines trained on the same trajectories, and generalization across peptide concentrations including dilute conditions.
k8ijbuQ0VT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending generative MD to many-molecule supramolecular assembly is a new and important direction with solid structural results and a careful held-out evaluation.
k8ijbuQ0VT.main_concern: Dynamics claims need more evidence: results use only a 2.5 ns lag, no assembly rate is compared with MD, the MD reference is a single run per sequence, and baselines are limited.

OBaXUJDxsu.one_liner: Models users leaving after privacy leakage and shows a finite differential-privacy budget can maximize long-term mean-estimation utility.
OBaXUJDxsu.problem: The claim that privacy protection sustains participation and improves long-term utility has not been formalized.
OBaXUJDxsu.method: Introduces performative privacy, where data leakage reduces future participation, and analyzes agents who repeatedly contribute data for mean estimation under local and centralized DP and may leave when their data is leaked.
OBaXUJDxsu.key_idea: Couple a leakage-participation feedback loop with differential-privacy noise so the privacy budget trades estimation noise against retained participants.
OBaXUJDxsu.evidence: A theoretical study of the dynamics (Bernoulli estimation, mean estimation and ridge regression per reviews) and numerical experiments on synthetic data.
OBaXUJDxsu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper formalizes a new, well-motivated problem and gives rigorous theoretical analysis of how privacy leakage drives participation dynamics.
OBaXUJDxsu.main_concern: Strong simplifying assumptions (fixed data distribution, per-step independence, no composition or differencing attacks) and synthetic-only experiments limit evidence for real feedback loops.

vN99xccsXA.one_liner: Accelerate Bench evaluates coding agents on 32 application-level CPU optimization tasks with private verification of correctness and speedup.
vN99xccsXA.problem: Existing evaluations do not test whether coding agents can discover and coordinate changes across a complete program to speed it up while preserving the required computation.
vN99xccsXA.method: 32 CPU tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions each give a working program and specify workload, correctness requirements, timing boundaries and permitted edits. Public tests support iteration and a separate verifier scores the final submission.
vN99xccsXA.key_idea: Define tasks by workload and correctness rather than by prescribed edits, so agents choose where to optimize, and use controlled replays to show build settings and code changes interact.
vN99xccsXA.evidence: On benchmark version 1.1, 16 coding agents (model plus harness pairs) are evaluated, with controlled replays of build and runtime settings.
vN99xccsXA.claimed_gains: Score@1 ranges from 25.5% to 67.4%; the two leading agents are at least 2x faster on 22 or more of the 32 tasks, the other fourteen reach 2x on 8 to 17, and 125 of their 412 correct outcomes fall below 1.25x.
vN99xccsXA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a realistic end-to-end optimization benchmark with whole-application correctness checks and useful insights into how agents optimize.
vN99xccsXA.main_concern: Ranking stability is unclear because most results use one run per agent and task while timing can be noisy, and the scaled-down CPU tasks may not represent the original workloads.

0uhzMXFKjp.one_liner: TTS-AE learns dense non-negative concept features and sparsifies only at test time, selecting input-specific concepts to a requested fidelity.
0uhzMXFKjp.problem: Sparse autoencoders couple feature learning with a sparsity constraint, and it is unclear whether sparsity is needed in the representation itself.
0uhzMXFKjp.method: TTS-AE learns a dense, non-negative reconstructive representation from data-grounded directions. Test-Time Sparsification then selects an input-specific set of concept coordinates and uses their observed values with the learned covariance structure to reconstruct the representation to a requested fidelity.
0uhzMXFKjp.key_idea: Keep the learned concept dictionary dense and choose a sparse input-specific subset at explanation time, inferring the rest through learned covariance.
0uhzMXFKjp.evidence: Three model-dataset pairs compared with nonlinear sparse autoencoders and sparse approximation baselines, reporting higher semantic-quality scores for dense features and matched fidelity with fewer positively activated concepts, plus covariance-aware interventions and sparse global explanations.
0uhzMXFKjp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating dense feature learning from explanation sparsity is a clear, well-motivated reframing, with dense dictionaries scoring better than SAEs on semantic-quality metrics and supporting steering.
0uhzMXFKjp.main_concern: The sparsity comparison is not like-for-like: TTS counts only concepts left active after refitting (two in Figure 2) although its search selects 617 coordinates, which may overstate sparsity against SAEs.

uAL5VSL9fC.one_liner: Trains composed image retrieval from image-text-text triplets by adding source-image preservation supervision and Chord scoring in a frozen image space.
uAL5VSL9fC.problem: Zero-shot composed image retrieval trained with target captions can lose source-image details that should be preserved.
uAL5VSL9fC.method: PACT learns from image-text-text triplets without target images or gallery updates, aligning composed queries with target captions while preserving source evidence through visual supervision. Chord scoring combines target similarity with source-relative directional agreement in the frozen image space.
uAL5VSL9fC.key_idea: Add source-image visual supervision (with negative-caption discrimination) to target-caption alignment, and rank by target similarity plus source-relative directional agreement.
uAL5VSL9fC.evidence: Four ZS-CIR benchmarks across datasets, backbone scales, and external galleries, with ablation studies.
uAL5VSL9fC.claimed_gains: Strong retrieval performance across four ZS-CIR benchmarks, backbone scales, and external galleries; no figures stated.
uAL5VSL9fC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation clear and the method intuitive, with each loss component well motivated and demonstrated on several datasets with ablations.
uAL5VSL9fC.main_concern: Reviewers question whether averaging modified queries isolates shared visual information, and one notes Table 1 omits DiffComp, which outperforms PACT on FashionIQ and CIRR.

QeRq8zo3fu.one_liner: Sorting-free 3D Gaussian rendering via hybrid primitive and fragment stochastic sampling plus a Gaussian-aware spatiotemporal reconstruction network.
QeRq8zo3fu.problem: 3DGS needs depth sorting and ordered alpha blending, and stochastic transparency avoids sorting but produces heavy spatial and temporal noise at low sample counts.
QeRq8zo3fu.method: Gaussian Stippling converts continuous Gaussian splats into discrete stochastic visibility samples on unmodified 3DGS assets, adaptively combining primitive-based and fragment-based stippling. A lightweight reconstruction network uses the Gaussian attributes retained by each stipple to aggregate samples across space and time and suppress noise.
QeRq8zo3fu.key_idea: Route each Gaussian to primitive-based or fragment-based stochastic sampling by cost, then denoise sparse samples with a network that reads per-stipple Gaussian attributes across space and time.
QeRq8zo3fu.evidence: Experiments on unseen scenes showing generalization of a network trained on diverse scenes (the abstract is cut off); reviews mention DL3DV scenes, mobile devices, and mobile NPU deployment.
QeRq8zo3fu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find revisiting stochastic transparency for order-independent Gaussian rendering interesting, the hybrid sampling effective for throughput, and the lightweight reconstruction network effective at low sample counts on mobile hardware.
QeRq8zo3fu.main_concern: The speed advantage is not compared against strongly optimized sorted-alpha renderers, and temporal stability (flicker) evaluation is weak.

4JoJwdXxtO.one_liner: Node injection attack on hyperedge prediction using a ranking objective and dual-level distribution constraints to stay in-distribution.
4JoJwdXxtO.problem: Group-level aggregation weakens injected-node influence (perturbation attenuation) and injection shifts membership- and hyperedge-level statistics (distributional deviation), so existing attacks are weak or detectable on hyperedge prediction.
4JoJwdXxtO.method: DPHIA uses an adaptive ranking-based objective to perturb the decision boundary between positive and negative hyperedges, plus a dual-level adversarial component that, per reviews, constrains membership- and hyperedge-level distribution measures.
4JoJwdXxtO.key_idea: Flip candidate hyperedge rankings with an adaptive ranking loss while regularizing injected nodes to match membership- and hyperedge-level statistics.
4JoJwdXxtO.evidence: Multiple victim models, surrogate architectures and negative-sampling strategies, component ablations, and defense filtering on citation-style datasets such as Citeseer and Cora per reviews.
4JoJwdXxtO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree hyperedge-prediction robustness is an underexplored problem and the attack design follows from the attenuation and deviation analysis, with broad empirical support.
4JoJwdXxtO.main_concern: The stealthiness evaluation is circular, since the attack and the defenses use the same distribution measures, and the theory is limited to max-min pooling.

rwXDHw7vxW.one_liner: Benchmark of 10,071 agricultural grounding queries framed as generalized set prediction with box and mask tasks and target-absent abstention.
rwXDHw7vxW.problem: Agricultural targets are small, repetitive, occluded or irregular and instructions may refer to one, many or no objects, so evaluation must test localization, target-set completeness and abstention.
rwXDHw7vxW.method: AgroVG combines ten source datasets across six target families into 10,071 image-query pairs with bounding-box (T1) and instance-mask (T2) tasks and single-target, multi-target and target-absent queries, with task-specific box-set and mask protocols.
rwXDHw7vxW.key_idea: Formulate grounding as generalized set prediction: return all matching instances or abstain, scored for localization, set completeness and existence-aware abstention.
rwXDHw7vxW.evidence: 26 model configurations on expert-reviewed annotations with separate development and test sets, mask audits and query-level validation per reviews.
rwXDHw7vxW.claimed_gains: Benchmark paper: the abstract reports 10,071 image-query pairs from ten source datasets across six target families and no model performance numbers.
rwXDHw7vxW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark covers an underexplored problem with multi-source data, multi-target and absent-target queries, and thorough validation.
rwXDHw7vxW.main_concern: Most queries come from templates that may not reflect natural agricultural instructions, and novelty is mainly dataset integration under an established set-prediction formulation.

68zYhCYwA1.one_liner: Measures marginal return of pyramid depth, width and resolution for small objects, then reallocates capacity without adding modules.
68zYhCYwA1.problem: Detectors inherit capacity allocation across pyramid depth, channel width and input resolution from general-purpose design, though small instances exceed 70% of objects in UAV, remote-sensing and traffic imagery.
68zYhCYwA1.method: They vary each axis in turn, measure marginal return per unit of compute, trace the pattern to effective feature area (inverse to squared pyramid stride, quadratic in input scale), and derive a three-step transformation that adds no modules; reviews describe moving prediction to P2, compressing deep channels and using 960 input resolution.
68zYhCYwA1.key_idea: Effective feature area a target occupies on its prediction grid, scaling inversely with squared stride and quadratically with input scale, predicts whether deep heads, channels or resolution pay off.
68zYhCYwA1.evidence: VisDrone axis sweeps, a COCO counter-experiment, YOLOv11 and D-FINE variants, five other datasets and deployment-hardware measurements per reviews.
68zYhCYwA1.claimed_gains: R-YOLOv11-L matches an identically resolved baseline on VisDrone (41.5 versus 40.8 AP50) with 96% fewer parameters and 76% less compute and runs 2.3x faster; R-D-FINE-L gains 5.1 AP50.
68zYhCYwA1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reallocating capacity rather than adding modules is an interesting perspective, with large efficiency gains at comparable accuracy across datasets and architectures.
68zYhCYwA1.main_concern: The configuration is tuned on VisDrone alone, the explanation for stranded capacity is mostly qualitative, and some comparisons change input resolution and lack multi-seed results.

gIL85FnRcA.one_liner: Teacher-free diffusion training weighting a high-noise path by its error gap to a low-noise reference from the same model.
gIL85FnRcA.problem: Diffusion training lacks an internal signal that identifies hard samples without external demonstrations or teacher networks.
gIL85FnRcA.method: SALD evaluates each image-caption pair at two noise levels with the same model, using the lower-noise path without gradient as a reference; Advantage-Guided Diffusion turns the error difference into a sample-level weight, Temporal Advantage Memory adapts the noise gap over training, and Spectral Advantage Decomposition builds frequency-derived latent-element weights.
gIL85FnRcA.key_idea: Use the error difference between easy and hard noise-level paths of one model as an advantage that reweights the hard-path loss per sample and per frequency.
gIL85FnRcA.evidence: Multiple backbones, model sizes, resolutions and datasets (MultiGen-20M mentioned in a review), FID comparisons, wall-clock-matched and 100k-step longer-training comparisons, and ablations.
gIL85FnRcA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is intuitive, needs no teacher, extra parameters or inference changes, and is supported by broad experiments and ablations.
gIL85FnRcA.main_concern: The method is unclear in places (gradient flow through the weight contradicts a reported ablation, and the SAD gate may be negative or weakly motivated), and novelty over difficulty-based sample reweighting is not established.

BP4U7GABJ8.one_liner: Trains spatial agents on same-scene outputs of two perception models so decision margins shift only when the right action changes.
BP4U7GABJ8.problem: Perception models are replaced after an agent is trained, and quality cues like depth spread rise both at real scene edges and with noisier models, so agents trained on one model's outputs underreact to a new model.
BP4U7GABJ8.method: CapSwap-Bench replays real model replacements on matched scenes with switch and retain pairs; CAPAgent trains on outputs of two models for the same scene and query so their difference isolates the model change, learning how decision margins should move within pairs, and reads one output at deployment.
BP4U7GABJ8.key_idea: Pair outputs of two perception models on the same scene so quality-cue changes can only come from the model, and supervise decision-margin movement across the task threshold.
BP4U7GABJ8.evidence: CapSwap-Bench with switch and retain pairs, compared with matched single-output training, domain generalization methods and alternative pair losses, with matched deferral-budget controls per reviews.
BP4U7GABJ8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the perception-model replacement problem is practically meaningful and that same-scene paired training with decision-margin supervision is well designed and clearly implemented.
BP4U7GABJ8.main_concern: Generalization depends on informative quality cues and calibrated references (predicted intervals reach 85.2% coverage on unseen providers versus a 90% target), and predefined task thresholds limit applicability.

wysmFFCOQ0.one_liner: Policy-gradient (REINFORCE) learning of budget-conditioned schedules choosing which diffusion steps to fully recompute under feature caching.
wysmFFCOQ0.problem: Feature-caching schedules for diffusion inference are not chosen to preserve fidelity to uncached outputs and to maximize generation quality under a fixed budget of full model evaluations.
wysmFFCOQ0.method: ReCache trains a budget-conditioned scheduling policy with REINFORCE, combining an output-fidelity objective with a generation-quality reward, without labeled data or backpropagation through the full denoising trajectory. It supports feature reuse and forecasting, and one trained policy per model and caching mechanism adapts across budgets at inference time.
wysmFFCOQ0.key_idea: A REINFORCE-trained policy conditioned on the compute budget selects which diffusion steps to fully recompute, rewarded by fidelity to uncached output and generation quality.
wysmFFCOQ0.evidence: Experiments on FLUX.1-dev, HunyuanVideo, and Wan2.1 compare against caching baselines including DiCache, DPCache, LeMiCa, and uniform HiCache.
wysmFFCOQ0.claimed_gains: On FLUX.1-dev, LPIPS drops 31% versus DiCache at a 5.04x FLOPs reduction; on Wan2.1 at a 3.50x FLOPs reduction, LPIPS drops 45% and VBench rises 6.77 points over uniform HiCache.
wysmFFCOQ0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework practical, well structured, and strong empirically across several models, with one policy serving multiple budgets and both reuse and forecasting mechanisms.
wysmFFCOQ0.main_concern: Comparisons and attribution are incomplete: no comparison to related learned-caching work such as ECAD and RL-based caching controllers, and ablations do not isolate the source of the gains.

9jX7SBDfMl.one_liner: Analyzes REINFORCE that updates its rollout distribution every S gradient steps as stage-wise KL minimization toward reward-weighted targets
9jX7SBDfMl.problem: On-policy sampling is viewed as crucial for policy gradient success, yet reward-guided self-training works even when the rollout distribution is updated infrequently, and theory for these off-policy methods is limited.
9jX7SBDfMl.method: The paper studies RE(S), a generalized REINFORCE that updates the rollout distribution once every S≥1 gradient steps, interpreting it as stage-wise optimization where each stage takes S gradient steps minimizing the KL distance to a fixed reward-weighted rollout distribution.
9jX7SBDfMl.key_idea: Treat each block of S gradient steps as minimizing KL to a fixed reward-weighted rollout distribution, giving a unified analysis of on-policy and off-policy updates.
9jX7SBDfMl.evidence: Theory for multi-arm bandits with softmax policies plus numerical experiments; reviewers describe the study as idealized, using population objectives.
9jX7SBDfMl.claimed_gains: For any fixed S, RE(S) enjoys global convergence to the optimal policy as the number of rollout distribution updates grows; the other findings are cut off in the batch abstract, and a reviewer cites matching Θ(1/T) rates in total gradient steps.
9jX7SBDfMl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and gives a timely theoretical analysis of off-policy REINFORCE, with global convergence and an interesting on-policy versus off-policy separation for poorly initialized policies.
9jX7SBDfMl.main_concern: Reviewers say the study is restricted to an idealized setting (softmax bandits, population objectives) with limited experiments, and the rate constants depend on a small trajectory-dependent optimal-action probability that may itself depend on S.

CqNmaUE2kf.one_liner: Shows neural classifiers identify the source dataset of human-LLM conversations from user messages alone, and traces consequences for user models
CqNmaUE2kf.problem: It is unclear how different human-LLM interaction datasets are from one another and what those differences mean for research, including user modeling, built on them.
CqNmaUE2kf.method: Across seven conversation datasets (in-the-wild chat logs and human preference data), the authors revisit the Torralba and Efros dataset classification experiment with neural classifiers on user messages, test separability after matching on taxonomy dimensions, and study effects on user-model outputs, evaluation, and data selection.
CqNmaUE2kf.key_idea: Dataset-source classifiers on user messages reveal signatures that persist after matching on human-designed taxonomies, and these signatures propagate into trained user models.
CqNmaUE2kf.evidence: Seven conversation datasets, classification with input ablations and taxonomy-matched controls, and experiments on user-model outputs, evaluation of user models, and classifier-guided training data selection.
CqNmaUE2kf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is important and well motivated, and that extensive ablations show dataset signatures persist after removing obvious cues.
CqNmaUE2kf.main_concern: Reviewers say the paper does not characterize which features drive the signatures beyond broad categories, the taxonomy matching leaves co-occurrences and length distributions uncontrolled, and the separability itself is unsurprising.

cFWYzh6OkV.one_liner: Proves global polynomial filters only halve the depth message-passing networks need to match color refinement: exactly floor(m/2) layers.
cFWYzh6OkV.problem: Message-passing networks can need m-1 layers to match color refinement on graphs whose stable coloring has m classes, and it was open how much depth global filters remove.
cFWYzh6OkV.method: The paper proves that with any filters that are polynomials in the adjacency matrix, arbitrary update functions, and unbounded width, exactly floor(m/2) layers are needed in the worst case, with an explicit matching lower-bound construction.
cFWYzh6OkV.key_idea: Filtering can separate color classes without producing their indicator vectors, and only a nonlinearity supplies those indicators, so nonlinear updates set the required depth.
cFWYzh6OkV.evidence: Theoretical proofs of an upper bound and a matching lower-bound construction; no experiments are stated.
cFWYzh6OkV.claimed_gains: Global filters reduce the worst-case depth from m-1 to exactly floor(m/2) layers.
cFWYzh6OkV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exact worst-case result is solid and interesting, with explicit constructions and a matching lower bound that holds for arbitrary polynomial filters, unrestricted width, and arbitrary updates.
cFWYzh6OkV.main_concern: The result relies on a highly permissive model (arbitrary updates, unbounded width, graph-dependent filters) and the presentation is hard to follow, so applicability to practical GNNs is unclear.

ZMiccB7An1.one_liner: CivWorldBench tests LLM world models in Freeciv via association forecasting, belief inference, and intervention prediction with recorded hidden states.
ZMiccB7An1.problem: Real-world forecasting benchmarks lack hidden-state ground truth and controlled experiments, so they cannot assess LLM world-model capabilities beyond predictive accuracy.
ZMiccB7An1.method: A benchmark on a multi-agent strategy game engine with recorded internal states, controlled observations, and paired intervention rollouts, containing 1,900 decision points from 475 worlds at three task levels. Reference predictors, an expert harness, and empirical ceiling estimates contextualize scores, and agent-play experiments test whether the capabilities help decision-making.
ZMiccB7An1.key_idea: Use a game engine's logged hidden states and paired counterfactual rollouts to give verifiable ground truth for belief inference and intervention effects.
ZMiccB7An1.evidence: Eleven frontier language models evaluated on 1,900 decision points from 475 worlds, with correlation analysis against real-world forecasting leaderboards and agent-play experiments.
ZMiccB7An1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark is comprehensive and verifiable, covering forecasting, hidden-state inference, and intervention prediction in one environment with logged internal states and paired rollouts.
ZMiccB7An1.main_concern: Statistical significance and generality are unclear: benchmark noise from game mechanics and sampling is under-reported, downstream decision-making gains are not significant, and all dynamics come from one simulator with bot agents.

1gOKz5MrW4.one_liner: Structural balancing yields a supervised contrastive objective that provably forms a regular simplex under long-tailed class distributions.
1gOKz5MrW4.problem: Supervised contrastive learning (SCL) and balanced variants (BCL) are assumed to give regular-simplex representations under long-tailed data, but their optima still depend on the number of samples per class.
1gOKz5MrW4.method: Gives a theoretical framework for whether a regular simplex forms at the optimum and shows SCL and BCL fail because they remain dependent on per-class sample counts. It then introduces structural balancing and a fully balanced contrastive objective (FBCL) that provably forms a regular simplex at its optimum.
1gOKz5MrW4.key_idea: Remove the remaining per-class sample-count dependence from the contrastive objective through structural balancing, so its optimum is a regular simplex.
1gOKz5MrW4.evidence: Theoretical analysis of representative objectives plus empirical results on long-tailed recognition and transfer learning (ImageNet-LT and iNaturalist per the reviews).
1gOKz5MrW4.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says only that the method yields a more balanced representation space and improves long-tailed recognition and transfer learning performance.
1gOKz5MrW4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis exposing the remaining class-count dependence in SCL and BCL is consequential and that the simple FBCL fix is principled, with consistent improvements.
1gOKz5MrW4.main_concern: The theory assumes every mini-batch contains all classes and a sufficiently large feature dimension (violated on iNaturalist), so it is unclear that the simplex geometry explains the modest accuracy gains.

zExAi2JK6f.one_liner: Benchmarks vision-only long-horizon UAV navigation where agents must find and interpret scene-embedded semantic beacons, with a waypoint-planning MLLM baseline.
zExAi2JK6f.problem: Vision-and-language navigation needs route instructions that require prior knowledge, while image-goal navigation breaks down when the target stays out of view during long outdoor UAV flights.
zExAi2JK6f.method: VoLN keeps image-goal specification but requires discovering and integrating en-route semantic beacons. VoLN-UAV has 7,210 episodes in 17 simulated environments with active and passive beacons, and VoLN-MLLM separates waypoint planning (a Vicuna-based planner predicting 3D waypoints) from visual target confirmation.
zExAi2JK6f.key_idea: Specify the goal only by image and make en-route semantic beacons the guidance signal, with waypoint planning decoupled from visual target confirmation.
zExAi2JK6f.evidence: VoLN-UAV benchmark with continuous 3D navigation and held-out environment evaluation; results are cut off in the available abstract.
zExAi2JK6f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task is a meaningful, robotics-motivated extension of image-goal navigation using en-route semantic guidance.
zExAi2JK6f.main_concern: Experiments do not show that the benchmark or model actually tests interpreting successive beacons while ignoring distractors, and the method depends on a fixed semantic bank.

dmXYZPyw2C.one_liner: OpAI-Bench builds nine cumulative human-to-AI revision versions per document with five edit operations and multi-granularity authorship labels for detector evaluation.
dmXYZPyw2C.problem: Existing AI-text detection benchmarks focus on final outputs and say little about how AI authorship signals emerge or fade during progressive human-AI co-editing.
dmXYZPyw2C.method: Starting from human documents, the benchmark creates nine sequentially revised versions under predefined AI coverage levels and five AI edit operations across four domains. Provenance is kept at document, sentence, token and span granularity.
dmXYZPyw2C.key_idea: Apply operation-guided AI edits cumulatively over predefined coverage levels so authorship provenance is preserved at every intermediate revision.
dmXYZPyw2C.evidence: Evaluation of 8 document-level, 7 sentence-level and 2 token/span-level detectors over four domains (about 280K samples per a review).
dmXYZPyw2C.claimed_gains: No gains stated; findings are that detectability depends on edit operation, domain and revision history, and mixed-authorship intermediate versions are often harder to detect than fully human or heavily AI-edited endpoints.
dmXYZPyw2C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a useful resource that goes beyond static human-versus-AI detection by providing intermediate versions, provenance and analysis across stages and domains.
dmXYZPyw2C.main_concern: Novelty is limited because only the cumulative trajectory is new and no task uses it, and shuffled-sentence editing departs from realistic left-to-right revision.

MDOMCmtk8c.one_liner: Shows a single autoregressive neuron with CoT can simulate feedforward circuits and Turing machines, via a Sidon-set construction.
MDOMCmtk8c.problem: It is unclear how simple a next-token predictor can be while still performing general computation through its autoregressively generated chain of thought.
MDOMCmtk8c.method: Proves that for threshold, ReLU, and related activations a single autoregressive neuron of dimension O(ns+s^2) simulates a size-s circuit on n inputs in O(s^2) generation steps, independent of circuit depth, and shows the simulation is efficiently learnable from CoT supervision.
MDOMCmtk8c.key_idea: A Sidon-set construction resolves parameter sharing across gates, so one neuron reuses its weights for every circuit gate over the generation steps.
MDOMCmtk8c.evidence: Theorems on simulation bounds, tightness under natural assumptions, and learning from CoT supervision; reviews mention experiments fitting ReLU circuits with Adam.
MDOMCmtk8c.claimed_gains: Neuron dimension O(ns+s^2) and O(s^2) generation steps for a size-s circuit on n inputs, independent of circuit depth, improving on Joshi et al. (COLT 2025) whose bounds scale exponentially with circuit depth.
MDOMCmtk8c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the minimal-capability question interesting and the Sidon-set construction a simple fix with polynomial overhead, in a clear, well-written paper with learning results from CoT supervision.
MDOMCmtk8c.main_concern: The significance over existing CoT universality results is unclear, and the learning bounds (for example a sample bound of order s^6/epsilon for ReLU circuits) are too large to show learnability of large networks.

6asxf3QBCZ.one_liner: Zero-shot inference-time intervention using kinematic-mask subspaces to strengthen visual evidence and filter textual priors in VideoLLMs.
6asxf3QBCZ.problem: VideoLLMs over-rely on textual priors rather than visual evidence (vision-knowledge conflicts), as language priors progressively dominate the residual stream in deeper layers, especially on counterfactual-physics videos.
6asxf3QBCZ.method: VERTEX isolates physical motion into binary kinematic masks used to build latent geometric subspaces, then at inference rebalances the model by strengthening focus on visual evidence while filtering out parametric textual biases. Reviews describe a two-stream intervention on the residual stream through orthogonal projections.
6asxf3QBCZ.key_idea: Build motion subspaces from binary kinematic masks and intervene on the residual stream to boost visual evidence while suppressing the textual priors carried by deep-layer MLP outputs.
6asxf3QBCZ.evidence: Counterfactual physics benchmarks (VideoHallu-Physics and VideoPHY2-Movement per reviews) across multiple model families, with mechanistic analyses (Logit Lens, Visual Knockout), ablations, and qualitative analyses.
6asxf3QBCZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important and the modular inference-time method is tied to solid mechanistic analysis, evaluated on multiple model families with ablations.
6asxf3QBCZ.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons with existing inference-time hallucination-mitigation methods, inconsistent Qwen3-VL-8B numbers between Tables 1 and 2, and ablations where simpler variants beat the full framework.

5k57TFSnja.one_liner: Survey synthesizing over 150 works on post-training reasoning data: forms, usefulness, construction, and scaling.
5k57TFSnja.problem: Research on reasoning data for post-training has grown rapidly, but the evidence remains fragmented.
5k57TFSnja.method: The primer organizes over 150 works around four questions (what forms reasoning data take, what makes them useful, how they are constructed, what scaling studies establish) across mathematics, code, science, and interactive tasks, comparing apparently conflicting findings and distilling seven practical lessons and reporting recommendations.
5k57TFSnja.key_idea: Compare conflicting findings under explicit conditions such as learner, target, update rule, and route, to explain when each conclusion holds.
5k57TFSnja.evidence: Literature synthesis of over 150 works across mathematics, code, science, and interactive tasks; reviewers note there is no new method, data, or experiment.
5k57TFSnja.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the survey is well organized, covers a broad range of reasoning-data practices, records the conditions behind reported comparisons, and will be useful to the community.
5k57TFSnja.main_concern: Reviewers say the paper adds no new experiment or quantitative pooling, leaves its central claim untested, cites two mid-2025 works that one reviewer says were debunked, and does not clearly distinguish itself from existing data-centric surveys.

i4U0mlO3QB.one_liner: Closed-form theory for continual linear regression: optimal step size decays as ln T / T and matches tuned L2 regularization.
i4U0mlO3QB.problem: How step size (implicit regularization) and explicit regularization should be set in high-dimensional continual linear regression over a sequence of tasks is not characterized.
i4U0mlO3QB.method: They derive an explicit closed-form generalization loss for gradient descent with a fixed number of steps per task and arbitrary teachers, then extend the analysis to generalized ridge regression with diagonal regularization matrices.
i4U0mlO3QB.key_idea: A closed-form generalization loss for sequential gradient descent shows the optimal fixed step size acts like optimally tuned isotropic L2 regularization, with conditions for when diagonal regularizers differ.
i4U0mlO3QB.evidence: Theory (random matrix theory), with predictions corroborated by experiments on linear models and neural networks.
i4U0mlO3QB.claimed_gains: The optimal fixed step size decays nearly as ln T / T and yields asymptotically the same generalization loss as optimally tuned L2 regularization; no empirical numbers stated.
i4U0mlO3QB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the results are insightful, technically sound and clearly written for continual-learning theory, covering optimal step size and regularization structure.
i4U0mlO3QB.main_concern: Reviewers question whether linear-model results transfer to practical neural networks, and one flags possible inconsistencies in the proofs of Theorems 1, 3 and 4.

T4oBTPoLnA.one_liner: Turns natural-language requirements into an executable model, then generates model-conditioned search operators for adaptive large neighborhood search.
T4oBTPoLnA.problem: Language-to-optimization systems treat mathematical models only as solver inputs and do not use the model's constraint structure to guide how solutions are built and improved.
T4oBTPoLnA.method: AutoHOpt recovers a source-reviewed executable model (OPTSPEC), then uses its decisions and constraints to generate SEARCHIR, a task-specific search program. With the model fixed, execution feedback refines initialization and neighborhood-repair operators that run inside adaptive large neighborhood search with no per-iteration LLM calls.
T4oBTPoLnA.key_idea: Use the accepted executable model's decisions and constraints to generate initialization and repair operators for ALNS, refined by execution feedback while the model stays fixed.
T4oBTPoLnA.evidence: Ten external benchmarks plus the authors' CoPBench, with ablations and common-budget controls on modeling feedback and model-conditioned search.
T4oBTPoLnA.claimed_gains: Highest mean zero-gap success on eight of ten external benchmarks; 83.5% on IndustryOR and 78.8% on MIPLIB-NL, ahead of the strongest baseline by 20.2 and 9.5 percentage points.
T4oBTPoLnA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see linking model recovery to search design as a useful idea backed by extensive benchmarks, many baselines and strong reported results.
T4oBTPoLnA.main_concern: The method is under-specified and hard to follow (prompts, agent interactions, CoPBench variants), and it is unclear why generating search operators beats sending the same OptSpec to a conventional solver.

Jo6U0y2omr.one_liner: Re-scores fine-tuning data for safety risk at the current model state each round, since sample risk depends on model state.
Jo6U0y2omr.problem: Safety filters for fine-tuning data score samples once on the initial model and keep that selection, assuming the initial ranking stays informative as the model changes, even though benign fine-tuning can weaken safety alignment.
Jo6U0y2omr.method: SABA re-scores the training pool at the current model state in each round and treats filtering as an allocation of a fixed training budget across rounds, using existing criteria such as GradShield for scoring (per reviews). The motivation is that the initialization risk ranking is almost uncorrelated with the ranking two epochs later, and a matched intervention shows the same benign groups cause different safety degradation at different model states.
Jo6U0y2omr.key_idea: Recompute per-sample safety-risk scores at the current model state every round and allocate a fixed training budget across rounds, rather than reusing the initialization ranking.
Jo6U0y2omr.evidence: Controlled fine-tuning runs, a matched intervention on benign sample groups, and filtering comparisons under matched sample-pass budgets on 8B models with LoRA, two instruction datasets and harmful-request benchmarks (per reviews).
Jo6U0y2omr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the diagnosis that sample-level safety risk changes with model state is well tested, with a matched intervention going beyond ranking correlations and a controlled comparison against many static and dynamic baselines.
Jo6U0y2omr.main_concern: Evidence is limited to 8B LoRA fine-tuning, two instruction datasets and automatic judges, and the experiments show harm depends on model state but not clearly that the most harmful samples change during training.

QVudSYUo68.one_liner: JEPA pretraining for dynamic graphs using partial interaction masking and a sparse discrete-Morse reference forest of relations across a window.
QVudSYUo68.problem: On dynamic graphs, masking interactions also removes relational evidence needed for prediction, and changing interactions leave relations observed at other times unavailable as context.
QVudSYUo68.method: MoJEPA partially masks interactions so the model predicts missing evidence from the relations that remain visible. A Morse reference context uses discrete Morse theory to reduce the relations observed across a window to a sparse rooted forest, so relations seen at other times can support information exchange at the target time.
QVudSYUo68.key_idea: Reduce relations observed across a window to a sparse rooted forest using discrete Morse theory, and use it as extra predictive context in a JEPA with partially masked interactions.
QVudSYUo68.evidence: Temporal link prediction on nine datasets and eighteen within-domain transfer directions (per reviews), with ablations and experiments at different training budgets.
QVudSYUo68.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design of partial masking plus a reference forest is well motivated and clearly explained, with broad evaluation and competitive results.
QVudSYUo68.main_concern: Ablations do not compare the Morse reference forest against alternative sparse structures such as random or maximum-weight spanning trees, so the source of the gains is unclear.

c4Ev1YuUfc.one_liner: Routes multi-objective test-time alignment by scaling token-wise reward guidance with disagreement among objective-conditioned autoregressive reward models.
c4Ev1YuUfc.problem: Multi-objective test-time alignment with autoregressive reward models lacks a principled signal for when reward guidance should matter and how strongly it should override the base policy.
c4Ev1YuUfc.method: DIR measures disagreement among objective-conditioned next-token distributions with a generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence, which equals the mutual information between objective identity and the next token. It uses this to modulate the token-wise step size from the base policy along the requested preference direction, with no learned router, auxiliary model or fine-tuning.
c4Ev1YuUfc.key_idea: Set token-wise guidance strength from the generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence among objective-conditioned ARM next-token distributions, which marks cross-reward forks.
c4Ev1YuUfc.evidence: Experiments on safety alignment, cross-domain transfer and model scales, with two and three objectives, against baselines such as PARM and GenARM (per reviews).
c4Ev1YuUfc.claimed_gains: ARM disagreement is strongly correlated with downstream cross-reward separation (Spearman 0.766); the abstract states effective multi-objective alignment without gain magnitudes.
c4Ev1YuUfc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that disagreement among reward models is a simple, operational signal for where guidance matters and that DIR consistently outperforms baselines with two and three objectives.
c4Ev1YuUfc.main_concern: The advantage over a well-chosen constant guidance strength is not isolated: DIR's average guidance may be stronger than PARM's fixed setting, and no fixed-strength sweep or realized routing means are reported.

q6jK94FAuE.one_liner: Decouples scene state from camera by tokenizing multi-view geometry-foundation-model features into a queryable state that an autoregressive world model predicts.
q6jK94FAuE.problem: Geometry foundation model features depend on the view, entangling scene dynamics with camera-induced variation and making state evolution harder to predict.
q6jK94FAuE.method: A scene tokenizer aggregates multi-view GFM features into a view-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder queries with camera rays. An autoregressive world model predicts future scene states while camera motion is modeled separately, and a single context-derived scale is kept through the rollout.
q6jK94FAuE.key_idea: Aggregate multi-view GFM features into a camera-independent scene state decoded by ray queries, so forecasting predicts scene change while camera motion is modeled separately.
q6jK94FAuE.evidence: Waymo comparisons with prior 3D world models, zero-shot transfer to KITTI and nuScenes, cross-view query consistency, and ablations including Copy-Last baselines and representation comparisons (per reviews).
q6jK94FAuE.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports outperforming prior 3D world models on Waymo and zero-shot generalization to KITTI and nuScenes, without numbers).
q6jK94FAuE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the separation of forecasting a scene state from choosing a decoding camera is clear and well motivated, lets the same predicted state be queried from different viewpoints, and gives consistent gains across datasets.
q6jK94FAuE.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate the benefit of view decoupling: gains over Copy-Last are modest and shrink with horizon, representation ablations confound model capacity and decoder effects, and baseline conditions are unequal.

OqVp28czTz.one_liner: Time-conditioned autoregressive neural quantum state with exact initial condition and residual-based lower bounds on time-averaged fidelity.
OqVp28czTz.problem: Learning quantum dynamics by minimizing the Schrodinger residual leaves open what the residual implies about state accuracy.
OqVp28czTz.method: Abel-tNQS is a time-conditioned autoregressive neural quantum state with an exact initial-state constraint, and its complex conditional-amplitude construction preserves normalization and direct sampling. A linear Abel bound supplies a remaining-time weight (T-t) for a training surrogate, and a cumulative residual form gives a tighter post-training bound on time-averaged fidelity.
OqVp28czTz.key_idea: Weight the Schrodinger residual by remaining time (T-t) during training, and bound time-averaged fidelity from the cumulative residual after training.
OqVp28czTz.evidence: Full-basis evaluations on N=4,5,6 Ising chains, controlled N=10 ablations with ten seeds per setting comparing linear and uniform weighting and soft penalties, and observable benchmarks up to 20 spins, a 4x4 lattice, segmented continuation and time-dependent transverse fields.
OqVp28czTz.claimed_gains: Numerical lower-bound estimates between 0.9972 and 0.9999 on N=4,5,6 Ising chains, and linear weighting reduces final mean magnetization and nearest-neighbor correlation errors by approximately 85% and 94% relative to uniform weighting at N=10.
OqVp28czTz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written with clearly stated assumptions and rigorous math, and consider the ten-seed controlled ablation convincing evidence for the benefit of temporal weighting.
OqVp28czTz.main_concern: Prior work on global-in-time autoregressive neural representations of quantum dynamics is under-discussed, so the architectural novelty is unclear.

CwnWJy2XZr.one_liner: Cross-modal hashing under noisy labels that judges sample reliability against class centers built from historically reliable samples.
CwnWJy2XZr.problem: Noise-robust cross-modal hashing estimates reliability from signals of the current model (loss, confidence, neighborhoods), so label noise biases the estimate and errors accumulate during training.
CwnWJy2XZr.method: Memory-guided Reliability Estimation (MRE) keeps modality-specific historical class centers, scores current samples by bidirectional cross-modal matching, splits them with a smooth threshold, and updates memory only with reliable samples. Reliable Cross-batch Learning (RCL) uses in-batch and historical cross-batch relations, plus uncertainty-aware learning for unreliable samples.
CwnWJy2XZr.key_idea: Estimate current-sample reliability against memory class centers updated only with historically reliable samples, instead of against signals from the noise-affected current model.
CwnWJy2XZr.evidence: Results on four datasets with multiple hash code lengths and component analyses (variants such as Current-batch and Historical-all compared by AUROC, Precision and Memory Purity), as described in the reviews; the abstract is truncated before the results.
CwnWJy2XZr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using historically reliable samples as a stable reference is well motivated, clearly formulated, and supported by broad experiments and component analyses.
CwnWJy2XZr.main_concern: The reliability threshold relies on an estimated noise rate, and behavior when the true noise rate is unknown (and under early memory contamination) is not validated.

QuDOzA1Mmj.one_liner: Tighter analysis of Fastfood shows near-subgaussian concentration for random Fourier features computed in O((d+m) log d) time.
QuDOzA1Mmj.problem: Structured random-feature maps are faster than the O(md) cost of i.i.d. features, but earlier analyses gave weaker concentration guarantees.
QuDOzA1Mmj.method: Re-analyzes the Fastfood feature map of Le, Sarlos and Smola using Brascamp-Lieb inequalities and the Schoenberg representation of radial kernels. This gives a feature map computable in near-linear time with near-subgaussian concentration, extended to radial kernels beyond the Gaussian.
QuDOzA1Mmj.key_idea: Bounds the moment-generating function of Hadamard-based Fastfood features via Brascamp-Lieb inequalities and Schoenberg's radial-kernel representation, removing dependence on the distance between inputs.
QuDOzA1Mmj.evidence: Theoretical proofs (Theorem 1.1, Lemma 3.6) for the Gaussian and other radial kernels; no experiments are described in the abstract or reviews.
QuDOzA1Mmj.claimed_gains: Random feature map computable in near-linear time O((d+m) log d) with near-subgaussian concentration, versus O(md) time for i.i.d. features.
QuDOzA1Mmj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a correct, tighter theoretical analysis of an established method, with exponentially decaying error terms and a useful lemma.
QuDOzA1Mmj.main_concern: The guarantees are pointwise for fixed input pairs, and the contribution is seen as incremental because the mechanism has been known for 13 years.

lWUM9JOGww.one_liner: Tailors the vector-quantization target space with query-guided weighting, cross-head normalization and covariance-aware grouping for 1-bit KV cache compression.
lWUM9JOGww.problem: Existing vector-quantization methods degrade substantially at 1-bit KV cache compression because each codebook must cover a larger group of channels with few centroids.
lWUM9JOGww.method: TaSQ combines query-guided channel weighting, cross-head normalization, and covariance-aware channel grouping before vector quantization. The transforms are RoPE-compatible and merge into projection weights and codebooks, so decoding stays a lookup; an SGLang implementation is provided.
lWUM9JOGww.key_idea: Reshapes cached channels before vector quantization by weighting by query-derived error sensitivity, normalizing across heads, and grouping by covariance, all folded offline into weights and codebooks.
lWUM9JOGww.evidence: General, long-chain-of-thought reasoning, and long-context retrieval benchmarks against low-bit KV cache VQ baselines, plus an SGLang serving implementation on a single RTX 6000 Ada GPU.
lWUM9JOGww.claimed_gains: On a single RTX 6000 Ada GPU, the SGLang implementation supports up to 14x larger batch sizes and 1.87x higher peak throughput than the BF16 baseline.
lWUM9JOGww.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that TaSQ gives strong 1-bit results, especially on long-context retrieval and long-CoT tasks, with a serving-aware design whose transforms fold offline.
lWUM9JOGww.main_concern: The component ablation covers only WikiText-2 perplexity (removing weighting or normalization changes it under 1%), so what drives the large retrieval and reasoning gains is unclear.

otD4wCnFKB.one_liner: Two-stage post-training of Protenix that adds eCLIP signals through supervised training and DiffusionNFT feedback for protein-RNA structures.
otD4wCnFKB.problem: Protein-RNA complex structures are scarce, while abundant eCLIP interaction data lack atomic resolution and are not used by structure prediction models.
otD4wCnFKB.method: Stage 1 post-trains Protenix on structural plus eCLIP data to learn binding-aware representations. Stage 2 adapts Diffusion Negative-aware Fine-Tuning (DiffusionNFT) to molecular structure generation, using eCLIP agreement and structural plausibility as feedback. The authors also build a set of 265,070 candidate protein-RNA pairs.
otD4wCnFKB.key_idea: Fine-tunes a pretrained structure diffusion model with reward feedback combining eCLIP agreement and structural plausibility via DiffusionNFT, after supervised training on mixed structure and eCLIP data.
otD4wCnFKB.evidence: A protein-RNA interface structure benchmark, a held-out test set of 190 experimental binding conditions, a check on other structural prediction tasks, and ablations (rep and nft baselines).
otD4wCnFKB.claimed_gains: Interface prediction success rate rises from 61.43% to 74.29%, interface RMSD falls from 7.61 Å to 5.02 Å, and peak F1 averaged across RBPs rises from 0.332 to 0.459.
otD4wCnFKB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that integrating eCLIP experimental signals into a pretrained structure model addresses an important protein-RNA problem and that the two-stage design is supported by ablations.
otD4wCnFKB.main_concern: The evaluation does not fully support the claims: Peak F1 allows any-overlap matching, there is no PDB-only fine-tuning or shuffled-eCLIP control, and the DockQ quality distribution is not reported.

USbMFtr7jD.one_liner: Non-Markovian uniform-state diffusion language models with a designable coupling between noise levels that preserves marginals.
USbMFtr7jD.problem: Uniform discrete diffusion language models fix a Markov coupling between noise levels, which jointly determines reverse dynamics, training objective, sampling behavior and likelihood evaluation.
USbMFtr7jD.method: NoMUD is a family of non-Markovian UDLMs whose coupling is made designable through two degrees of freedom while keeping the same marginals. The coupling is then tuned for likelihood evaluation, confidence-aware sampling, and few-step distillation.
USbMFtr7jD.key_idea: Parameterizes marginal-preserving non-Markovian couplings with two free variables; all couplings share one optimal predictor, so the coupling can be chosen at inference time.
USbMFtr7jD.evidence: Three settings: a tighter negative ELBO for likelihood evaluation, confidence-aware sampling, and learnable-coupling few-step distillation; reviews mention perplexity results in Table 2 including PTB.
USbMFtr7jD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the coupling perspective is clear and sensible, recovers Markov UDLM and absorbing diffusion as special cases, and is backed by reasonable experiments.
USbMFtr7jD.main_concern: Optimizing the coupling per example and time step makes the likelihood comparison unclear (which model is bounded, and whether it measures model quality or bound tightness), and only uniform-corruption models are evaluated.

1SqnHfZJja.one_liner: Diagnostic benchmark of 7K+ examples measuring VLM robustness to material, viewpoint, lighting and geometry stress in robot scenes.
1SqnHfZJja.problem: In embodied systems it is hard to tell whether a VLM failure comes from visual stress or from the underlying task or scene.
1SqnHfZJja.method: An image-formation-inspired taxonomy organizes stress into four dimensions (Material, Viewpoint, Lighting, Geometry) and 16 fine-grained categories. The benchmark has more than 7K examples from natural stress cases, targeted synthesis, and real-world collection, covering grounding, spatial reasoning, state understanding and action-selection-style QA, plus matched nominal-stressed pairs.
1SqnHfZJja.key_idea: Organizes visual stress by image-formation factors and pairs stressed scene-question instances with nominal versions, so degradation is measured on matched instances.
1SqnHfZJja.evidence: Evaluation of 16 VLMs across stress types and task formats; reviews also mention a rectification method (StressDART) tested on the benchmark.
1SqnHfZJja.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the image-formation taxonomy is intuitive and interpretable, and that matched nominal-stressed pairs are the strongest part of the benchmark.
1SqnHfZJja.main_concern: The matched-pair evidence is under-specified: the size, task and category composition of the verified subset, and how often edits break the question, are not clearly reported.

o8dMgzvbS7.one_liner: Source-aware benchmark for video-to-spatial audio with 1,274 annotated videos and 12 reference-free metrics in five dimensions.
o8dMgzvbS7.problem: Evaluation of video-to-spatial-audio models is mono-centric and scores the global scene rather than individual sound sources.
o8dMgzvbS7.method: A human-annotated dataset of 1,274 perspective and 360-degree videos (stereo, binaural, extended to first-order ambisonics), scored on semantics, temporal, spatial, acoustics and perceptual quality with 12 fine-grained, reference-free, human-aligned metrics.
o8dMgzvbS7.key_idea: Scores each sound source separately, gating spatial and temporal metrics on verified source presence using existing separation, recognition, synchronization and localization tools.
o8dMgzvbS7.evidence: Evaluation of 13 baselines, controlled experiments on source presence, and a human study (described in reviews as covering three models).
o8dMgzvbS7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that source-level evaluation addresses a practical gap that scene-level scores miss, with broad coverage of video types and audio formats.
o8dMgzvbS7.main_concern: Novelty and reliability are limited: the metrics integrate existing tools whose errors propagate (ground-truth audio scores only 77.7 on multi-source semantics), and the human study is small.

FRVIY6igvD.one_liner: Dataset of about 16,000 multi-table instances with injected integrity violations measuring LLMs' silent failure rate.
FRVIY6igvD.problem: Evaluations on corrupted multi-table inputs score only the final output, so they cannot distinguish a model that misses a violation from one that detects it but answers without disclosing it.
FRVIY6igvD.method: RELIC injects six violation types at controlled severities into integrity-verified synthetic table pairs, defines the silent failure rate (SFR), and decomposes silent failures by whether the reasoning trace detects the violation.
FRVIY6igvD.key_idea: Splits silent failures into missed versus undisclosed violations by checking whether the reasoning trace mentions the violation even when the final answer does not.
FRVIY6igvD.evidence: Evaluation of 20 models, analysis of detection versus reasoning budget, and prompt-level interventions across violation types.
FRVIY6igvD.claimed_gains: SFR exceeds 84% for all 20 models and 97% for all three frontier models despite clean accuracy of up to 98.3%.
FRVIY6igvD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating detection from disclosure is a useful, new framing and that the six-violation, 20-model evaluation is extensive.
FRVIY6igvD.main_concern: SFR measurement validity is doubtful: in the base setup models have no field to report a violation, so SFR mostly counts non-abstention, and detection is inferred from reasoning traces.

g1kI00OQSV.one_liner: Attack in which an ordinary user induces a reflective agent to write overbroad tool-use rules into shared reflection memory.
g1kI00OQSV.problem: Reflective agents turn successful trajectories into reusable lessons without checking which actions were necessary, leaving the reflection step open to exploitation.
g1kI00OQSV.method: Reflection-Coupled Credit Assignment Poisoning (R-CAP): an authorized user elicits a plausible tool-use behavior during a successful task, and the agent's reflection writer promotes it into standing guidance that widens tool scope in later sessions. The attacker does not modify memory, tools, system prompts, or the victim query.
g1kI00OQSV.key_idea: Exploits the reflection writer's unchecked credit assignment: a behavior that coincides with task success is stored as a general rule, without touching memory or prompts.
g1kI00OQSV.evidence: AgentDojo cases across three backbones on a 53-task cohort, with comparisons to direct memory injection and several defenses (per reviews).
g1kI00OQSV.claimed_gains: Conditional on successful induction, 98-99% keyword-based reflection implantation rate and 88-92% Conditional TOSR with 97-99% utility; end-to-end TOSR is 68-76% on the same 53-task cohort.
g1kI00OQSV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a meaningful security risk in which successful task completion hides overbroad learned guidance, shown across multiple models and domains.
g1kI00OQSV.main_concern: The role of incorrect credit assignment is not isolated (keyword-based RIR, necessity test on a separate cohort), and the separation from prior work on overbroad rules (OEP) is unclear.

opIfMHUbJP.one_liner: Trains visual autoregressive models on imagined next tokens beyond ground truth, bounded by a criterion tied to the data distribution.
opIfMHUbJP.problem: Visual autoregressive models predict each token from ground-truth prefixes and are supervised only on the ground-truth next token, which limits how much of the visual distribution they capture.
opIfMHUbJP.method: Next Token Imagination (NTI) lets the model explore beyond the ground-truth next token under a criterion that keeps the exploration bounded by the visual distribution. It changes only training targets and inputs and leaves inference unchanged.
opIfMHUbJP.key_idea: Replaces the single ground-truth target and prefix with model-explored plausible alternatives, filtered by a criterion that keeps them within the underlying visual distribution.
opIfMHUbJP.evidence: ImageNet experiments (class-conditional 256x256 per the reviews) with several tokenizers and ablations on context and target choices.
opIfMHUbJP.claimed_gains: The abstract gives no numbers (fidelity improves substantially with a smaller model and lower training cost); reviewers cite FID dropping from 3.02 to 1.67 on the AR-L backbone.
opIfMHUbJP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, changes only training targets and inputs, adds roughly 10% training cost, and the gains carry over to other tokenizers.
opIfMHUbJP.main_concern: It is unclear how much of the FID gain comes from NTI (and its CRI component) rather than guidance schedules, since the baseline guidance settings are unreported and the CRI ablation gain is small.

vOieetdCT2.one_liner: One-step trajectory decoder for driving trained with a drift field toward feasible trajectories and a critic-based reward field.
vOieetdCT2.problem: Generative trajectory decoders need multiple denoising or flow steps, and existing reinforcement learning methods assume multi-step generation chains that mismatch one-step generators.
vOieetdCT2.method: FieldDrive clusters a trajectory vocabulary and selects high-scoring trajectories as a feasible distribution that guides the output through a Drift Field Vector. A trained critic supplies a Reward Field Vector toward high-reward regions, in a two-stage training scheme.
vOieetdCT2.key_idea: Treats the drift field and the reward field as optimization directions of one distributional energy function, so a one-step generator can be reward-optimized without a multi-step chain.
vOieetdCT2.evidence: A theoretical shared-origin argument for the two fields, plus planning benchmark results scored by PDMS/EPDMS with ablations and a MeanFuser comparison (per reviews).
vOieetdCT2.claimed_gains: Not stated in the visible abstract; reviewers cite 92.14 PDMS for the full method versus 85.58 for Drift-only, and a reported 1.26x speedup over MeanFuser.
vOieetdCT2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that one-step decoding with reward optimization is a worthwhile goal and that the ablations and planning results show the approach is effective.
vOieetdCT2.main_concern: The contribution is seen as incremental, applying existing Drifting and metric-critic ideas to driving, with training heavily tailored to the PDMS metric.

hMhoJMXnrl.one_liner: RL reward for software-engineering agents that reweights tests by how few patch groups pass them and scores repository snapshots.
hMhoJMXnrl.problem: Binary pass-all-test rewards are sparse, and raw pass-rate is unreliable because one challenging test and a hundred trivial or already-passing tests can cover the same functionality.
hMhoJMXnrl.method: At each iteration CodeLift groups tests that kill the same patches and patches that pass the same tests, and weights test groups more when fewer patch groups pass them. The same scoring rule is applied to repository snapshots inside a rollout to credit useful actions.
hMhoJMXnrl.key_idea: Calibrates pass-rate rewards with test-group difficulty estimated from behavioral grouping of tests and patches, and applies the score to intermediate repository snapshots.
hMhoJMXnrl.evidence: Experiments on SWE benchmarks against binary and pass-rate baselines; reviews mention two benchmarks, an additional model and training setting, paired confidence intervals, and ablations.
hMhoJMXnrl.claimed_gains: Consistently improves pass@1/2/4/8 over binary and pass-rate baselines; no further numbers stated.
hMhoJMXnrl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that test imbalance in pass-rate rewards is a real problem and that the scoring rule provides denser execution-based signal, with gains and analyses that support it.
hMhoJMXnrl.main_concern: Overlap with and missing comparison against VeRPO (online test difficulty and density correction), and the individual contribution of test grouping, patch grouping and adaptive weighting is not isolated.

CespIWOBYY.one_liner: Fairness-regularized random shock pricing: queue-weighted penalty on past group-price gaps applied before the exploration shock.
CespIWOBYY.problem: Prices used in pricing experiments to learn demand are also the offers customer groups receive, so exploration creates price disparities between groups.
CespIWOBYY.method: Extends Random Shock Design (RSD) with a fairness penalty scaled by virtual queues: past disparities correct the next price, then an independent shock is added for demand estimation. The paper proves bounded terminal disparity, vanishing disparity with diminishing shocks, and consistent demand estimation.
CespIWOBYY.key_idea: Corrects each price using virtual-queue-weighted past group-price disparities before adding the exploratory shock, keeping the shock independent so demand stays identifiable.
CespIWOBYY.evidence: Theory (terminal disparity bound, consistency, revenue analysis with a fair benchmark and lower bounds) plus synthetic experiments and an Online Retail-calibrated simulation against RSD, fixed penalties and current-gap penalties.
CespIWOBYY.claimed_gains: Synthetic results show a 92% reduction in mean disparity with a 2.4% increase in mean revenue relative to RSD; the Online Retail-calibrated simulation shows a 19% disparity reduction with small revenue and estimation costs.
CespIWOBYY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that applying the fairness correction before the shock is well motivated and that the terminal-disparity guarantee with consistent demand estimation is the main strength.
CespIWOBYY.main_concern: The revenue cost of fairness is not bounded against the best fair policy (price-adjustment cost left uncontrolled), and experiments show mixed benefit over simpler penalties.

CYZbnNobTC.one_liner: Builds a fixed flow-matching training-time distribution from measured speed of path marginals, before velocity training.
CYZbnNobTC.problem: Uniform training-time sampling in flow matching may recover a target distribution's modes, connected components and loops more slowly than necessary.
CYZbnNobTC.method: PathSpeed estimates squared path speed from adjacent marginal samples, smooths and standardizes it, and uses it as a fixed training-time sampling distribution. The speed splits into changes in projected means and scales and changes in standardized shape, and integrated speed bounds persistence-diagram changes.
CYZbnNobTC.key_idea: Allocates timestep sampling probability by the measured motion (squared speed) of the prescribed path marginals, computed offline from data before the velocity network is trained.
CYZbnNobTC.evidence: Controlled distributions, CIFAR-10, and class-conditional latent ImageNet-256, with ablations on shape information and placement of sampling probability along time.
CYZbnNobTC.claimed_gains: On controlled distributions it reaches Uniform's final structural error with 33-49% fewer updates; on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-256 it has the lowest mean FID among compared schedules and reaches Uniform's final FID with 42% and 52% fewer updates.
CYZbnNobTC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the signal is principled and interpretable because it comes from the data and prescribed path rather than the model's training state, with extensive experiments and ablations.
CYZbnNobTC.main_concern: The acceleration claims lack seed-level uncertainty and offline-cost accounting, and recent adaptive time-allocation baselines such as cDOL are not compared.

9zSL8VXyFk.one_liner: Benchmark porting the incomplete-drawing divergent-thinking task to tool-using multimodal LLM agents, with human-rated drawings and an automated scorer.
9zSL8VXyFk.problem: Creativity evaluation of language models rarely covers figural divergent thinking in multi-turn tool use.
9zSL8VXyFk.method: The agent draws on a canvas through tool calls, sees the result each turn, and must work an un-erasable starting shape into the most original drawing it can, deciding itself when to stop. Drawings are rated by crowd workers for creativity and recognizability, and an automated scorer (ViDrA-adapted) predicts creativity ratings.
9zSL8VXyFk.key_idea: Adapts the human incomplete-drawing test to an agent loop in which the model incrementally draws with tool calls, scored on creativity and recognizability.
9zSL8VXyFk.evidence: 14 multimodal models, 2,700 drawings across a primary study and six sensitivity analyses, ratings for the drawings and for 300 human reference drawings.
9zSL8VXyFk.claimed_gains: The ViDrA-adapted scorer predicts human creativity ratings at r = 0.85 on a random held-out split; agent drawings score higher in creativity but lower in recognizability than human drawings.
9zSL8VXyFk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a useful, carefully measured benchmark that extends creativity evaluation beyond text, with substantial human ratings and validated scoring.
9zSL8VXyFk.main_concern: The claim that agents are more creative than humans is weakly controlled, since human and agent drawings come from different stimuli and production interfaces.

I44VHWrckF.one_liner: Feed-forward dynamic Gaussian Splatting with a history-aware depth head, compact Gaussian adapter and motion-aware frame sampling for streams.
I44VHWrckF.problem: Existing feed-forward dynamic view synthesis methods process short clips or only adjacent frames, which limits context and causes flicker in long monocular streams.
I44VHWrckF.method: A History-aware Depth Prediction Head uses past information for temporally consistent Gaussians, a Compact Gaussian Adapter gives high-resolution rendering with fewer holes, and training-free Motion-aware Farthest View Sampling selects informative frames to reduce spatial and temporal redundancy.
I44VHWrckF.key_idea: Feeds historical depth states into depth prediction and chooses context frames with motion-aware farthest view sampling, keeping resource use bounded on long streams.
I44VHWrckF.evidence: Benchmark datasets (three benchmark groups plus 290 additional videos per reviews) and in-the-wild videos, with temporal consistency metrics and component ablations.
I44VHWrckF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that summarizing context from earlier frames is a reasonable approach, supported by broad experiments and ablations that show better rendering quality and temporal consistency.
I44VHWrckF.main_concern: The streaming claim is weakly supported: cache growth, historical search cost and quality over longer histories are not quantified, and baselines could also be made constant-memory by adding a sampling module.

1E1Id8744W.one_liner: Locate-Corroborate-Isolate search paradigm and Savanna benchmark for generating images of entities newer than the generator's training data.
1E1Id8744W.problem: Search-augmented image generation struggles with entities that appeared only days ago, where web visual evidence is limited, confusable, and rarely shows the target alone.
1E1Id8744W.method: An automated pipeline turns recent headlines into hard prompts (Savanna, 500 prompts across 16 subcategories). The Locate-Corroborate-Isolate paradigm pins down the target's identity by text search, verifies candidate images against multiple sources, then crops a clean reference for the generator; Ranger-8B is trained on 15K such trajectories.
1E1Id8744W.key_idea: The agent first fixes the target's identity through text search, then cross-verifies candidate images across sources, then crops an isolated reference image for the generator.
1E1Id8744W.evidence: The Savanna benchmark with frontier-model harnesses as comparison, tests with several generators, and results on Mind-Bench and KnowGen (per reviews).
1E1Id8744W.claimed_gains: Ranger-8B reaches a search score of 67.2, outperforming harnesses equipped with frontier models, which retrieve a correct reference for only about half of the prompts; it also gives the best generation quality with every generator tested.
1E1Id8744W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical and challenging, the benchmark is solid because frontier models struggle on it, and separate search and generation scores help explain failures.
1E1Id8744W.main_concern: Entity and event leakage between training and test data is not controlled beyond timestamps, and the Locate and Corroborate stages are not ablated separately.

lwpVFdq21K.one_liner: Derives scaling laws for mixture-of-experts diffusion LLMs and uses them to train a 30B-A3B model from scratch.
lwpVFdq21K.problem: Sparse MoE diffusion LLMs largely inherit autoregressive training recipes, although the masked denoising objective calls for diffusion-specific scaling laws.
lwpVFdq21K.method: A systematic scaling study over optimization hyperparameters, compute allocation and MoE architecture across compute budgets guides the training of LLaDA MoE v2, a 30B-A3B diffusion LLM trained from scratch on 23.5T tokens, followed by supervised fine-tuning.
lwpVFdq21K.key_idea: Fits diffusion-LLM-specific scaling laws for hyperparameters, compute allocation and MoE architecture on small runs, then applies the resulting settings to a 30B-A3B pretraining run.
lwpVFdq21K.evidence: Scaling-law experiments across compute budgets, then benchmark comparisons on knowledge, reasoning and coding against LLaDA MoE, Qwen3 30B-A3B and SDAR Chat.
