lwpVFdq21K.claimed_gains: Surpasses LLaDA MoE at half of its training FLOPs; the base model approaches Qwen3 30B-A3B using 65% as many pretraining tokens; after SFT it outperforms SDAR Chat on seven of eight reasoning and coding benchmarks.
lwpVFdq21K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the systematic small-scale study gives practical guidance for pretraining diffusion LLMs and that the resulting model scores well and is a valuable released resource.
lwpVFdq21K.main_concern: Large-scale comparisons do not isolate the scaling laws' contribution from differences in architecture, data, optimization and size, and the fitted laws lack uncertainty analysis.

0bsGLcFOQt.one_liner: Song generation that trains an autoregressive token planner jointly with a continuous semantic flow model through differentiable readouts.
0bsGLcFOQt.problem: Low-rate discrete semantic tokens make long song planning tractable but quantization limits information for acoustic rendering, and separately optimized stages stop downstream objectives from shaping the planner.
0bsGLcFOQt.method: A VQ tokenizer supplies tokens for autoregressive planning and an SSL-derived variational encoder supplies continuous semantic targets. A full-sequence flow model, conditioned on the completed token plan and differentiable readouts of the planner's predictive states, generates semantic features for acoustic rendering.
0bsGLcFOQt.key_idea: Flow-matching gradients reach the language model through differentiable readouts of its predictive states, without differentiating through token sampling, while autoregressive feedback stays discrete.
0bsGLcFOQt.evidence: 192 shared prompts compared with a discrete baseline using SongEval, micro-PER and expert listening scores, plus downstream semantic probes and conditioned reconstruction.
0bsGLcFOQt.claimed_gains: The 48D configuration improves SongEval from 4.152 to 4.269 and reduces micro-PER from 20.26% to 14.47% relative to a discrete baseline, with substantially higher expert listening scores.
0bsGLcFOQt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the architecture is clear and that the evaluation, combining automatic metrics and expert ratings, shows better lyric fidelity and perceived sound quality than the discrete baseline.
0bsGLcFOQt.main_concern: There are no controlled ablations isolating joint training from changes in representation and renderer, and comparisons rely on an in-house baseline.

kmuerJsq5S.one_liner: Trains a trajectory predictor for robot-assisted dressing with differentiable-physics gradients and parallel body-relative auxiliary prediction.
kmuerJsq5S.problem: Dressing needs trajectories that depend on arm pose under complex cloth dynamics, and differentiable-physics gradients require full garment states that the solver does not have at inference.
kmuerJsq5S.method: GwoP separates observation-conditioned trajectory prediction from full-state physical evaluation within a differentiable computation graph, so physical gradients train the solver without full garment states at inference. It also predicts trajectories and auxiliary body-surface relations in parallel as structural guidance.
kmuerJsq5S.key_idea: Back-propagates differentiable-simulator gradients into a policy that sees only observations, while an auxiliary body-surface relation head shapes the shared representation without prescribing trajectory geometry.
kmuerJsq5S.evidence: Unseen arm configurations in simulation, cross-simulator transfer, and real-robot execution across arm poses, with baselines such as OnePolicy, TD-MPC2 and Query-to-Trajectory (per reviews).
kmuerJsq5S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the task is challenging and that the method gives substantial dressing-progress gains on many unseen arm poses in simulation, with real-robot experiments added.
kmuerJsq5S.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited: training through differentiable simulators is established, and the new body-relative auxiliary supervision is hand-designed and task-specific.

r79qi64N5t.one_liner: Flow-matching map from normal data to a Gaussian; chi-squared test on the transported norm gives an explicit type I error.
r79qi64N5t.problem: Learned anomaly detectors usually lack an explicit, controllable type I error (false alarm rate).
r79qi64N5t.method: Learns a flow-matching transport from the reference distribution to a standard Gaussian. A new sample's squared transported norm follows a chi-squared law under the reference, giving a threshold with explicit type I error, and bounds link the training loss to the resulting error for Gaussian and spherically symmetric references.
r79qi64N5t.key_idea: Transport the reference distribution to a standard Gaussian so the squared norm of a transported sample is chi-squared distributed, turning the anomaly threshold into a test with known level.
r79qi64N5t.evidence: Numerical validation of the bounds, image out-of-distribution detection, radar target detection, imbalanced biological data classification, and tabular anomaly detection benchmarks.
r79qi64N5t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical chain from flow-matching loss to type I error is clear and valuable, with the radar detection case the strongest application.
r79qi64N5t.main_concern: The empirical results do not show a consistent advantage over baselines (image out-of-distribution pairs are weak), and the Lipschitz-dependent bounds are loose and not studied in experiments.

ve6kfpCq6U.one_liner: Benchmark of 49 real customer-project cases requiring interactive requirement clarification and iterative optimization by agents.
ve6kfpCq6U.problem: Existing optimization benchmarks start from explicit objectives and clarification benchmarks add synthetic gaps, so end-to-end delivery from underspecified real business requests is untested.
ve6kfpCq6U.method: 49 cases spanning combinatorial optimization and machine learning are built from real customer projects. Agents elicit missing requirements from a simulated customer, and case-specific evaluators score final artifacts against acceptance criteria using customer-accepted forward-deployed-engineer solutions as references.
ve6kfpCq6U.key_idea: Hides requirements distilled from practitioner-engineer discussions behind a simulated customer and scores delivered artifacts against customer-accepted reference solutions.
ve6kfpCq6U.evidence: 18 agent configurations with three repeats per task, paired information ablations, and human audits of customer answers and clarification judgments (per reviews).
ve6kfpCq6U.claimed_gains: The highest mean delivery score is 0.5510 versus an FDE reference of 1.0, and the highest delivery success rate is 6.12%.
ve6kfpCq6U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding in real projects, with customer-accepted solutions as the quality reference, makes a meaningful and extensive evaluation setting.
ve6kfpCq6U.main_concern: All systems interact with one fixed LLM customer simulator that acts as an oracle (annotators found cross-turn inconsistencies in 9-10 of 105 audited dialogues), and its effect on rankings is untested.

UZb9XokfvD.one_liner: Bimanual robot-hand policy using 3D keypoints plus per-keypoint contact intensity auto-labeled from human egocentric videos.
UZb9XokfvD.problem: Human videos show where hands move but not how firmly they press, so policies pretrained on them still need many teleoperated demonstrations.
UZb9XokfvD.method: ConAct extends the shared human-robot point-based action representation with a contact intensity at each 3D keypoint, labeled automatically on about 1M egocentric video episodes without tactile sensors. At deployment the predicted contact displaces the robot hand's keypoint targets, without force sensing.
UZb9XokfvD.key_idea: Adds a contact-intensity channel to each keypoint action so the policy learns pressing strength from human video, and uses it to offset keypoint targets at deployment.
UZb9XokfvD.evidence: A real bimanual robot with two 20-DoF hands on three tasks at several amounts of teleoperated demonstrations, compared with three vision-language-action models pretrained on human videos, plus ablations.
UZb9XokfvD.claimed_gains: Outperforms three VLA models pretrained on human videos on all three tasks at every amount of teleoperated data; with only 20 teleoperated demonstrations in total it more than doubles the average success rate of the comparison (abstract truncated).
UZb9XokfvD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that adding contact to a keypoint-based action interface is an interesting, practical idea, with real-robot gains especially in the low-data regime.
UZb9XokfvD.main_concern: Contact intensity (pooled contact probabilities from an existing hand tracker) is not validated as a proxy for pressing force, and the contact estimation procedure is thinly documented.

pAfkkwR3JL.one_liner: Framework and simulation gym for proactive LLM agents organized around Task Capability, Temporal Allocation and Trust.
pAfkkwR3JL.problem: Proactive agents can misread user context, impose review costs or undermine trust even when their work is correct, and there are no shared principles or testbeds for designing and evaluating them.
pAfkkwR3JL.method: Three principles (3T), a five-dimension design space (task scope, anticipation horizon, activation trigger, processing timing, intervention depth), and a specification of user and environment modeling. PROACTIVITY-GYM adds multi-day scenarios, stateful environments and persona-conditioned simulated users.
pAfkkwR3JL.key_idea: Evaluates proactive assistance jointly on task capability, compute timing and trust across multi-day stateful simulations with simulated users, rather than single-turn task success.
pAfkkwR3JL.evidence: Evaluations across 23 model-harness configurations in the gym, and a human-subject study of 30 participants (per reviews).
pAfkkwR3JL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the 3T framework and design dimensions are clear and useful, and that the testbed evaluates behavior across interactions rather than only task completion.
pAfkkwR3JL.main_concern: Trust is measured by LLM judges and by intervention-depth agreement (TR-D), which are not validated against human judgments on real agent trajectories.

ExbaotJPaB.one_liner: Frozen forecast-conditioned neural transform gives correction patterns; observations set their coefficients through a linear-Gaussian Bayesian update.
ExbaotJPaB.problem: Data assimilation must spread sparse observation information to unobserved variables, but climatological covariances are static, small ensembles are rank-limited, and neural methods keep nonlinear decoders in the online optimization.
ExbaotJPaB.method: A forecast-conditioned neural transform builds multivariate physical-space correction patterns, trained with held-out-variable and sparse-observation objectives to recover errors from partial information. During assimilation the transform is frozen and observations determine the coefficients by a linear-Gaussian Bayesian update.
ExbaotJPaB.key_idea: Separates learned error representation from online inference: a frozen network supplies state-dependent correction patterns and a closed-form linear-Gaussian update solves for their coefficients.
ExbaotJPaB.evidence: Global cycling data-assimilation experiments against baselines such as VAE-Var and LoRA-EnVar, with retraining ablations of the training objectives (per reviews); all experiments use noise-free observations.
ExbaotJPaB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learned correction patterns inside a directly solvable Bayesian update is a meaningful design, with objectives matched to partial-observation recovery and improvements over baselines.
ExbaotJPaB.main_concern: The experiments are idealized (noise-free observations of all channels) and compare methods with different observation-error weights and unstandardized tuning, so gains are not cleanly attributed.

6Bs99JWmh6.one_liner: Sample-based algorithm learning second-best gains from trade in matching markets, with matching upper and lower sample bounds.
6Bs99JWmh6.problem: The sample complexity of learning Bayesian second-best gains from trade in matching markets with unknown value and cost distributions is not known.
6Bs99JWmh6.method: For independent distributions, an algorithm always outputs a dominant-strategy incentive-compatible, ex-post individually rational mechanism and, with high probability, an ex-ante weakly budget-balanced one within epsilon of the second-best benchmark. The upper bound uses a critical-contact decomposition; the lower bound uses hard instances on star forests.
6Bs99JWmh6.key_idea: A critical-contact decomposition localizes the effect of marginal-distribution perturbations, with aggregate exposure controlled by the maximum feasible matching size r.
6Bs99JWmh6.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bounds only; no experiments are described.
6Bs99JWmh6.claimed_gains: Per-marginal sample complexity of Theta-tilde(d r h^2 / epsilon^2) for d marginals on [0,h] and maximum matching size r, tight up to logarithmic factors.
6Bs99JWmh6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a solid, nontrivial extension of bilateral-trade results to matching markets, with nearly matching upper and lower bounds.
6Bs99JWmh6.main_concern: The technical novelty is unclear, since the Lagrangian characterization, matching-mechanism structure and critical-contact property come from earlier work.

dT8MlS2ZkQ.one_liner: A graph neural network selects which search-tree node to expand next with bounded local MCTS, trained from action-level supervision.
dT8MlS2ZkQ.problem: Standard MCTS allocates search budget implicitly through repeated local traversal decisions that do not globally prioritize the most informative region of the tree.
dT8MlS2ZkQ.method: LASER separates where to search from how to search: a graph neural network selects a node in the current tree, and a bounded local MCTS explores from it. This is posed as a metalevel decision problem, trained without annotations of where search should occur, and integrated into EfficientZero.
dT8MlS2ZkQ.key_idea: Makes node selection a separate learned metalevel step: a GNN picks the subtree root, ordinary MCTS runs locally, and training uses action-level outcomes rather than search-location labels.
dT8MlS2ZkQ.evidence: Sokoban and sliding puzzles under matched search budgets against standard MCTS and alternative subtree-selection strategies, and Atari 100k with EfficientZero.
dT8MlS2ZkQ.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms standard MCTS and alternative subtree-selection strategies on Sokoban and sliding puzzles under matched budgets, and improves aggregate Atari 100k performance; no numbers stated.
dT8MlS2ZkQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating where-to-search as a trainable step is a clean and useful idea, with ablations showing consistent gains.
dT8MlS2ZkQ.main_concern: The advantage largely disappears once MCTS uses a policy prior (PUCT), and the stronger Gumbel MuZero-style baseline is missing.

CKUYgOyb5Z.one_liner: Distills flow-based VLA models by weighting candidate teacher layers per task instruction and flow stage.
CKUYgOyb5Z.problem: Fixed-layer attention distillation may give suboptimal supervision because the teacher layers that suit a compressed student vary across task instructions and flow stages.
CKUYgOyb5Z.method: For each retained student layer, TFC-KD picks candidate teacher layers around its aligned counterpart and weights them using the task instruction and one of three flow stages. The weighted attention maps over vision-language tokens become distillation targets, with an ordering constraint keeping selections roughly aligned with student depth.
CKUYgOyb5Z.key_idea: A router combining instruction and flow-stage signals weights nearby teacher layers, and their weighted attention maps serve as distillation targets under a depth-ordering regularizer.
CKUYgOyb5Z.evidence: LIBERO experiments with an 8-layer student (abstract truncated), across different backbones, compression levels and perturbation scenarios per reviews, with ablations.
CKUYgOyb5Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is new for VLA distillation, adds no inference overhead, and improves over the reference model across backbones and compression levels, with good ablations.
CKUYgOyb5Z.main_concern: Baselines are missing (other layer-wise distillation methods such as TED, SemCKD, C2KD, and fixed depth-aligned targets on all layers), so the benefit of adaptive selection is not isolated.

reQVgFF5Vh.one_liner: Spectral analysis in probability space shows LLM next-token variation concentrates in few canonical token modes, stable under fine-tuning.
reQVgFF5Vh.problem: It is unclear whether LLM predictive distributions use the full vocabulary dimensionality (over 10^5 tokens) or vary within a much smaller structure as context varies.
reQVgFF5Vh.method: A spectral framework separates the predictive marginal from context-dependent probability variation and decomposes next-token prediction into orthogonal token-side canonical modes, from which dimensionality and orientation are read. It proposes the Canonical Subspace Hypothesis.
reQVgFF5Vh.key_idea: Eigendecomposes the covariance of marginal-normalized next-token probability deviations across contexts to get canonical token modes, then compares spectra and subspaces across models and after fine-tuning.
reQVgFF5Vh.evidence: Analyses across model families and context distributions with random-initialization controls and several energy thresholds, plus a LoRA fine-tuning check on Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct (per reviews).
reQVgFF5Vh.claimed_gains: Only 9.7%-24.0% of token-space dimensions account for 99.9% of context-dependent predictive variation.
reQVgFF5Vh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the probability-space formulation is well defined, clearly distinct from logit-rank arguments, and backed by clean theory and controls.
reQVgFF5Vh.main_concern: The fine-tuning preservation evidence is thin (one model, 100 LoRA steps, performance change unreported), so high subspace overlap may reflect little adaptation.

aKJCIuxEUr.one_liner: Paper-to-slides generation via executable transduction graphs binding audience-driven adaptations to source evidence, with prefix-sensitive selection.
aKJCIuxEUr.problem: One shared deck must serve audiences with different knowledge and goals while preserving evidence, required conditions and claim scope, but prior systems leave the link between source meaning, audience purpose and order implicit.
aKJCIuxEUr.method: AudienceDeck aligns source-anchored semantic units and audience specifications into a frozen contract. Each adaptation becomes an executable transduction graph recording source meaning, operation, story role and required conditions; candidates are filtered by fidelity, coverage, structure, slide and time budgets, and a prefix-sensitive selector picks among feasible graphs.
aKJCIuxEUr.key_idea: Represents each candidate talk as an executable graph tying every transformation to source evidence and audience goal, rejects claims exposed before their conditions, then selects by prefix-sensitive risk.
aKJCIuxEUr.evidence: Two benchmarks with a wide range of baseline systems and evaluation metrics (per reviews), using Expert, Novice and Adopter audiences.
aKJCIuxEUr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the executable graph linking source semantics, audience goals and slide decisions is a meaningful design, with experiments covering many baselines and metrics.
aKJCIuxEUr.main_concern: Baseline settings are unmatched (audience briefs, slide counts and durations differ across systems), and the two core components lack dedicated ablations.

SdVdfPNEX9.one_liner: Training-free inversion-free flow editing using a shared-observation velocity difference and progress-adaptive step lengths.
SdVdfPNEX9.problem: Inversion-free editing differences source- and target-conditional velocities evaluated at different noisy states, mixing the condition response with a denoising response, and standard integration concentrates edits in late low-noise steps.
SdVdfPNEX9.method: GRAPE builds a gradient-aligned field that evaluates both conditions at a shared noisy observation of the current edit, proportional to the target-to-source log-density-ratio gradient under population-optimal velocities. Progress-adaptive integration then compensates for the mismatch between noise-schedule progress and clean-state progress.
SdVdfPNEX9.key_idea: Evaluates source and target velocities at the same noisy state and lengthens integration steps adaptively when editing progress lags the noise schedule.
SdVdfPNEX9.evidence: Three flow backbones, preservation-editability curves, approximately matched-CLIP operating points, and ablations, per the reviews.
SdVdfPNEX9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared-state field is simple, removes a clear confounder and has a useful density-ratio interpretation, with consistent gains across three backbones and extensive ablations.
SdVdfPNEX9.main_concern: Progress-adaptive integration is not distinguished from adaptive step-size or guidance scheduling, and tuned nonuniform-schedule baselines and direct analysis of how it works are missing.

ramfQvZtZt.one_liner: Continual-learning MoE for LLMs that expands experts into complementary feature directions and routes with a task-supervised gate.
ramfQvZtZt.problem: Replay-based continual learning depends on the quantity and quality of rehearsal data, and updating shared parameters across tasks causes interference and forgetting.
ramfQvZtZt.method: AEI encourages each new expert to capture feature directions complementary to existing experts, so expansion stays compact with less redundancy. A context-aware gating module trained with task-identity supervision identifies and combines the relevant experts for each input.
ramfQvZtZt.key_idea: Regularizes new experts toward the complement of the feature subspace already spanned by existing experts, and trains a gate with task-identity supervision to select experts per input.
ramfQvZtZt.evidence: Multiple LLM backbones (including Qwen3-4B), task sequences of up to 50 tasks on SuperNI with 1% rehearsal data, plus ablations, significance tests and parameter and runtime comparisons (per reviews).
ramfQvZtZt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the results are strong across backbones, task orders and long sequences, and that the adaptive expansion idea is clearly motivated.
ramfQvZtZt.main_concern: The evaluation is limited to SuperNI instruction tasks (no reasoning benchmarks), and the benefit of the subspace regularizer over plain group-sparsity regularization is not isolated.

kWH5SzYp6d.one_liner: Zero-feedback pretraining-data selection for time-series foundation models using GMM soft clustering and coverage-based sampling quotas.
kWH5SzYp6d.problem: Existing data selection for time-series foundation models relies on training feedback or external supervision, so the selected corpus cannot be fixed before pretraining begins.
kWH5SzYp6d.method: TRACS uses GMM-based soft clustering to organize candidate series by temporal pattern, assigns sampling quotas by the coverage each cluster needs rather than by cluster size, and repairs missing patterns. Proofs cover coverage of reachable patterns, finite-step termination of repair, and bounded representation error.
kWH5SzYp6d.key_idea: Assigns per-cluster sampling quotas by required pattern coverage instead of cluster size, then swaps in series to repair missing discrete patterns, all before pretraining.
kWH5SzYp6d.evidence: MOMENT-1 Small, PatchTST and Timer under a 10B-token pretraining budget, evaluated on 20 stable zero-shot forecasting tasks from GIFT-Eval, with five seeds per reviews.
kWH5SzYp6d.claimed_gains: Using only 25% or 50% of the candidate corpus, TRACS attains the lowest aggregate MASE and CRPS among evaluated pretraining baselines on 20 stable zero-shot GIFT-Eval tasks (abstract truncated before the full-corpus comparison).
kWH5SzYp6d.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that zero-feedback selection with explicit pattern-coverage guarantees is clearly described and well organized, and is tested on three architectures under a fixed token budget.
kWH5SzYp6d.main_concern: It mostly combines existing components (GMM clustering, Sobol sampling, replacement) and is compared against weak or modified baselines (Random, Stratified, a modified BLAST-style method).

BXZeGxuBrH.one_liner: Represents each control timestep as one continuous latent token reconstructed by a diffusion VLM's own masked-token procedure.
BXZeGxuBrH.problem: Vision-language-action policies must turn a discrete-token backbone into continuous control, and each current answer (action expert, action tokens, swapped objective) carries a cost.
BXZeGxuBrH.method: MONAD represents each control timestep as one continuous latent token and reconstructs temporally ordered action blocks with the same masked-token procedure the diffusion VLM applies to language. Two position-wise projections hold 0.45% of parameters, with no action expert, tokenizer or codec.
BXZeGxuBrH.key_idea: Treats an action vector as a masked span in the diffusion VLM's own hidden space and reconstructs it with the backbone's native masked-token objective.
BXZeGxuBrH.evidence: Standard benchmarks including LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus and CALVIN against a wide range of baselines, plus layer probes of the shared backbone (per reviews).
BXZeGxuBrH.claimed_gains: 98.15% on regular LIBERO and 85.9% on the 10,030-task benchmark (abstract truncated); action-specific parameters are 0.45% of the model versus 16.5% and 19.2% for the action experts in π₀ and π₀.₅.
BXZeGxuBrH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified design without a separate action expert is simple and gives competitive results across several simulation benchmarks, particularly LIBERO-Plus.
BXZeGxuBrH.main_concern: The benefit of the shared-backbone reconstruction formulation is not isolated: there is no same-backbone, same-data comparison with action experts, direct regression or flow matching, and latency and memory are not reported.

iPFrJBDqRA.one_liner: RL for long-horizon agents that jointly optimizes task actions and context summaries, with token-level loss normalization and cross-segment GAE.
iPFrJBDqRA.problem: Long-horizon agentic LLMs are limited by finite context windows, and context compaction is mostly used as an inference-time heuristic rather than trained in reinforcement learning.
iPFrJBDqRA.method: CompactionRL continues rollouts under summarized context and jointly optimizes task execution and summary generation using token-level loss normalization and cross-segment generalized advantage estimation, so the agent learns from compacted long trajectories.
iPFrJBDqRA.key_idea: Shares one task reward across execution and summary segments, normalizing loss per token and propagating advantages across compaction boundaries with cross-segment GAE.
iPFrJBDqRA.evidence: Training on open models GLM-4.5-Air (106B-A12B) and GLM-4.7-Flash (30B-A3B), evaluated on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0, with ablations.
iPFrJBDqRA.claimed_gains: GLM-4.5-Air reaches Pass@1 of 66.4% on SWE-bench Verified and 26.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, 6.6 and 4.9 points above the base model with inference-time compaction; GLM-4.7-Flash improves by 5.5 and 6.7 points to 56.0% and 20.2%.
iPFrJBDqRA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that compaction-aware RL is a timely, practical problem, tackled at realistic scales with comprehensive ablations of the training design.
iPFrJBDqRA.main_concern: The evidence that training the summarizer drives the gains is weak (differences within the standard deviation, a single run on a 200-task subset, few tasks trigger compaction), and novelty over SUPO is questioned.

2wR8rGf3AE.one_liner: Training-free caching for multi-view world action models: per-view cache validity and action-aware token delaying.
2wR8rGf3AE.problem: Multi-view world action models are expensive, and existing caching treats multi-view representations as one sequence, ignoring the uneven dynamics across camera views.
2wR8rGf3AE.method: View asynchronous computing checks cache validity separately for each camera view, computes only active views and predicts stable ones from cache. Within active views, world-action contribution-aware token delaying weighs token cache deviation and the change in visual-to-action contribution to prioritize urgent tokens.
2wR8rGf3AE.key_idea: Decides recompute versus reuse separately per camera view, then within active views delays tokens whose cache deviation and visual-to-action contribution change are small.
2wR8rGf3AE.evidence: Multi-view robotic action experiments; reviews describe a single backbone (Motus) in the RoboTwin simulation environment with ablations.
2wR8rGf3AE.claimed_gains: Not stated in the visible abstract; reviewers cite about a 3.45x latency speedup with a 1.55 percentage-point drop in average success rate.
2wR8rGf3AE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the per-view and action-aware allocation is reasonable and gives a strong speed-accuracy trade-off with small loss in task success.
2wR8rGf3AE.main_concern: Evaluation covers one backbone (Motus) in one simulator, and the design is seen as a combination of existing caching ideas such as SeaCache and ToCa.

8rRLc5sCxL.one_liner: One-shot full-precision weight correction using the intersection and union of quantization intervals to block quantization-activated attacks.
8rRLc5sCxL.problem: A model that behaves normally in full precision can show malicious behavior (advertisement injection, over-refusal, jailbreak) only after quantization.
8rRLc5sCxL.method: IUC models local parameter intervals under different quantization configurations: their intersection gives a shared reference region and their union bounds the correction magnitude. Parameters with a smaller intersection are corrected first, and a single correction of the full-precision model covers multiple common configurations.
8rRLc5sCxL.key_idea: Prioritizes correcting weights whose quantization-interval intersection across configurations is narrowest, and caps each correction by the union of the intervals.
8rRLc5sCxL.evidence: Multiple LLMs, attack scenarios and quantization configurations (INT8, NF4, FP4, several GGUF settings, unseen GPTQ, and a defense-aware attack per reviews).
8rRLc5sCxL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is practically valuable because one correction supports multiple quantization configurations and it generalizes to unseen settings such as GPTQ.
8rRLc5sCxL.main_concern: The theory does not show that leaving the interval intersection suppresses malicious behavior, and with GGUF in the reference set the exit cost is zero regardless of intersection width.

FJePc0DmXn.one_liner: Two-stage RL distillation: optimize aggressively on a fixed rollout batch, then restart and distill the log-probability difference with clipping.
FJePc0DmXn.problem: LLM reinforcement learning trades sample efficiency against asymptotic performance: on-policy methods need costly rollouts, off-policy reuse causes distribution mismatch, and continued fixed-data updates shift token probabilities and reduce entropy.
FJePc0DmXn.method: Stage 1 runs weakly constrained optimization on a fixed rollout batch to build a strong policy-difference signal. Stage 2 restarts from the policy that generated the batch and optimizes the fixed teacher-reference log-probability difference with a clipped update.
FJePc0DmXn.key_idea: Uses the fixed log-probability difference between an aggressively optimized teacher and the reference as the target, learned by a student restarted from the reference with a clipped update.
FJePc0DmXn.evidence: Mathematical reasoning benchmarks on Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 including HMMT, with weak-teacher settings and comparisons to on-policy SAPO (per reviews).
FJePc0DmXn.claimed_gains: Abstract truncated before the numbers; reviewers cite 73.3% on the HMMT validation set after roughly 21 hours versus 68.5% for on-policy SAPO.
FJePc0DmXn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and practical, and that the fixed versus evolving reference analysis, including the weak-teacher result, is insightful.
FJePc0DmXn.main_concern: Results rest on single runs with extensive checkpoint and hyperparameter selection on HMMT Feb 25, without seeds or uncertainty intervals, so benchmark-specific tuning cannot be ruled out.

r1H9TwpMFX.one_liner: Spectral anti-collapse regularizer on backbone representations, motivated by lambda-balance, applied to JEPA self-supervised learning.
r1H9TwpMFX.problem: Anti-collapse objectives are applied after the projection head, yet downstream tasks use backbone features, which can still show dimensional collapse with low effective rank.
r1H9TwpMFX.method: SACReg is a spectral regularizer on the backbone motivated by lambda-balance, the relative scale of weight matrices across layers. In a two-layer linear network the authors show lambda-balance prevents collapse and the regularizer induces it; applied to JEPA it gives lambda-JEPA.
r1H9TwpMFX.key_idea: Regularizes the spectrum of backbone representations so that layer weight scales stay balanced (lambda-balance), which prevents low-rank collapse before the projector.
r1H9TwpMFX.evidence: Two-layer linear theory, rank measurements on ImageNet100, ImageNet-1k classification, linear-probe transfer on eight downstream datasets, and video SSL on Something-Something-v2 and Kinetics-400.
r1H9TwpMFX.claimed_gains: Improves over LeJEPA and VISReg on ImageNet-1k classification and average linear-probe transfer across eight datasets, and over LeVJEPA and V-JEPA 2 on Something-Something-v2 and Kinetics-400; no numbers stated.
r1H9TwpMFX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the gap between projected and backbone collapse is an important, well-motivated observation, with an interesting layer-balance theory and a broad empirical evaluation.
r1H9TwpMFX.main_concern: The regularizer resembles existing LogDet and covariance-decorrelation objectives (such as CorInfoMax and LogDet from KDD 2024), and the guarantees cover idealized settings that differ from the implementation.

tYwj7wgonc.one_liner: Rotary positional encoding from graph-Laplacian diffusion features so mesh vertices attend by connectivity, not spatial proximity.
tYwj7wgonc.problem: Feed-forward video-to-4D mesh generation shows sticking artifacts, where geodesically distant vertices move together when they become spatially close (cross-part motion leakage).
tYwj7wgonc.method: TRoPE derives spectral features from the graph Laplacian, builds pairwise topological relations from distances between multi-scale diffusion features, and uses them to modulate vertex-anchor attention through rotary phases. A vertex-wise tail-risk objective targets persistently high-error vertices, and the MeshSticking-4D benchmark measures the failure.
tYwj7wgonc.key_idea: Rotary phases in vertex-anchor attention encode multi-scale diffusion distances on the mesh graph, so attention separates topological distance from spatial proximity.
tYwj7wgonc.evidence: The MeshSticking-4D benchmark (human motion) and Motion-80, with ablations against Euclidean relative RoPE, geodesic relative encoding and content-only encodings (per reviews).
tYwj7wgonc.claimed_gains: Not stated in the visible abstract; a reviewer cites a 39.4% reduction in worst-vertex error that combines several architectural and training changes.
tYwj7wgonc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sticking is a practical failure mode and that the topology-aware encoding is a reasonable, clearly motivated fix supported by ablations over encodings.
tYwj7wgonc.main_concern: The gain over a simpler geodesic relative positional encoding, and over a matched content-only model trained with the tail-risk objective, is not clearly isolated.

EP6yXB55sl.one_liner: Local preferential Bayesian optimization using trust regions and derivative-informed search on a Laplace-approximated GP preference posterior.
EP6yXB55sl.problem: Preferential Bayesian optimization methods use global search and struggle beyond low- and medium-dimensional problems.
EP6yXB55sl.method: Adapts trust-region and derivative-informed local search to pairwise preference feedback, using first- and second-order derivatives of the Laplace-approximated Gaussian process posterior, and adds global-to-local variants that start with global exploration.
EP6yXB55sl.key_idea: Runs preferential BO locally around an incumbent, choosing steps from trust regions or from gradient and Hessian information of the GP preference posterior.
EP6yXB55sl.evidence: GP sample paths, standard optimization benchmark functions and policy-search tasks, against global preference-based baselines with ten repeated runs (per reviews).
EP6yXB55sl.claimed_gains: Can substantially reduce cumulative regret versus global preference-based baselines, especially in high-dimensional landscapes with steep optima; no numbers stated.
EP6yXB55sl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the work is a well-organized, systematic extension with correct derivations of posteriors, gradients and Hessians and extensive experiments.
EP6yXB55sl.main_concern: Novelty is limited because it adapts existing local BO mechanisms to preference feedback, and gains are not cleanly attributed (PrefSQP and GIPBO differ in several design choices).

noNeL90WlU.one_liner: Coreset selection for dirty tabular data that types errors from training signals, applies light fixes, and keeps reliability-weighted coresets.
noNeL90WlU.problem: Multiple error types and high training costs make it hard to balance accuracy and runtime in large tabular data, and cleaning, coreset and hybrid methods each target one objective or error type.
noNeL90WlU.method: CleanCore iteratively uses training signals for error typing and lightweight error handling, and dynamically maintains the training coreset based on per-sample reliability. Theory covers error-typing reliability, error-handling bias and coreset representativeness.
noNeL90WlU.key_idea: Shares per-sample reliability weights between error handling and coreset selection, updated from training signals at each iteration.
noNeL90WlU.evidence: Eleven baselines on eleven public tabular datasets with MLP and tabular ResNet, a SmartFactory dataset with REIN-provided corruption, and other error-injection settings.
noNeL90WlU.claimed_gains: Best ACC and F1 in 21 and 20 of the 22 model-dataset settings, with about 2-24x runtime speedups over three data cleaning methods.
noNeL90WlU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining data cleaning with coreset selection is interesting and sensible, with broad benchmark coverage and good end-to-end accuracy and runtime.
noNeL90WlU.main_concern: All experiments use one fixed seed with no standard deviations while margins are small, and the error-typing assumptions are not verified.

LwOs9PyFgD.one_liner: Learned score of whether a world model's predicted video follows its action, trained contrastively on same-state alternative-action futures.
LwOs9PyFgD.problem: Existing evaluations measure visual quality, VLM-judged plausibility or downstream performance and none isolates action fidelity, while reference-based metrics such as PSNR can rank models the wrong way.
LwOs9PyFgD.method: LAFS rates a prediction from its history and action without a reference rollout, trained by contrasting each future with futures of alternative actions executed from the same state. BranchPairs pairs an executed future that follows the queried action with one that deviates, on LIBERO, RoboTwin and Action-MNIST.
LwOs9PyFgD.key_idea: Uses negatives that are futures of other actions from the same state, which removes the history-matching shortcut so the contrastive score measures action consistency.
LwOs9PyFgD.evidence: BranchPairs on LIBERO, RoboTwin and Action-MNIST, plus a test on checkpoints of a Cosmos world model (per reviews).
LwOs9PyFgD.claimed_gains: Trained only on clean executions, LAFS prefers the action-following future in 89% of LIBERO pairs (abstract truncated); a history-matching contrastive scorer reaches 99% on its training task but exactly chance (12.5%) at choosing among eight same-state futures.
LwOs9PyFgD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the key insight that the negative distribution determines what a contrastive metric learns is clear and well supported, with controlled BranchPairs comparisons.
LwOs9PyFgD.main_concern: LAFS needs domain-specific same-state branch data (a simulator or resettable environment), and evidence is mostly from simulation with one main Cosmos world-model setup.

lSDAFaxeOZ.one_liner: Benchmark of 65 microservice performance-optimization instances created by injecting performance anti-patterns into open-source systems.
lSDAFaxeOZ.problem: Coding benchmarks test function or repository level, leaving end-to-end performance optimization in distributed microservice systems largely unexplored.
lSDAFaxeOZ.method: Because reproducible system-level performance fixes are sparse, MicroPerf-Bench injects empirically grounded anti-patterns into real open-source systems while preserving functionality and ensuring measurable degradation. It has 65 instances across seven systems and nine anti-patterns, each with an executable environment, functional tests and a mixed-workload evaluation.
lSDAFaxeOZ.key_idea: Creates ground truth by injecting known performance anti-patterns into working systems, then scores agents by how much of the injected degradation they recover under load.
lSDAFaxeOZ.evidence: 1,755 runs across nine agent-model configurations, with repeated trials, failure labels and a profiling-augmentation intervention (per reviews).
lSDAFaxeOZ.claimed_gains: The best configuration recovers only 42.0% of the injected performance degradation.
lSDAFaxeOZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a real gap by evaluating end-to-end performance optimization in redeployed multi-service systems, with a clear construction process and transparent reporting.
lSDAFaxeOZ.main_concern: Agents were not instructed to deploy, measure and iterate (they stopped after 7.7 to 18.0 minutes on average), which undermines the conclusion that they fail to localize bottlenecks.

WQ2RA2sLpb.one_liner: Mixture-of-experts domain generalization where routing decides which source domains' representations are aligned per expert and class.
WQ2RA2sLpb.problem: Enforcing exact invariance across all source domains can exclude predictive factors that are shared only within subsets of the source domains.
WQ2RA2sLpb.method: Subset-shared invariance is implemented with a mixture-of-experts: routing induces expert- and class-specific alignment strengths across source-domain pairs and softly composes expert representations for prediction. Training objectives encourage selective alignment, confident and balanced routing, and diverse expert specialization.
WQ2RA2sLpb.key_idea: Weights the pairwise cross-domain alignment loss by router responsibilities per expert and class, so each expert aligns only the domain subsets it handles.
WQ2RA2sLpb.evidence: DomainBed benchmarks and a controlled synthetic domain-growth analysis, with comparisons to GMoE and same-architecture baselines (per reviews).
WQ2RA2sLpb.claimed_gains: Improved out-of-domain generalization and greater robustness under increasing domain heterogeneity on DomainBed; no numbers stated.
WQ2RA2sLpb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that relaxing global invariance to subset-shared structure is well motivated and that routing-conditioned alignment is a reasonable design.
WQ2RA2sLpb.main_concern: The gain over GMoE is marginal (64.3 versus 64.2 with MMD), and the learned subset structure is not shown to correspond to meaningful shared predictive factors.

Slvs7Ada25.one_liner: Compiles skill libraries into Datalog-derived relation graphs evaluated under partial observation, with offline ontology evolution and Lean-proved invariants.
Slvs7Ada25.problem: Static skill graphs treat links as always active regardless of runtime state, and independently authored skill documents lack shared domain types to connect compatible skills.
Slvs7Ada25.method: Each skill document is extracted once per release into a typed manifest, from which Soufflé Datalog rules derive five relation families. At runtime a Strong-Kleene projection labels edges confirmed, unknown or rejected under partial observations, and offline evolution stages new ontology terms with verbatim source support and recompiles the graph.
Slvs7Ada25.key_idea: Separates a release-level potential relation graph from its runtime applicability using three-valued evaluation, and grows the ontology offline to connect skills that have coarse types.
Slvs7Ada25.evidence: SkillsBench with Qwen3.8-Max and Claude Opus 4.8, ALFWorld runtime ablations, and Lean 4 proofs of core projection and publication invariants.
Slvs7Ada25.claimed_gains: On SkillsBench, offline evolution improves SkillWorld by 12.5-18.5 percentage points and surpasses the strongest retrieval and graph baselines by 11.1-15.3 points across Qwen3.8-Max and Claude Opus 4.8.
Slvs7Ada25.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating a potential relation graph from state-conditioned applicability, with explicit unknowns, is a clean idea supported by ablations that reduce invalid actions.
Slvs7Ada25.main_concern: Evolution drives all of the SkillsBench gain, yet there is no equal-cost fixed-graph control, no account of which edits matter, and leakage from benchmark task cases is not ruled out.

OngxuYvpoB.one_liner: Plug-and-play test-time module clustering test images and fusing cluster-level class priors with per-image VLM predictions by confidence.
OngxuYvpoB.problem: Open-vocabulary camouflaged object segmentation methods process each test image independently and ignore the latent consensus among related samples.
OngxuYvpoB.method: Cluster-Consensus Bayes groups unlabeled test images by visual similarity, estimates cluster-level class priors from predicted categories, and fuses them with individual vision-language predictions according to confidence. It runs as iterative offline refinement across encoder views or as online inference with a confidence-weighted centroid memory, with no gradient updates.
OngxuYvpoB.key_idea: Empirical-Bayes fusion of cluster-level class priors with per-image vision-language predictions, weighted by prediction confidence, so uncertain samples borrow evidence without labeling a whole cluster.
OngxuYvpoB.evidence: Five base models and two additional single-target datasets, including OVCamo, with offline and streaming modes.
OngxuYvpoB.claimed_gains: On OVCamo, CLIP-only CCB improves OVCoser's accuracy from 68.8% to 73.2%, with a 6.2% average relative gain across six class-aware segmentation metrics.
OngxuYvpoB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cross-sample consensus idea is well motivated, lightweight and gradient-free, and gives consistent gains across base models.
OngxuYvpoB.main_concern: Novelty over test-time adaptation and transductive methods is limited, and there are no direct comparisons with T3A, TDA, LAME, TENT or TPT.

SxLSMZz5SR.one_liner: Hierarchical KV cache for streaming video that promotes salient KV pairs to parents, keeps residuals in children, and searches best-first.
SxLSMZz5SR.problem: Streaming video understanding must store evidence for questions unknown at arrival time, and existing granularity-agnostic storage compresses all evidence uniformly, losing detail at different granularities.
SxLSMZz5SR.method: ResKV-Tree merges nodes by semantic similarity, temporal proximity and evidence saliency, applies KV non-maximum suppression to drop redundant KV pairs, recursively promotes salient KV pairs to parents while residuals stay in children, and answers questions by best-first search from the roots.
SxLSMZz5SR.key_idea: Recursively splits cached KV pairs into salient parent and residual child sets, enabling question-guided best-first retrieval at multiple granularities.
SxLSMZz5SR.evidence: Two streaming and three offline video understanding benchmarks across three backbones (StreamingBench and OVO-Bench with Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B and LLaVA-OV per reviews).
SxLSMZz5SR.claimed_gains: The abstract gives no numbers (superior to baselines and recent methods across three backbones); reviewers cite Qwen2.5-VL-7B rising from 73.31 to 80.48 on StreamingBench.
SxLSMZz5SR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the residual hierarchy is well motivated, training-free, and gives consistent gains across backbones on streaming and offline benchmarks.
SxLSMZz5SR.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed to the tree components (a stripped variant already gets about 70% of the gain), and results are single runs with incomplete baselines.

QZEReO7jbW.one_liner: Newton's method applied to a nonlinearly preconditioned optimality mapping, analyzed under Lipschitz continuity of a preconditioned Hessian.
QZEReO7jbW.problem: Newton-type methods are analyzed under Lipschitz continuity of the Hessian, which fails for objectives with higher-order or polynomial growth.
QZEReO7jbW.method: Applies Newton's root-finding scheme to a transformed optimality mapping and proves local superlinear and quadratic convergence under Lipschitz continuity of the preconditioned Hessian. It adds a globalization strategy for the non-regularized method, a regularized variant for isotropic preconditioners, and an adaptive version that tolerates inexact subproblem solutions.
QZEReO7jbW.key_idea: Transforms the optimality condition with a nonlinear preconditioner and runs Newton on it, so convergence needs only Lipschitz continuity of the preconditioned Hessian.
QZEReO7jbW.evidence: Theoretical convergence and complexity analysis; no experiments are described in the abstract or reviews.
QZEReO7jbW.claimed_gains: The regularized variant returns an approximate (eps_g, eps_H)-second-order stationary point in O(max{eps_g^(-3/2), eps_H^(-3)}) iterations, and the adaptive version keeps the same complexity order.
QZEReO7jbW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the nonlinear-preconditioning idea is elegant, with a sound convergence analysis that relaxes the classical Hessian-Lipschitz assumption.
QZEReO7jbW.main_concern: The comparison with the closest generalized-smooth Newton and cubic-regularized work (Fang et al., 2026) is missing, so the practical and quantitative advantage is unclear.

mPTOxcFj25.one_liner: Training-free interface converting external controls into clean visual evidence consumed by a frozen causal video world model's self-attention.
mPTOxcFj25.problem: Extending pretrained video world models to new forms of control typically requires control-specific architectures or additional training.
mPTOxcFj25.method: World in World converts source observations, target-view projections, rendered geometry and generated history into clean visual evidence annotated with camera, temporal and spatial-validity information. Correspondence-guided attention routing (CGAR) directs queries to geometrically corresponding tokens, and evidence-wise attention CFG (EWA) regulates each source's influence; it is instantiated on a frozen LingBot-World 2.0 backbone.
mPTOxcFj25.key_idea: Feeds heterogeneous controls as annotated clean visual tokens through the backbone's native self-attention, routing queries to geometrically corresponding tokens and weighting evidence sources with attention-level CFG.
mPTOxcFj25.evidence: Camera-controlled video rerendering on DAVIS and OpenVid-1M across viewpoint changes, comparisons with six baselines, and same-backbone ablations (per reviews).
mPTOxcFj25.claimed_gains: Not stated in the visible abstract; reviewers cite a PSNR of 22.98 for the full system versus 20.92 for target-view warping alone.
mPTOxcFj25.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using native self-attention as a unified, training-free interface for heterogeneous controls is elegant and competitive against baselines.
mPTOxcFj25.main_concern: The advance over Warp-as-History (training-free camera control through the native visual-history pathway) is unclear without a direct same-backbone comparison, and the method depends on external geometry estimates.

FOQhjQTkzj.one_liner: Multi-bit LLM watermark spreading coded payload bits across tokens with soft-decision ECC and unbiased multilayer reweighting.
FOQhjQTkzj.problem: Existing multi-bit LLM watermarks trade off extraction accuracy, text quality, and payload capacity.
FOQhjQTkzj.method: WeaveMark lets each token carry several payload bits through multilayer reweighting (weaving), shuffles layers to spread observations across bits, and decodes with soft-decision error-correcting codes; dedicated zero-bit layers detect watermark presence.
FOQhjQTkzj.key_idea: Let each token carry several coded payload bits through unbiased multilayer reweighting, shuffle layers to balance observations per bit, and decode with soft-decision ECC.
FOQhjQTkzj.evidence: Experiments against BiMark on message match rate under editing attacks, with appendix tests on other model families, messages up to 64 bits, insertion and deletion, mixed editing, rewriting, and translation and summarization quality checks.
FOQhjQTkzj.claimed_gains: 89.8% match rate for 32-bit messages at 200 tokens versus 20.8% for BiMark; under 10% substitution attacks on 16-bit messages at 200 tokens, 86.0% versus 30.7%.
FOQhjQTkzj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the components well motivated and the experiments broad, crediting spreading and layer shuffling for part of the gains.
FOQhjQTkzj.main_concern: Gains are not cleanly attributed: most improvement appears after adding soft ECC, and the attack and long-message tables compare mainly against BiMark without that component.

szFBNMQo7M.one_liner: Training-free rectification of intermediate denoising states in unified multimodal models using the model's own understanding-based reflection.
szFBNMQo7M.problem: Unified multimodal models understand better than they generate, so their internal understanding is underused during image generation.
szFBNMQo7M.method: At intermediate denoising steps the model produces a state-conditioned reflection whose autoregressive negative log-likelihood defines a model-native semantic loss; its gradient rectifies the image latent, and candidates are chosen with a likelihood-based score from the same model.
szFBNMQo7M.key_idea: Backpropagate the UMM's own likelihood of a state-conditioned reflection to the intermediate image latent during denoising, and pick candidates with the same model's likelihood score.
szFBNMQo7M.evidence: GenEval and DPG-Bench on four flow-based UMMs (Janus-Flow, OpenUni-RecA, OmniGen2, BAGEL), with semantic-target ablations.
szFBNMQo7M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit a training-free, model-native design with consistent gains across four UMMs and targeted ablations on the reflection target and selection.
szFBNMQo7M.main_concern: Overlap with related work and thin analysis of the proxy: interleaved reflection and likelihood-based rewards already exist, and failure and over-rectification analysis is limited.

fhfwDlMovu.one_liner: Current-mode CMOS analog circuit for Bistable Memory Recurrent Units whose discrete outputs stop noise accumulating over time.
fhfwDlMovu.problem: Analog inference is mostly feedforward because recurrent feedback is considered impractical due to noise accumulation through time.
fhfwDlMovu.method: Co-designs BMRUs, RNNs with discrete outputs and hysteretic dynamics, as a current-mode analog circuit with a one-to-one map from learned parameters to circuit elements, after reformulating them for first-quadrant operation with fixed thresholds.
fhfwDlMovu.key_idea: Discrete BMRU outputs confine analog errors to near-threshold events at each cell boundary, so noise cannot accumulate through time; learned parameters map directly to bias currents and mirror ratios.
fhfwDlMovu.evidence: Transistor-level simulations in 180 nm CMOS compared with software predictions, with reviews citing 49 of 50 prediction agreement at roughly 100 nW core power and sMNIST/pMNIST comparisons.
fhfwDlMovu.claimed_gains: Transistor-level simulations in 180 nm CMOS show close agreement between software predictions and circuit behavior, down to each cell's binary state; no numeric gain stated.
fhfwDlMovu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the explicit parameter-to-circuit correspondence and its transistor-level validation.
fhfwDlMovu.main_concern: Evidence is simulation-only at tiny scale (d=4, two layers, binary keyword spotting) with larger-scale claims extrapolated and no silicon; one review also disputes the expressivity proof.

nS6Whua0UL.one_liner: Computes globally optimal channel-wise quantization scales under round-to-nearest by exploiting piecewise-quadratic layer-output error.
nS6Whua0UL.problem: Post-training quantization scale factors are usually set by simple data-free heuristics even though they define the quantization grid.
nS6Whua0UL.method: PiSO sweeps the finitely many intervals over which RTN grid assignments are constant, applying each interval's closed-form minimizer on calibration data; it extends to group-wise quantization and integrates with GPTQ and Qronos.
nS6Whua0UL.key_idea: Under RTN, grid assignments are piecewise constant in the scale, so layer-output error is piecewise quadratic and the global minimum is found by an incremental sweep over intervals.
nS6Whua0UL.evidence: Llama and Qwen models across sizes and bit-widths, standalone and combined with GPTQ and Qronos, measured by perplexity and zero-shot accuracy.
nS6Whua0UL.claimed_gains: Consistent perplexity and zero-shot gains that grow as bit-width narrows; on Llama-3, PiSO reduces the 2-bit perplexity of Qronos by up to 7x.
nS6Whua0UL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory solid and the closed-form scale optimization a clever, practically useful advance that integrates with GPTQ and Qronos.
nS6Whua0UL.main_concern: Optimality holds only for channel-wise RTN, not for error-correcting methods such as GPTQ and Qronos that move weights off the nearest grid points; group-wise extensions are heuristic.

XY3EbTkYXj.one_liner: Cellular-automata benchmark isolating rule-shift in transition dynamics to evaluate out-of-distribution generalization in reinforcement learning.
XY3EbTkYXj.problem: RL out-of-distribution benchmarks change dynamics, observations, goals, and rewards together, so generalization failures are hard to attribute.
XY3EbTkYXj.method: TAPE varies only the cellular-automaton transition rule while fixing observation-action interface, goal, and reward, using deterministic splits, 20-seed replication, bootstrap uncertainty, and continuous endpoints for sparse-success regimes.
XY3EbTkYXj.key_idea: Hold interface, goal, and reward fixed and vary only a finite, explicit space of cellular-automaton transition rules, so held-out-rule performance isolates dynamics generalization.
XY3EbTkYXj.evidence: Baseline families, matched heuristic controls, recurrent and rule-inference controls, finite-budget true-dynamics planning, and exact smaller-scale reachability analysis, over 20 seeds.
XY3EbTkYXj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a clear, cheap, controlled testbed with extensive multi-seed, multi-algorithm evaluation.
XY3EbTkYXj.main_concern: The benchmark's added value over neighboring benchmarks is unclear, and changing rules also changes task difficulty, which confounds the claimed isolation; most baselines lack memory to infer rules.

vnj6zGKI7q.one_liner: Unified song generation model with a two-stream Cover-Tokenizer and joint autoregressive-diffusion training via continuous hidden-state conditioning.
vnj6zGKI7q.problem: Song generation work centers on text-conditioned generation with limited cover-song support, and AR and diffusion stages are trained separately and linked only by discrete tokens.
vnj6zGKI7q.method: Mugi supports text-to-song, cover, and timbre-controllable generation; a Cover-Tokenizer encodes melody and linguistic content as parallel token streams, and the diffusion model is conditioned on the AR model's continuous hidden states, training both with language-modeling and flow-matching losses end to end.
vnj6zGKI7q.key_idea: Condition the diffusion decoder on the AR model's continuous hidden states with gradient flow, so the flow-matching loss also updates the AR model, alongside a melody-plus-content two-stream tokenizer.
vnj6zGKI7q.evidence: Subjective and objective evaluations across text-to-song, cover, and timbre tasks (SongBench, AudioBox, MuQ, pitch metrics, phoneme error rate) plus ablations on tokenizer features and continuous versus discrete conditioning.
vnj6zGKI7q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the coherent multi-task framework and the joint-training and tokenizer ablations.
vnj6zGKI7q.main_concern: Evaluation of the distinctive cover and timbre claims is mostly automatic: human evaluation covers only text-to-song, test sets are small, and metrics do not show harmony, rhythm, or alignment preservation.

8GyKjbTQUd.one_liner: Shows stop-on-success logging lets episode duration alone reveal outcomes, making agreement-based robot policy evaluator validation uninformative.
8GyKjbTQUd.problem: Validating robot policy evaluators by agreement with success labels can give no evidence of evaluation ability when the protocol itself reveals the outcome.
8GyKjbTQUd.method: Intervenes on the termination channel, builds a frame-blind witness that reproduces a vision-language judge's metrics, formalizes an evidence budget and randomization floor for certification, and proposes fixed-horizon logging.
8GyKjbTQUd.key_idea: Under stop-on-success, failures all end at the time horizon so duration separates outcomes; fixed-horizon logging removes this duration leakage without adding rollouts.
8GyKjbTQUd.evidence: A controlled termination-channel intervention, a frame-blind witness matching a VLM judge's metrics, and a screen of 47 conditions against the derived randomization floor.
8GyKjbTQUd.claimed_gains: Across 47 screened conditions, only two satisfy the randomization floor, and neither remains admissible after suppressing the termination channel.
8GyKjbTQUd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the critique relevant and the theory plus termination-channel intervention convincing.
8GyKjbTQUd.main_concern: The presentation is hard to follow, and the frame-blind witness is built from the original evaluator's scores, so the scope of the non-identifiability claim needs clearer limits.

mq6KFxmjdK.one_liner: EM over covariance priors using conditional stochastic interpolants trained on their own reconstructions to sample posteriors from noisy estimates.
mq6KFxmjdK.problem: Given only noisy empirical covariances from a known sampling mechanism, learn the prior over true covariances and sample the posterior when no clean covariance is ever observed.
mq6KFxmjdK.method: Distributional EM where each step's posterior sampler is a conditional stochastic interpolant trained on simulated pairs from the current prior; a variant for rotationally invariant priors learns only the eigenvalue distribution and draws orientation from an explicit conditional law.
mq6KFxmjdK.key_idea: Train a conditional stochastic interpolant on pairs simulated from the current prior estimate and use it as the posterior sampler inside each EM iteration.
mq6KFxmjdK.evidence: An identifiability theorem (exact when each estimate uses at least as many samples as dimensions), convergence analysis, synthetic prior recovery, and EEG and market-record experiments.
mq6KFxmjdK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the identifiability and convergence theory and the distinction between observation-space fit and latent prior recovery.
mq6KFxmjdK.main_concern: Empirical claims look overstated: the reconstructed posterior has a visible Wasserstein gap to the oracle, EEG gains shrink in full-cohort evaluation, and the finance setup has inconsistent likelihood specifications.

n3kgaLYA4p.one_liner: Solves semilinear PDEs with BSDE-style losses on Brownian bridges that end on the domain boundary, sampled in closed form.
n3kgaLYA4p.problem: BSDE-based deep solvers need sequential path simulation and, on bounded domains, random exit times that add numerical error.
n3kgaLYA4p.method: Uses Ito's formula for general continuous semimartingales to derive a loss on Brownian bridges whose terminal endpoint lies on the boundary, so boundary data enter the interior residual and samples are generated in parallel.
n3kgaLYA4p.key_idea: Brownian bridges with endpoints prescribed on the boundary give closed-form Gaussian samples and remove exit times, because Ito's formula holds beyond Markov processes.
n3kgaLYA4p.evidence: Comparisons against PINNs, BSDE losses, and the diffusion loss, and against recent BSDE time-discretization methods on a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman example.
n3kgaLYA4p.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory clear and the closed-form bridge sampling with boundary anchoring a well-motivated, useful training strategy.
n3kgaLYA4p.main_concern: Boundary-handling consistency is not justified (bridges may leave the domain and node rejection does not preserve the bridge law), and one review gives a counterexample to the general zero-loss equivalence claim.

XHSWDmsGta.one_liner: LLM layer over lexical scientific search that plans subqueries and selects evidence, serving natural-language requests from agents.
XHSWDmsGta.problem: Lexical scientific search engines expect keyword syntax and return whole papers, forcing each agent to issue several searches and read full articles.
XHSWDmsGta.method: LIBRARIAN uses a single LLM to plan complementary subqueries executed by the search engine (instantiated on Europe PMC), then read selected papers and return the passages that answer the request.
XHSWDmsGta.key_idea: One LLM orchestrates retrieval on top of an existing lexical index: plan subqueries, run the search engine, then select evidence passages, with no new dense index.
XHSWDmsGta.evidence: ScholarQABench plus literature synthesis, claim verification, and open-form question answering with several agents, biology workflow tasks as a control, and ablations on evidence selection.
XHSWDmsGta.claimed_gains: On ScholarQABench, with corpus and Synthesis Agent fixed, LIBRARIAN improves Citation F1 over BM25 by 6.0 and 8.7 points (abstract continues beyond the provided text).
XHSWDmsGta.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the system gives consistent gains across benchmarks and agents, and ablations show LLM evidence selection matters.
XHSWDmsGta.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (query expansion, BM25, and LLM evidence selection are established), and several comparisons mix retrieval changes with changes in model, corpus, or pipeline.

D24KshjoH7.one_liner: Agents learn executable cognitive programs of Ground, Plan, Check, and Act operations with a cost-aware router and test-time repair.
D24KshjoH7.problem: Adaptive reasoning methods choose among predefined reasoning modes and cannot evolve structured cognitive procedures across interactive environments.
D24KshjoH7.method: Programs built from four typed operations under a causal grammar are learned in three stages: program-conditioned SFT, Sparse Counterfactual Program Optimization (SCPO) for execution and a step-level router, and test-time program repair from failures without parameter updates.
D24KshjoH7.key_idea: Represent reasoning as grammar-constrained programs over Ground/Plan/Check/Act, train a router to pick programs per step via sparse counterfactual optimization, and repair programs from failures at test time.
D24KshjoH7.evidence: ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and WebShop experiments with Qwen2.5-7B against GPT-5 and other baselines, with ablations and token-cost comparisons.
D24KshjoH7.claimed_gains: With Qwen2.5-7B, EvoCog reaches a 77.47% success rate, outperforming GPT-5 (+26.57%) (abstract continues beyond the provided text).
D24KshjoH7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit adaptive reasoning routing, an effective SCPO objective, and low token use with clear ablations.
D24KshjoH7.main_concern: Novelty and generality are limited: only Qwen2.5-7B is tested, the four-operation abstraction is not analyzed, comparisons with CogRouter and similar methods lack statistical evidence, and reproducibility details are missing.

34LPPnJLer.one_liner: Benchmark of 20,655 dialogue cases for 37 game NPCs testing whether LLMs stay in character under supplied state.
34LPPnJLer.problem: Game NPCs are bound to authored dialogue, and LLM role-play lacks evaluation of whether a model keeps a character's obligations and boundaries given its state.
34LPPnJLer.method: NPCBank builds structured dialogue cases from source evidence using a capability ontology, a contract-based case schema, and a construction agent, with a web inspection tool, a demo game, and three challenges (supplied-state role-play, consumer-GPU inference, long-horizon persistence).
34LPPnJLer.key_idea: Each case contract separates what a reply must do (obligations) from what it must not violate (invariants), tied to an explicit state, with matched state pairs probing state sensitivity.
34LPPnJLer.evidence: 20,655 cases for 37 NPCs across seven games covering 21 dialogue capabilities, with model evaluations on three challenges, judge audits, and matched-state experiments.
34LPPnJLer.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the benchmark as solidly constructed and the obligations-versus-invariants design and matched-state interventions as interpretable and valuable.
34LPPnJLer.main_concern: Judge reliability and construct coverage: absolute pass rates look inflated and judge bias varies across systems, most cases are static, and the rationale for the capability taxonomy is unclear.

8n63rxHToT.one_liner: Training-free foveated resampling of ultra-high-resolution remote-sensing images guided by a frozen MLLM's question-based region selection.
8n63rxHToT.problem: Selection-based and crop-based methods do not redistribute pixels within a continuous full-scene view, and cropping detached from context does not reliably improve MLLM answers on ultra-high-resolution imagery.
8n63rxHToT.method: The MLLM selects evidence cells from an indexed overview; a deterministic, topology-preserving warp resamples the full image onto a fixed-size canvas, enlarging their neighborhood and compressing the periphery; the same frozen model answers, using at most two MLLM calls.
8n63rxHToT.key_idea: Spend a fixed pixel budget by warping the whole scene so question-selected cells are magnified and the periphery compressed, instead of cropping.
8n63rxHToT.evidence: Three UHR remote-sensing benchmarks and four frozen backbones, with a pilot study separating localization from presentation and a one-region, four-rendering comparison.
8n63rxHToT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple, cheap, and training-free, with a useful pilot study showing cropping can hurt and consistent results across backbones.
8n63rxHToT.main_concern: Headline comparisons against task-trained methods are confounded by different backbones, same-backbone gains over the Overview baseline are smaller, and a rule-based bounding-box bypass is not reported.

X2cuvFmdQ5.one_liner: Data-free continual model merging that keeps a fixed-budget shared-private memory of historical task directions instead of cumulative-vector subspaces.
X2cuvFmdQ5.problem: Historical subspaces built from the cumulative merged task vector degrade as tasks accumulate in data-free continual merging.
X2cuvFmdQ5.method: CUSP-Merge stores explicit historical directions: directions supported across tasks go to Shared Memory, task-specific residuals to Private Memory, and private directions are promoted by cumulative cross-task support; direction-level adaptive protection balances stability and plasticity.
X2cuvFmdQ5.key_idea: Maintain explicit shared and private direction memories of fixed size, promoting private directions to shared by cross-task support, rather than reconstructing history from the merged vector.
X2cuvFmdQ5.evidence: Multiple architectures and task configurations (including 8-, 14-, and 20-task sequences on ViT-B/32), averaged over ten task orders, with coverage analysis and a growing-memory comparison.
X2cuvFmdQ5.claimed_gains: Highest average accuracy in all settings, with more pronounced gains on longer task sequences; no numbers in the provided abstract text.
X2cuvFmdQ5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated and the explicit directional memory plausible, with experiments across architectures and sequence lengths supporting the main claims.
X2cuvFmdQ5.main_concern: The source of gains is not isolated and not statistically tested: CUSP-Merge stores 320 directions versus rank-128 for NUFILT, and there are no paired tests for the modest gains in 8- and 14-task settings.

CJ5flUjgS0.one_liner: Temporal convolutional decoder aligns windows of fMRI frames with text, audio and speech embeddings to retrieve heard speech segments.
CJ5flUjgS0.problem: fMRI's noisy, temporally smeared measurements make the multi-timescale structure of naturalistic speech hard to recover from brain activity.
CJ5flUjgS0.method: NOEMA is a temporal convolutional decoder that aligns windows of consecutive fMRI measurements with stimulus embeddings combining text, audio and speech representations of the same segment, so the segment is retrieved directly from brain activity. Per reviewers, training uses CLIP-style contrastive learning with pretrained embeddings.
CJ5flUjgS0.key_idea: Align a window of consecutive fMRI frames, via temporal convolution, with combined text, audio and speech stimulus embeddings through contrastive retrieval.
CJ5flUjgS0.evidence: Two naturalistic speech datasets (Cephalonauts One and LeBel), with ablations of temporal modeling and stimulus representations and retrieval pools extended with thousands of distractors absent from training.
CJ5flUjgS0.claimed_gains: Retrieves the correct segment among 2,000 candidates within the top 10 for more than 42% of held-out queries, substantially outperforming baseline decoders.
CJ5flUjgS0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree NOEMA consistently beats the evaluated baselines across both datasets and participants, with session-disjoint evaluation and substantial ablation analysis.
CJ5flUjgS0.main_concern: Baselines and novelty are limited: no transformer-based fMRI decoders are compared, and the model combines standard temporal convolutions, pretrained embeddings and CLIP-style contrastive learning.

SzYbCqS5c7.one_liner: Distributional credit assignment turns learned conditional return distributions into per-step risk advantages for PPO under a lower-quantile return constraint.
SzYbCqS5c7.problem: Maximizing expected return under a lower-quantile constraint requires assigning trajectory-level risk to individual decisions, which terminal binary violation outcomes alone do not support.
SzYbCqS5c7.method: Accumulated rewards define the future return still needed to meet the constraint, a transition-based risk advantage is defined from the change in violation probability between consecutive augmented states, and those probabilities come from return distributions learned by distributional Bellman updates. Risk and reward advantages are combined in PPO.
SzYbCqS5c7.key_idea: Risk advantage is the change in estimated violation probability between consecutive budget-augmented states, computed from learned conditional future-return distributions.
SzYbCqS5c7.evidence: Theory (density-free risk-gradient representation, risk-gradient error bounds, convergence under a three-time-scale stochastic approximation) and experiments in a synthetic mean-risk trade-off environment and SimpleButton against QCPO and TQPO.
SzYbCqS5c7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well written and coherent, linking accumulated rewards, distributional estimation, and per-step risk feedback clearly, with error bounds and convergence analysis under stated assumptions.
SzYbCqS5c7.main_concern: Empirical coverage is narrow (one synthetic task and SimpleButton, a single 20% violation level, only QCPO and TQPO as baselines) and the theory is asymptotic, with Theorem 2 assuming much of what it claims.

Bn5aaQlNC2.one_liner: Malicious third-party skills exploit metadata-to-body trust transfer and instruction-hierarchy training to hijack LLM agents and plant persistent instructions in memory.
Bn5aaQlNC2.problem: Instruction hierarchy training defends against prompt injection, but third-party skill text is a new attack surface whose benign metadata sits in high-authority positions, and models poorly recognize natural-language text carrying malicious intent.
Bn5aaQlNC2.method: HierJack uses natural-language payloads in skill bodies that gain authority through the agent's metadata-body mapping, so the agent generates and executes malicious scripts and writes malicious instructions into local memory files that persist after the skill is removed.
Bn5aaQlNC2.key_idea: Skill metadata placed in high-authority context transfers trust to the skill body, so natural-language payloads that evade code audits are obeyed and can persist via memory writes.
Bn5aaQlNC2.evidence: 16 LLM-agent combinations with a carrier comparison, payload ablations, scanner tests, a defense test, and a position-swap study according to reviews, plus payloads ported from InjecAgent (abstract truncated).
Bn5aaQlNC2.claimed_gains: Average one-shot attack success rate of 88.46% and average persistent ASR of 69.57% across 16 LLM-agent combinations.
Bn5aaQlNC2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the threat is important and well scoped, the persistent compromise after skill removal is concerning, and the evaluation is broad across agents, models, and ablations.
Bn5aaQlNC2.main_concern: The metadata-to-body trust-transfer mechanism is not isolated by controlled experiments because carrier conditions differ in several factors, and realism is limited by preinstalled skills in Full-Access mode.

3Tu3NsZPhh.one_liner: Prunes cross-expert attention connectivity in Mixture-of-Transformer robot policies during fine-tuning, keeping fusion in the early half.
3Tu3NsZPhh.problem: Mixture-of-Transformers robot policies keep dense expert connectivity across depth, and it is unclear how much of it downstream adaptation needs.
3Tu3NsZPhh.method: They sparsify pretrained MoT policies during fine-tuning across multiple architectures and manipulation benchmarks, then propose an early-half fusion pattern that concentrates cross-expert connectivity in the first half of the network and structurally prunes the rest.
3Tu3NsZPhh.key_idea: Mask cross-expert connections during fine-tuning and keep them only in the first half of the network, enabling truncation of unused conditioning layers and smaller KV caches.
3Tu3NsZPhh.evidence: Sparsification of pretrained MoT policies (pi0.5, InternVLA-A1, and others per reviewers) on robot manipulation benchmarks such as LIBERO and RoboTwin, with deployment measurements of parameters, memory, and latency.
3Tu3NsZPhh.claimed_gains: Half of the dense expert connectivity can be pruned during fine-tuning with little loss (TL;DR), with reductions in loaded parameters, GPU memory, and per-chunk latency; no exact percentages are stated in the abstract.
3Tu3NsZPhh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is simple and relevant to deployment cost, the paper is clearly written, and the measurements cover deployment efficiency (parameters, latency) as well as task success.
