ZfqmvwU6VV.problem: Poorly tuned and hard-to-reproduce long-horizon RL baselines obscure whether gains come from new methods or infrastructure fixes.
ZfqmvwU6VV.method: XYZ-SWE uses small-pool overfitting to diagnose failures and coordinate gated rewards, importance-weight control, aligned training and inference engines, and consistent policy-update state. It then filters and refines R2E-Gym, SWE-rebench V2, and Scale-SWE training data.
ZfqmvwU6VV.key_idea: Use overfitting on a small task pool to reveal hidden training failures and guide coordinated optimization and system repairs.
ZfqmvwU6VV.evidence: Experiments train Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B and evaluate SWE-bench Verified and Pro variants using raw and curated software-engineering data.
ZfqmvwU6VV.claimed_gains: Raw-data training reaches 62.0% pass@1 versus FrogNano's 61.5% after about one-sixth as many rollouts, and curation raises 4B scores from 47.4%/25.0%/37.9% to 65.0%/38.3%/59.7% on SWE-bench Verified/Pro-v1/Pro-v2.
ZfqmvwU6VV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the documented training failures and coordinated engineering practices useful for building stronger long-horizon RL baselines.
ZfqmvwU6VV.main_concern: Mostly single-seed experiments in one harness and one model family do not establish the recipe's stability or broader generality.

kvqVPElzC8.one_liner: A local verification simulator separates GUI answer correctness from acceptance of grounded interaction traces.
kvqVPElzC8.problem: GUI-agent benchmarks often omit verification steps that require visual reasoning, state tracking, and process-consistent interaction.
kvqVPElzC8.method: HLL provides authorized local CAPTCHA-style tasks varying intrinsic difficulty, webpage distraction, and trace-conditioned validation. Static and dynamic variants distinguish semantic correctness from interaction acceptance, with legality audits and trace-repair studies.
kvqVPElzC8.key_idea: Evaluate semantic answers and simulator-observed interaction traces separately under controlled verification rules.
kvqVPElzC8.evidence: Eight multimodal agents use a common Mobile-Agent-v2 harness in Android/Chrome across ten task families, supplemented by legality audits and trace-repair experiments.
kvqVPElzC8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating answer correctness from interaction acceptance and auditing both agent and validator errors.
kvqVPElzC8.main_concern: Dynamic rules reject some legal actions, so low acceptance scores may reflect validator restrictions rather than agent capability.

bm5Bvszv36.one_liner: Offline token-specific confidence thresholds determine which diffusion-language-model predictions can commit in parallel.
bm5Bvszv36.problem: A global confidence threshold treats equally confident tokens as equally reliable despite systematic token-dependent miscalibration.
bm5Bvszv36.method: TC-APD estimates a separate confidence threshold for each vocabulary token from offline denoising traces. Inference uses token-ID threshold lookups for adaptive parallel decoding without additional model components.
bm5Bvszv36.key_idea: Calibrate confidence thresholds separately by token identity and use them to select parallel commitments during diffusion decoding.
bm5Bvszv36.evidence: Mathematical reasoning and code-generation experiments compare speed-quality trade-offs against fixed-threshold decoders and examine token-dependent final consistency.
bm5Bvszv36.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find token-dependent miscalibration empirically motivated and appreciate the negligible online overhead of threshold lookup.
bm5Bvszv36.main_concern: Calibration reliability remains insufficiently established across data sizes, domains, and the altered trajectories produced by earlier token commitments.

YXADNJNBj1.one_liner: Optimal transport aligns teacher-student prediction evolution and selects supervision that addresses student deficiencies.
YXADNJNBj1.problem: Static layer matching can align different refinement stages, while indiscriminate transfer can supply teacher signals that do not help the student.
YXADNJNBj1.method: EvaKD uses prediction-evolution optimal transport to align teacher and student refinement across depth and selectively transfer beneficial signals. It reuses each model's normalization and output head rather than introducing learned representation projectors.
YXADNJNBj1.key_idea: Match teacher and student prediction-refinement stages through optimal transport and weight transfer according to its usefulness for student deficiencies.
YXADNJNBj1.evidence: Experiments compare output-layer and intermediate-layer distillation across two model families in domain-agnostic and domain-specific settings, with ablations.
YXADNJNBj1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize useful intermediate-layer transfer and strong empirical results without extra trainable alignment parameters.
YXADNJNBj1.main_concern: The four representative evolution stages used in practice are unspecified and leave the claimed flexible alignment mechanism difficult to assess.

sXAa9qlMpr.one_liner: Training-set randomness defines expected adversarial risk, whose gradients motivate a data-centric purification objective.
sXAa9qlMpr.problem: The conditions under which adversarial purification works remain unclear, particularly when local class overlap or imbalance affects density guidance.
sXAa9qlMpr.method: The paper defines Expected Adversarial Risk as mislabeling probability across randomly sampled datasets and analyzes alignment between purification directions and its negative gradient. It derives an EAR-inspired purification objective based on class-density margins.
sXAa9qlMpr.key_idea: Analyze purification through alignment with the negative gradient of training-set-averaged classification error and construct a class-density-margin objective.
sXAa9qlMpr.evidence: Theoretical analysis using a fixed-radius nearest-neighbor classifier accompanies experiments on synthetic and image datasets.
sXAa9qlMpr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a data-centric explanation of purification that examines finite-sample instability, class overlap, and imbalance.
sXAa9qlMpr.main_concern: The theory does not sufficiently connect finite-sample EAR and its approximate gradient alignment to conventional adversarial robustness or effective purification.

sfqzH7IzsJ.one_liner: CIG-SFT weights demonstrated tokens using task-conditioned likelihood ratios and a KL-regularized policy projection.
sfqzH7IzsJ.problem: Supervised fine-tuning can disrupt pretrained behaviors, while predictive compatibility does not necessarily identify tokens worth learning.
sfqzH7IzsJ.method: CIG-SFT compares frozen-reference token likelihoods with and without the task input while fixing the gold solution prefix. It converts this conditional information gain into a KL-regularized projection of the current policy.
sfqzH7IzsJ.key_idea: Compare reference-model token likelihoods with and without task input, then use the conditional information gain in a KL-regularized policy projection.
sfqzH7IzsJ.evidence: Mathematical reasoning and code generation experiments compare standard and adaptive SFT, with component ablations and sensitivity analyses.
sfqzH7IzsJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the distinction between task information and predictability and report useful empirical results across math and code.
sfqzH7IzsJ.main_concern: Reviewers question whether task-conditioned information measures learning value, especially when probability-dependent weights suppress unfamiliar but useful tokens.

avL29Lomou.one_liner: ANPO separates stage rewards and estimates tool necessity to train small multimodal agents when and how to use tools.
avL29Lomou.problem: Small multimodal agents misinterpret tool results and invoke tools unnecessarily, while trajectory rewards conflate tool decisions with downstream failures.
avL29Lomou.method: ANPO rewards tool decisions, execution, and final answers separately. It evaluates tool-call decisions using question-specific tool necessity rather than only individual trajectory outcomes.
avL29Lomou.key_idea: Assign separate rewards to decision, execution, and answer stages while conditioning tool-decision rewards on estimated question-level necessity.
avL29Lomou.evidence: Experiments cover fifteen benchmarks, two model sizes, and four tools, with baseline comparisons and reward-component ablations.
avL29Lomou.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the diagnosis of tool-use credit assignment and the broad experimental evaluation.
avL29Lomou.main_concern: Reviewers question the stability of necessity estimates from few tool-on and tool-off rollouts and the lack of sensitivity or uncertainty analysis.

dQkcRU0Fpo.one_liner: OR-License evaluates agents on original industrial optimization materials using simulated client interactions and expert-relative feasibility checks.
dQkcRU0Fpo.problem: Existing operations research benchmarks underrepresent translating incomplete client materials into professionally validated executable solutions.
dQkcRU0Fpo.method: OR-License preserves de-identified industrial requirements and deliverables, while ORSim discloses client facts without optimization expertise. Hidden checks assess feasibility and expert-relative objective quality, assigning infeasible deliveries zero DAQ credit.
dQkcRU0Fpo.key_idea: Combine original client materials, controlled fact disclosure, and hidden feasibility checks with expert-relative quality scoring.
dQkcRU0Fpo.evidence: The benchmark evaluates 11 frontier LLMs on 31 instances across 10 industrial scenarios drawn from engagements totaling $3.68 million.
dQkcRU0Fpo.claimed_gains: The strongest system achieves 83.23% strict feasibility and a DAQ of 0.82, while none matches the expert reference's DAQ.
dQkcRU0Fpo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the real industrial source materials and the evaluation of requirement interpretation through executable solutions.
dQkcRU0Fpo.main_concern: Reviewers find the experimental controls and reporting insufficient to establish the effects of client interaction and support model comparisons.

YBHzwQ0OsR.one_liner: ReoNa distills region-specific channel usage from vision foundation models into CLIP for segmentation under appearance shifts.
YBHzwQ0OsR.problem: Feature-level distillation does not prevent CLIP's dense representations from deteriorating on unseen visual domains.
YBHzwQ0OsR.method: ReoNa uses vision-foundation-model-guided region-to-channel distillation to encourage CLIP to reuse MLP channel support across appearances. Region-specific routers reweight internal MLP activations.
YBHzwQ0OsR.key_idea: Use teacher-guided region routers to reweight CLIP MLP channels and encourage consistent channel usage across appearances.
YBHzwQ0OsR.evidence: Experiments evaluate open-vocabulary domain-generalized semantic segmentation across multiple benchmarks, including zero-shot and fine-tuned decoder settings.
YBHzwQ0OsR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent segmentation gains and the relevance of transferring stable internal channel usage to CLIP.
YBHzwQ0OsR.main_concern: Reviewers agree that the neuron attribution analysis does not establish semantic circuit consistency or isolate the benefit of channel routing.

oOy3m7NmDu.one_liner: An additive power law models long-context training returns, while averaging recent checkpoints tracks an extensible constant-learning-rate run.
oOy3m7NmDu.problem: The relationship between long-context continual pretraining token budgets and subsequent long-context performance remains unclear.
oOy3m7NmDu.method: The paper fits an additive power law over model size and short- and long-context training budgets. Constant-Last4 averages the four most recent consecutive checkpoints to monitor a constant-learning-rate training trajectory.
oOy3m7NmDu.key_idea: Model short- and long-context token budgets separately and monitor constant-learning-rate training through rolling four-checkpoint averages.
oOy3m7NmDu.evidence: Experiments span five model scales and over one hundred budget configurations, including a 1.22B-parameter model with approximately 100B LCCP tokens.
oOy3m7NmDu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the systematic multi-scale budget study and empirical validation of the predictive scaling law.
oOy3m7NmDu.main_concern: Reviewers consistently question generalization beyond the single architecture family, fixed data mixture, GovReport LongPPL target, and models up to 1.22B parameters.

h3bawejFSA.one_liner: A primal-dual trading algorithm adapts regret to adversarial corruption while maintaining global budget balance.
h3bawejFSA.problem: Stochastic and adversarial bilateral-trade settings permit no-regret learning against different budget-balanced pricing benchmarks.
h3bawejFSA.method: The paper designs a corruption-adaptive algorithm for stochastic markets subject to adversarial perturbations. Its primal-dual formulation maintains global budget balance while providing guarantees against distributional and per-round budget-balanced benchmarks.
h3bawejFSA.key_idea: Use a corruption-adaptive primal-dual algorithm to preserve global budget balance while competing against different pricing benchmarks.
h3bawejFSA.evidence: Theoretical analysis establishes corruption-dependent regret against a distributional benchmark under smoothness and worst-case fixed-price regret without smoothness.
h3bawejFSA.claimed_gains: The algorithm achieves $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{3/4}) + \mathcal{O}(C\log(T))$ regret against the best budget-balanced price distribution and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{3/4})$ worst-case regret against a per-round budget-balanced baseline.
h3bawejFSA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the technical improvement in combining stochastic and adversarial trade guarantees.
h3bawejFSA.main_concern: A remaining concern questions whether the inherited market model has been sufficiently vetted; the reported proof concern was resolved after rebuttal.

KM8kL0EvKY.one_liner: A transparency taxonomy evaluates whether language models disclose conflicts between verified prior knowledge and fabricated domain evidence.
KM8kL0EvKY.problem: Knowledge-conflict evaluations typically measure which source models follow instead of whether they communicate contradictions to users.
KM8kL0EvKY.method: The framework verifies models' prior knowledge, generates domain-grounded counterfactual evidence, and scores responses against an epistemic-transparency taxonomy. It varies evidence format, plausibility, and task stakes.
KM8kL0EvKY.key_idea: Introduce counterfactual domain evidence after verifying prior knowledge, then score explicit conflict disclosure across transparency dimensions.
KM8kL0EvKY.evidence: Experiments evaluate five frontier models across domains, document formats, and task stakes using generated knowledge conflicts.
KM8kL0EvKY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating conflict disclosure and the broader experimental setup with verified prior knowledge.
KM8kL0EvKY.main_concern: Reviewers question the reliability of LLM-based transparency and plausibility scoring without substantial independent human validation.

tCP83T8Ur6.one_liner: EGAR repairs web-agent targets by matching task requirements to structured evidence or locally extracted visual attributes.
tCP83T8Ur6.problem: Manipulated screenshots can redirect visual web agents to incorrect elements while preserving syntactically valid browser actions.
tCP83T8Ur6.method: EGAR separates task understanding, local evidence extraction, and target correction without training. It bypasses screenshots when non-visual evidence uniquely supports an action; otherwise, it checks local visual attributes against task requirements.
tCP83T8Ur6.key_idea: Select evidence by task requirements, bypass redundant screenshots, and revise target elements only after checking candidate attributes.
tCP83T8Ur6.evidence: Paired tasks and controlled interventions across three web-agent interfaces evaluate four visual attack types through generated actions and page-element binding.
tCP83T8Ur6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating actual target misselection and the systematic analysis of visual attacks across agent settings.
tCP83T8Ur6.main_concern: Reviewers find the component attribution and comparisons with simpler task-grounded verification methods insufficient.

Ij98HxaklA.one_liner: H2RB aligns hand-anchored representations and shares action latents with separate decoders to transfer human demonstrations into robot policies.
Ij98HxaklA.problem: Robot-pretrained vision-language-action policies struggle to learn new behaviors from human demonstrations because embodiment mismatches affect observations and actions.
Ij98HxaklA.method: H2RB co-trains pretrained VLA policies on unpaired human and robot demonstrations. Hand-geometry alignment connects representations, while an action tokenizer shares latent actions and uses embodiment-specific decoders.
Ij98HxaklA.key_idea: Align observations with hand geometry and encode actions in shared latents decoded separately for each embodiment.
Ij98HxaklA.evidence: Real-robot evaluations test object and skill transfer, including object-placement shifts and comparisons with co-training and shared-action baselines.
Ij98HxaklA.claimed_gains: H2RB improves object transfer performance from 8.0 to 51.8 and reaches a skill transfer score of 62.7.
Ij98HxaklA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize meaningful real-robot transfer gains from unpaired human demonstrations.
Ij98HxaklA.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization and reliability given a single robot platform, few objects and skills, and limited statistical evidence.

UlW35UavEm.one_liner: BoundSafe distills contrasting multimodal safety examples into external memory, refines it with feedback, and applies it during inference.
UlW35UavEm.problem: Subtle cross-modal differences can change safety judgments, but static instructions and case-level reflection do not explicitly capture those boundaries.
UlW35UavEm.method: BoundSafe builds boundary-aware textual memory from paired policy-labeled examples. Cross-validated refinement revises this memory before memory-guided inference without target-model parameter updates.
UlW35UavEm.key_idea: Distill contrasting safety examples into reusable boundary rules, refine them with labeled feedback, and consult them at inference.
UlW35UavEm.evidence: Experiments compare BoundSafe with baselines across multiple multimodal safety benchmarks and target models, evaluating unsafe refusals and benign responses.
UlW35UavEm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value explicit, inspectable safety distinctions learned without updating target-model parameters.
UlW35UavEm.main_concern: Reviewers find that the experiments do not adequately isolate contrastive memory construction and refinement under matched comparison conditions.

JSlXTU7wpk.one_liner: A fictitious-ally construction models risk-seeking play and links welfare effects to strategic substitutes versus complements.
JSlXTU7wpk.problem: Prior welfare gains from strategic risk aversion lack a general account of when risk-seeking behavior could also help.
JSlXTU7wpk.method: The paper replaces the fictitious adversary in strategic robustness with a fictitious ally in two-player quadratic games. It derives a substitutes-complements rule and a closed-form optimal robustness level.
JSlXTU7wpk.key_idea: Replace the fictitious adversary with an ally and use strategic interaction structure to characterize welfare changes under robustness.
JSlXTU7wpk.evidence: Theoretical results for two-player scalar quadratic games are illustrated through trading, shared-effort aggregation, and Bertrand price competition.
JSlXTU7wpk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the risk-seeking counterpart and its implications for equilibrium welfare interesting.
JSlXTU7wpk.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about the clarity and scope of the welfare theorem, including an apparent contradiction in its stated conditions.

1LXuGC53fB.one_liner: JACE mixes candidate tests with safe fallback episodes and uses anytime risk bounds to certify policy selection and stopping.
1LXuGC53fB.problem: Testing policies can itself cause safety violations, so selecting a safe policy also requires controlling risk during evidence collection.
1LXuGC53fB.method: JACE searches a fixed policy library with predetermined scores by mixing candidate tests with known-safe fallback episodes. Anytime risk bounds certify a recommendation and determine when sufficiently better safe candidates have been ruled out.
1LXuGC53fB.key_idea: Allocate risk-limited candidate tests through safe fallback mixing, and stop when anytime certificates eliminate relevant higher-scoring competitors.
1LXuGC53fB.evidence: Upper and worst-case lower sample-complexity bounds accompany policy-selection experiments including PointGoal1 and CarPush1.
1LXuGC53fB.claimed_gains: On PointGoal1, JACE completes in 37% fewer online episodes on average than matched safe round-robin allocation.
1LXuGC53fB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value jointly addressing safe evidence collection, policy certification, and verifiable completion.
1LXuGC53fB.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical utility guarantee because fixed preference scores and safety margins can exclude better safe policies.

Cju8nVSOa8.one_liner: Learns static per-layer, per-frequency binary gates choosing between RoPE and NoPE during Transformer pretraining
Cju8nVSOa8.problem: Hybrid RoPE–NoPE Transformers rely on manually prescribed rotary fractions or layer schedules rather than learning which layers and frequencies benefit from explicit positional encoding.
Cju8nVSOa8.method: Mixture of Position Embeddings (MoPE) jointly trains Transformer weights alongside binary gates that select either rotary position embedding (RoPE) or identity (NoPE) for each layer and frequency channel. Once trained, the binary gates freeze into a static positional architecture with no input-dependent routing overhead during inference or context extension.
Cju8nVSOa8.key_idea: Jointly optimize per-layer, per-frequency binary gates selecting between RoPE rotations and NoPE identity during pretraining, then freeze the learned mask for zero-overhead inference.
Cju8nVSOa8.evidence: Evaluated on language models from 70M to 1B parameters pretrained at 4K context and extended to 64K–256K (including with YaRN) on short-context benchmarks, PG19 perplexity, and Needle-in-a-Haystack retrieval.
Cju8nVSOa8.claimed_gains: After 4K pretraining and context extension to 64K, the 410M and 1B models achieve 94.9% and 98.8% NIAH accuracy at 128K, and the 410M model combined with YaRN achieves 99.1% NIAH accuracy at 256K.
Cju8nVSOa8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find learning a static binary RoPE and NoPE mask across layers and frequencies simple, practical, free of inference overhead, and effective on NIAH retrieval across model scales.
Cju8nVSOa8.main_concern: Experiments omit Full NoPE and random-mask baselines needed to isolate the learned mask's benefit, and long-context evaluation is limited mainly to perplexity and single-needle NIAH rather than complex reasoning.

2Eak0Awrj9.one_liner: Agentic multimodal clinical diagnosis framework combining uncertainty-guided cross-image zoom-and-select routing with multi-horizon RL credit assignment
2Eak0Awrj9.problem: Passive single-pass multimodal models struggle to locate subtle findings and align distributed visual evidence across multiple heterogeneous clinical images.
2Eak0Awrj9.method: MedInSight trains a multimodal agent via supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to iteratively select and zoom into regions across medical image sets. Cross-image Evidence Routing (CER) prioritizes inspection using per-image predictive and cross-image spatial uncertainty, while Cross-horizon Credit Assignment (CCA) weights RL policy updates by combining short-horizon action confidence deltas with long-horizon outcome direction.
2Eak0Awrj9.key_idea: Route active cross-image selection and region zoom-in via grounding and spatial uncertainty, and optimize multi-step inspection with RL credit combining action-level confidence changes and trajectory-level outcomes.
2Eak0Awrj9.evidence: Evaluated across multi-image clinical diagnosis benchmarks against open-source and proprietary multimodal models, with uncertainty, credit-assignment, and full-image-access ablations.
2Eak0Awrj9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling multi-image clinical diagnosis as an active, traceable cross-image inspection loop with fine-grained RL credit assignment aligns well with clinical workflows and improves over its open-source backbone.
2Eak0Awrj9.main_concern: Uncertainty-guided routing is never directly evaluated for true lesion localization versus image noise, CCA relies on uncalibrated self-reported confidences with small-sample controls, and proprietary frontier models outperform the reported scores.

P89DxUlEiN.one_liner: Post-generation agentic ECG report verifier combining clinical-criteria RAG, waveform measurement tools, and memory-gated selective editing
P89DxUlEiN.problem: Single-pass multimodal LLMs generate ECG reports containing unverified or waveform-inconsistent diagnostic claims without revisiting the underlying signal against clinical criteria.
P89DxUlEiN.method: ECG-RePAIR audits an initial generated ECG report at test time by retrieving diagnostic criteria via RAG, invoking signal-processing tools to extract lead-specific waveform measurements into structured Evidence Cards, and querying a learned repair advantage memory to decide whether to apply or abstain from local report edits.
P89DxUlEiN.key_idea: Verify draft ECG report claims against clinical criteria retrieved via RAG and quantitative waveform tool measurements, then gate local edits using a learned repair-advantage memory.
P89DxUlEiN.evidence: Evaluated across base MLLMs and evaluators on ECG diagnostic accuracy and report-quality benchmarks with tool and memory ablations and clinical expert assessment.
P89DxUlEiN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clinically grounded, auditable workflow that separates criteria lookup, quantitative waveform verification, and selective local report editing.
P89DxUlEiN.main_concern: Fitting the repair advantage memory and thresholds via cross-validation on folds of the benchmark test set introduces cohort-specific supervision without independent held-out validation or simple rule-based baselines.

kTKsrreGcy.one_liner: Controlled fictional-entity benchmark probing whether image-generation training injects text-accessible knowledge into unified multimodal models, paired with interleaved alignment
kTKsrreGcy.problem: It remains unclear whether knowledge taught to unified multimodal models exclusively through text-to-image generation targets becomes accessible to their text-only question-answering pathway.
kTKsrreGcy.method: Knowledge Transfer Probing (KTP) fine-tunes unified multimodal models on image-generation targets depicting fictional entities across seven attribute categories, then probes zero-shot text-only QA recall. To bridge observed visual-to-text recall gaps, the authors introduce Textual Alignment and Interleaved Image-Text Alignment on a subset of entities to transfer QA accessibility to held-out visually learned entities.
kTKsrreGcy.key_idea: Inject synthetic fictional entity attributes solely via image-generation supervision to measure text-only QA recall, then bridge cross-modal recall gaps using interleaved image-text alignment on anchor entities.
kTKsrreGcy.evidence: Evaluated across seven visual knowledge categories on three unified multimodal models (BAGEL, GLM-Omni, and SenseNova-U1) with alignment and loss-masking ablations.
kTKsrreGcy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled KTP experimental design using isolated fictional entities to cleanly measure visual-generation-to-text knowledge transfer across unified multimodal models.
kTKsrreGcy.main_concern: Direct unaligned transfer is near or below random guessing on two of three models, conceptual differentiation from prior Modal Aphasia work is thin, and interleaved alignment ablations do not control for supervision density.

mAdpRnGpPp.one_liner: Standardized 14-organ cell-matched dataset and benchmark evaluating spot-supervised single-cell spatial transcriptomics prediction from histopathology images
mAdpRnGpPp.problem: Weakly supervised virtual spatial transcriptomics—predicting single-cell gene expression from histopathology images trained only on coarse spot-level data—lacks a standardized cell-matched dataset and evaluation suite.
mAdpRnGpPp.method: CellHIST curates and aligns segmented histopathology nuclei to single-cell measurements across 169 public samples spanning 14 organs (around 36 million cells and 1 million patches). CellHIST-Bench compares weakly supervised, super-resolution, and fully supervised paradigms under matched patient splits across accuracy, data scaling, cell-shuffling specificity, and biological utility.
mAdpRnGpPp.key_idea: Register histopathology cell nuclei to single-cell transcriptomes and pool them into synthetic spots on identical patient splits to benchmark weakly supervised single-cell expression inference.
mAdpRnGpPp.evidence: Benchmarks weakly supervised, fully supervised, and super-resolution baselines across 169 curated samples from 14 organs (around 36 million cells and 1 million image patches) with scaling and cell-permutation specificity tests.
mAdpRnGpPp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the nuclei-to-cell registration across 169 samples and the controlled comparison between pooled spot-level and single-cell supervision on shared patient splits.
mAdpRnGpPp.main_concern: Per-organ single-cell test cohorts contain very few independent slides (such as two ovary and three skin samples), most samples derive from HEST-1K, and within-type cell-shuffling controls are incomplete.

78rFfNcePc.one_liner: One-step flow-based virtual try-on removing classifier-free guidance and combining garment-preservation, self-consistency, and adversarial distillation losses
78rFfNcePc.problem: Flow- and diffusion-based virtual try-on models inherit curved unconditional trajectories and classifier-free guidance from pretrained image generators, requiring slow multi-step sampling despite strong garment-person conditioning.
78rFfNcePc.method: DirectTryOn fine-tunes a flow-based virtual try-on model using pure conditional transport (eliminating unconditional dropout and CFG), a garment preservation loss, and a trajectory self-consistency loss, followed by one-step adversarial distillation. This pipeline produces try-on images in a single neural function evaluation.
78rFfNcePc.key_idea: Drop unconditional training and classifier-free guidance in conditional flow matching while adding self-consistency, garment-preservation, and adversarial one-step distillation losses for single-step virtual try-on.
78rFfNcePc.evidence: Evaluated at 1 NFE on VITON-HD and DressCode against 4-step and 30-step diffusion and flow try-on models and controlled DMD and LADD distillation baselines.
78rFfNcePc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method delivers fast single-step virtual try-on with competitive FID and KID on VITON-HD and DressCode, supported by useful CFG and distillation controls.
78rFfNcePc.main_concern: Trajectory curvature is never directly measured—sharpness relies heavily on adversarial distillation rather than conditional path straightness—and fine-grained garment fidelity (logos, text, textures) lacks unmasked quantitative metrics.

5K3XPz8FAi.one_liner: Gated recurrent neural network embedding simplicial operators inside memory gates for higher-order spatiotemporal forecasting
5K3XPz8FAi.problem: Graph recurrent architectures model only pairwise node-edge interactions, ignoring higher-order group dynamics across nodes, edges, and triangles in spatiotemporal networks.
5K3XPz8FAi.method: Simplicial Topological Recurrent Models (STORM) and a parameter-reduced variant (LightSTORM) embed simplicial operators directly inside recurrent gating updates so node, edge, and higher-order signals co-evolve over time. The authors also derive permutation equivariance, finite-horizon topology-perturbation stability, and temporal Rademacher generalization bounds.
5K3XPz8FAi.key_idea: Replace pairwise graph operations inside recurrent memory gates with simplicial complex operators that jointly evolve node, edge, and triangle hidden states across time.
5K3XPz8FAi.evidence: Supported by equivariance, perturbation-stability, and Rademacher generalization proofs, plus long-horizon spatiotemporal forecasting experiments on traffic (PeMS-D4, PeMS-D8) and hydraulic water network datasets.
5K3XPz8FAi.claimed_gains: Improves over the best evaluated baselines by up to 50% at long horizons on traffic and hydraulic datasets, with LightSTORM using up to roughly two orders of magnitude fewer parameters.
5K3XPz8FAi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that embedding higher-order simplicial operators into gated recurrent architectures is well formulated and performs well at long forecasting horizons, including a compact LightSTORM variant.
5K3XPz8FAi.main_concern: Traffic benchmarks synthesize higher-order edge and triangle signals merely by averaging node sensors (while true edge-measured hydraulic gains are smaller), baseline coverage is narrow, and gated simplicial filtering closely extends graph-RNN designs.

1CisPYFRcZ.one_liner: Decoupled short- and long-horizon representations and multi-start bootstrapping improve off-policy representation and value learning.
1CisPYFRcZ.problem: Fixed-horizon prediction limits reinforcement learning across environments with different temporal characteristics.
1CisPYFRcZ.method: SHARV combines independently learned short- and long-horizon representations for policy and value learning. Multi-Start Bootstrapping supervises value targets from multiple starting points to control internal TD residual components not fixed by first-start target error.
1CisPYFRcZ.key_idea: Separate horizon-specific representations and multi-start TD supervision exploit complementary temporal signals within off-policy learning.
1CisPYFRcZ.evidence: Evaluation covers 34 continuous-control tasks in four benchmark suites with proprioceptive and visual observations, ten seeds, strong baselines, component ablations, and TD-residual analyses.
1CisPYFRcZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that SHARV is clearly presented and supported by broad benchmark results, uncertainty estimates, and component ablations.
1CisPYFRcZ.main_concern: Reviewers most often find that ablations do not fully isolate DDR and MSB from architectural, capacity, and supervision changes.

C6ORB9Fgv2.one_liner: Phase-aware expert rerouting balances prefill token loads and decode active-expert counts across MoE ranks.
C6ORB9Fgv2.problem: Expert-parallel MoE inference waits for the busiest rank, with peak tokens limiting prefill and active experts limiting decode.
C6ORB9Fgv2.method: RankCast preserves each token's Top-p experts and selects the remaining experts from Top-L candidates. Prefill uses rank prices to steer assignments, while decode closes experts on busy ranks; implementations in SGLang and DeepEP overlap balancing with execution.
C6ORB9Fgv2.key_idea: A protected expert prefix and wider candidate set permit phase-specific rerouting by rank pricing during prefill and expert closure during decode.
C6ORB9Fgv2.evidence: End-to-end evaluations in SGLang and DeepEP use two large production MoE models and measure phase-specific load balancing, overhead, and accuracy effects.
C6ORB9Fgv2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the phase-aware formulation is clear and that the overlapped, CUDA-compatible system implementation is strong.
C6ORB9Fgv2.main_concern: Reviewers most often find validation of cross-layer routing prediction insufficient for the protected experts and balancing decisions that depend on it.

oki4NIsjDJ.one_liner: Measurement-map geometry characterizes conservation laws and active training dimensions in parameterized quantum circuits.
oki4NIsjDJ.problem: The trainable unitary, measurement observable, and circuit architecture jointly determine which parameter directions remain visible to optimization.
oki4NIsjDJ.method: The paper develops a geometric theory of local smooth data-independent conservation laws and distinguishes parametrization redundancy from unitary motions invisible to readout. It derives complete nullspace-based characterizations for Basic Entangler circuits and completeness results for specified two-layer noncommuting architectures.
oki4NIsjDJ.key_idea: Measurement-map differential geometry separates redundant parameters from readout-invisible unitary motions and characterizes conserved quantities through Lie-closure rank.
oki4NIsjDJ.evidence: Theoretical results characterize Basic Entangler circuits at arbitrary width and depth and establish completeness for specified Strongly Entangling and Clifford-entangler circuits under explicit conditions.
oki4NIsjDJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the geometric framework is timely and valuable, with clearly formulated mathematical results and apparently correct proofs.
oki4NIsjDJ.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the practical scope and computational difficulty of extending the characterization to general variational quantum circuits.

rEmL4edMwn.one_liner: Correlated joint beliefs and Bayesian Nash equilibria coordinate model-merging contributions under incomplete information.
rEmL4edMwn.problem: Task-specific models cannot directly observe one another's private characteristics, making contribution coordination during merging uncertain.
rEmL4edMwn.method: BeliefMerge formulates merging as a Bayesian game with correlated joint beliefs over unobserved model characteristics. Bayesian Nash Equilibrium coordinates interdependent contributions, with sufficient conditions for uniqueness and convergence of exact best-response updates.
rEmL4edMwn.key_idea: Correlated beliefs over private model characteristics determine equilibrium contribution strategies for uncertainty-aware model merging.
rEmL4edMwn.evidence: Experiments cover nine CLIP configurations and eight GLUE tasks, with comparisons against existing merging methods and component ablations.
rEmL4edMwn.claimed_gains: BeliefMerge achieves the best performance on all nine CLIP configurations and five of eight GLUE tasks.
rEmL4edMwn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the Bayesian-game formulation is principled and well motivated and that empirical results are competitive across many benchmarks.
rEmL4edMwn.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether the game-theoretic formulation and equilibrium theory justify or explain the empirical gains.

5rPCwFoPyP.one_liner: A dynamic task-execution graph selects step-relevant memory and writes observations back for long-horizon agents.
5rPCwFoPyP.problem: Fragmented growing memories can obscure task progress, earlier goals, and constraints during long-horizon agent execution.
5rPCwFoPyP.method: TaskGraph represents goals, stages, steps, and atomic constraint, evidence, and variable records in a hierarchical graph with inclusion, mainline, and dependency relations. Each step receives graph-selected historical dependencies, and observed results update the shared execution-memory structure.
5rPCwFoPyP.key_idea: Task progress and memory share a hierarchical dependency graph used for both step-specific context construction and state updates.
5rPCwFoPyP.evidence: Experiments include StableToolBench and longer-memory evaluations, with component ablations that remove step-anchored context and structured records.
5rPCwFoPyP.claimed_gains: On StableToolBench, TaskGraph improves macro-average final answer correctness by 14.97 percentage points.
5rPCwFoPyP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that binding memory roles to task progress is coherent and well motivated, with ablations supporting the graph formulation.
5rPCwFoPyP.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the headline comparison confounded by additional model calls and computation without matched cost accounting.

JL4v0U5HkB.one_liner: Residual latent flow generates all-atom GPCR–ligand trajectories from dimension-preserving, atom-anchored representations.
JL4v0U5HkB.problem: Conventional all-atom molecular-dynamics simulation of ligand-bound GPCR conformational transitions is computationally prohibitive.
JL4v0U5HkB.method: GPCRLMD uses an Atom-Anchored Thermal Variational Autoencoder with physics-informed constraints to map complexes into a regularized dimension-preserving latent space. Residual Latent Flow samples relative-displacement trajectories anchored to the initial structure before decoding atomic coordinates.
JL4v0U5HkB.key_idea: Residual latent dynamics anchored to the initial atomic structure decouple static molecular topology from time-varying geometric fluctuations.
JL4v0U5HkB.evidence: Evaluation covers held-out receptors and ligands, multiple systems and horizons, structural distributions, ensemble observables, and ligand-receptor interactions against retrained baselines.
JL4v0U5HkB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that joint all-atom receptor-ligand modeling is relevant and supported by substantial held-out structural evaluation and controlled ablations.
JL4v0U5HkB.main_concern: Reviewers agree that ensemble-distribution metrics do not establish correct transition rates, temporal correlations, or kinetic ordering.

sd4mb3HD8X.one_liner: Complexity, expressivity, and generalization analyses establish theoretical capabilities and limits of discrete prompts.
sd4mb3HD8X.problem: The theory of practical hard or discrete prompting remains much less developed than that of soft prompting.
sd4mb3HD8X.method: The paper proves NP-completeness for hard-prompt existence and NP-hardness for optimal-prompt search, then analyzes expressivity limits of short and long prompts and an exception for linear prompts. It also derives a generalization bound relating finite-task performance, prompt length, and task size.
sd4mb3HD8X.key_idea: Separate complexity, expressivity, and generalization arguments characterize when discrete prompts can represent and learn task-specific transformer behavior.
sd4mb3HD8X.evidence: The support consists of theoretical reductions and proofs covering prompt existence, optimization, short- and long-prompt limitations, prompt-dominating answers, and finite-task generalization.
sd4mb3HD8X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the questions are important and that the paper offers a clear, comprehensive theoretical treatment of hard prompting.
sd4mb3HD8X.main_concern: The central theoretical claims are weakened by identified gaps and inconsistencies in key proofs.

PwlYzqIzOb.one_liner: Hard-negative-trained bundled classifiers activate skill backdoors only for conjunctions of schema-valid parameter assignments.
PwlYzqIzOb.problem: Source review of installable agent skills can miss activation conditions encoded in bundled model weights.
PwlYzqIzOb.method: BadSkill trains a bundled classifier using full-trigger positives and independently generated near-trigger hard negatives for an attacker-chosen parameter conjunction. A source-visible router executes a harmless canary on activation while returning the advertised task result in either branch.
PwlYzqIzOb.key_idea: Near-trigger hard negatives teach bundled weights an approximate conjunctive activation boundary while source-visible routing preserves normal task outputs.
PwlYzqIzOb.evidence: Evaluation covers eight target skills, five non-trigger controls, eight models, four integration settings, and 32 model-integration cells.
PwlYzqIzOb.claimed_gains: BadSkill attains 97.2% mean canary-delivery ASR, while 97.5% of non-triggered runs return a visible result, at most 4.5 points below clean artifacts.
PwlYzqIzOb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that model-in-skill poisoning exposes a relevant supply-chain blind spot and is evaluated across multiple skills, models, and integrations.
PwlYzqIzOb.main_concern: The defense evaluation does not adequately test realistic code inspection, skill-level screening, or blind discovery of unknown trigger templates.

F0J9eQ9C87.one_liner: Uses Mixture-of-Depths Attention in latent world models so high-level queries selectively retrieve fine spatial details from early encoder layers.
F0J9eQ9C87.problem: Latent world models operating only on final-depth encoder features lose fine-grained spatial and geometric details needed for precise visuomotor control.
F0J9eQ9C87.method: ReWorldModel (ReWM) integrates Mixture-of-Depths Attention (MoDA) into a modernized Transformer encoder so top-level latent queries selectively attend to earlier encoder layers, preserving control-relevant details alongside latent predictability.
F0J9eQ9C87.key_idea: Applies Mixture-of-Depths Attention to let high-level latent world-model queries selectively retrieve features from earlier encoder depths.
F0J9eQ9C87.evidence: Evaluated on five visuomotor control tasks (including PushT, Reacher, TwoRoom) against LeWM across three seeds with layer-wise probing and component ablations.
F0J9eQ9C87.claimed_gains: Achieves 100% success on four of five tasks and 99.0% mean success on PushT, reaching 95% on PushT with 5x fewer processed sequences than LeWM, and improves Reacher success by 74.4 percentage points at 8 updates (95% with 8x fewer updates on Reacher and TwoRoom).
F0J9eQ9C87.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that ReWM is clearly written, well-motivated, and demonstrates strong early-control sample efficiency with informative ablations.
F0J9eQ9C87.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty (reusing MoDA inside LeWM), missing world-model baselines like PLDM and DINO-WM, and no planning results.

jDfYdcQDSj.one_liner: Evicts older search observations from the KV cache and caps redundant search loops in deep research agents without retraining.
jDfYdcQDSj.problem: Deep research agents accumulate large KV caches from search observations, while naive context compression triggers repeated search loops that add inference rounds.
jDfYdcQDSj.method: SearchTrimmer applies Search-Selective KV Eviction (retaining reasoning and browse observations while keeping only the k most recent search observations) and Loop Gating (capping cumulative non-restoring repeat searches while exempting Restores).
jDfYdcQDSj.key_idea: Retains only the k most recent search observations in the KV cache and caps redundant repeat-search loops by distinguishing Restores from Loops.
jDfYdcQDSj.evidence: Evaluated on WebExplorer-8B and WebSailor-32B across three benchmarks (WebWalkerQA, xbench-DeepSearch, GAIA) on vLLM and SGLang.
jDfYdcQDSj.claimed_gains: Reduces average KV-cache usage by 44–56% on WebExplorer-8B and 32–36% on WebSailor-32B, with maximum KV-cache reductions of 73–83% and 28–48%.
jDfYdcQDSj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that SearchTrimmer is grounded in a clear trajectory analysis, runs training-free without attention scores, and reduces KV-cache memory competitively.
jDfYdcQDSj.main_concern: Reviewers note that the method relies on hand-crafted per-agent heuristics (such as tuned k and lexical query overlap) that may not generalize, and lacks prompt-masking and loop-gating-only controls.

5vsweezVPF.one_liner: Extends pretrained RGB diffusion/flow generators to RGBA using LoRA, a unidirectional alpha decoder branch, and Endpoint-Aware Alpha Loss.
5vsweezVPF.problem: Training RGBA-specific VAEs adds a separate reconstruction stage and can alter the pretrained RGB decoding capability.
5vsweezVPF.method: AlphaAnything freezes the pretrained RGB VAE, attaches a trainable alpha branch to the decoder with unidirectional RGB-to-alpha feature sharing, adapts the generative transformer with LoRA, and trains with Endpoint-Aware Alpha Loss (EA Loss) derived from compositing weights.
5vsweezVPF.key_idea: Shares features unidirectionally from a frozen RGB VAE decoder to an attached alpha branch while adapting the transformer with LoRA under an endpoint-aware compositing loss.
5vsweezVPF.evidence: Evaluated on text-to-RGBA and image-to-RGBA generation and extraction across multiple pretrained RGB backbones with ablations on gradient flow and loss design.
5vsweezVPF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that preserving exact fixed-latent RGB decoding via unidirectional feature sharing while avoiding RGBA VAE pretraining is practical and well-validated.
5vsweezVPF.main_concern: Reviewers note missing evaluations of RGB-only task retention after RGBA adaptation, unisolated components within EA Loss, and missing comparison to dual-latent frozen-VAE concatenation.

sS9rVZOFyx.one_liner: Applies post-hoc Dependency-Sparsity Regularization to linearly identified JEPA representations to recover individual world latents up to signed permutation.
sS9rVZOFyx.problem: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) identify latent states only up to an arbitrary linear transformation, leaving individual world factors mixed.
sS9rVZOFyx.method: DSReg assumes Structural Diversity across observation dependency footprints and optimizes a post-hoc sparsity regularizer over an orthogonal rotation of a frozen linearly identified representation (e.g., LeJEPA) without a global decoder or labels.
sS9rVZOFyx.key_idea: Selects an orthogonal rotation of a frozen linearly identified representation by minimizing the sparsity of local observation-to-latent dependency footprints.
sS9rVZOFyx.evidence: Theoretical identifiability proofs (Theorems 2–3) and controlled empirical evaluations across high-dimensional benchmarks, multiple seeds, and failure regimes.
sS9rVZOFyx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that isolating coordinate recovery post-hoc from subspace learning is a clean, well-formalized contribution with thorough controlled experiments.
sS9rVZOFyx.main_concern: Reviewers point out a gap between the theoretical guarantees (exact/thresholded population support) and the implemented anchor-averaged l1 ridge-Jacobian surrogate, and question the 'without reconstruction' framing.

HMD0xk4A6J.one_liner: Combines state-adaptive latent safety steering on masked tokens with early-block detection and targeted remasking for diffusion language models.
HMD0xk4A6J.problem: Harmful content in diffusion language models can emerge at arbitrary positions during iterative denoising, where fixed steering or aggressive remasking degrades quality.
HMD0xk4A6J.method: The inference-time defense computes a gating direction to modulate steering strength from the current denoising state, steers masked positions, and uses a lightweight detector after the first generation block to trigger targeted remasking of generated and prompt tokens.
HMD0xk4A6J.key_idea: Pairs continuous state-gated activation steering on masked positions with an early-block harmfulness detector that triggers targeted remasking.
HMD0xk4A6J.evidence: Evaluated on LLaDA and Dream diffusion language models across three safety benchmarks.
HMD0xk4A6J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that this training-free, plug-in defense is well-motivated for diffusion language models and balances safety with capability preservation.
HMD0xk4A6J.main_concern: Reviewers note missing baselines (such as ReFuse and fixed/scheduled steering), unclear justification for remasking prompt tokens (a distribution shift), and reliance on linear separability.

nKFgH8T9a8.one_liner: Represents compressed visual tokens as composable states tracking original positions, contribution weights, and selection metadata for VLM attention.
nKFgH8T9a8.problem: Existing visual token compression methods discard how much visual evidence each retained token represents and where it originated, causing compounding errors under progressive layer-wise compression.
nKFgH8T9a8.method: CoViST constructs a composable visual state via coverage-guided selection and conservation-based contribution composition, injecting contribution weights and original positions into decoder attention so the state remains closed under repeated reductions.
nKFgH8T9a8.key_idea: Maintains a reduction-closed visual state of features, original positions, and conserved contribution weights integrated directly into decoder attention.
nKFgH8T9a8.evidence: Evaluated on seven LLaVA-1.5-7B benchmarks and multiple VLM backbones under fixed prefill and progressive decoder compression budgets.
nKFgH8T9a8.claimed_gains: On seven LLaVA-1.5-7B benchmarks, CoViST-Fixed retains 99.9% and 99.5% of uncompressed performance (exact third budget truncated in abstract).
nKFgH8T9a8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that making compressed visual states closed under successive reductions is a clean conceptual fix with thorough component ablations.
nKFgH8T9a8.main_concern: Reviewers point out that competitor numbers are taken from prior papers under different full-model references and harnesses, making CoViST's small margins over VisionTrim unreliable.

MiWymoRYwg.one_liner: Composes layer-wise ViT prompts per task and uses a Hebbian co-selection history to freeze hubs and orthogonally re-initialize unused prompts.
MiWymoRYwg.problem: Prompt-based continual learning faces a trade-off between task-specific prompt allocation (no reuse, growing pool) and shared prompts (catastrophic interference).
MiWymoRYwg.method: Learning to Compose (L2C) selects compositions of prompts across ViT layers and maintains a gradient-free Hebbian transition history (via Oja's rule) of co-selected prompts to stabilize active pathways, freeze hubs, and orthogonally re-initialize rarely used prompts.
MiWymoRYwg.key_idea: Accumulates a Hebbian co-selection matrix across adjacent ViT layers to freeze frequently composed prompt hubs and re-initialize underused prompts orthogonally.
MiWymoRYwg.evidence: Evaluated on three continual learning benchmarks (5 to 40 tasks, five class-order seeds) against ten baselines.
MiWymoRYwg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting protection from tasks to composed prompts is conceptually clear and achieves strong average incremental accuracy and low forgetting across nine settings.
MiWymoRYwg.main_concern: Reviewers note that the benefit of cross-stage Hebbian pathways is not isolated from simple per-prompt usage counts, some recent prompt baselines (e.g., ConvPrompt, LEAPGen, NorGA) and standard deviations are missing, and classifier growth qualifies parameter efficiency.

RyzMiPANe6.one_liner: Fuses pretrained visual priors with lightweight temporal representations via adaptive gating for time-series anomaly detection.
RyzMiPANe6.problem: Time-series anomaly detection methods using pretrained visual models capture global structure but often miss fine-grained temporal dynamics and domain-specific sequential dependencies.
RyzMiPANe6.method: TVF-AD freezes a pretrained visual backbone and trains lightweight temporal encoding and adaptive fusion modules to combine cross-modal visual priors with sequential representations.
RyzMiPANe6.key_idea: Adapts frozen pretrained visual priors to multivariate time-series anomaly detection by fusing them with lightweight learned temporal encoders.
RyzMiPANe6.evidence: Evaluated on univariate and multivariate TSB-AD benchmarks (TSB-AD-U and TSB-AD-M) across five metrics with ablations on grouping, fusion, and post-processing.
RyzMiPANe6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that TVF-AD achieves strong aggregate results on TSB-AD benchmarks with extensive ablation studies.
RyzMiPANe6.main_concern: The geometry alignment objective admits a trivial visual-only solution, and post-processing controls and random-vs-pretrained encoder ablations are incomplete.

NwtGawlQ6b.one_liner: Internalizes domain documents into a dedicated trained MEMORY model queried at inference time by an executive LLM.
NwtGawlQ6b.problem: Frozen LLMs lack domain-specific or up-to-date knowledge, while standard fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting and RAG remains vulnerable to retrieval distractors.
NwtGawlQ6b.method: MeMo synthesizes and trains document knowledge into a separate MEMORY model, which any black-box or open-weight EXECUTIVE LLM queries at inference time to retrieve and reason over relevant knowledge.
NwtGawlQ6b.key_idea: Offloads domain knowledge into a separate trained MEMORY model queried by an unmodified executive LLM at inference time.
NwtGawlQ6b.evidence: Evaluated across three benchmarks including MuSiQue and NarrativeQA using Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct and Gemini-3-Flash against parametric, latent, and retrieval baselines.
NwtGawlQ6b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that MeMo offers a clean, plug-and-play modular design that works across closed- and open-weight executive LLMs.
NwtGawlQ6b.main_concern: The core idea is incremental, rankings depend heavily on the executive LLM choice, and Step 5 question-derived document grouping may leak evaluation structure.

a7sisyAuRA.one_liner: Recovers soft-error-corrupted DNN representations at the post-backbone interface using range projection and input-conditioned multi-scale context.
a7sisyAuRA.problem: Hardware soft errors corrupt DNN weights or activations, while existing mitigations either require backbone retraining or leave residual errors after terminal range projection.
a7sisyAuRA.method: ReAnchor keeps the backbone and task head frozen, applies a fixed range projection to the terminal backbone feature, and fuses it with sample-aligned multi-scale context extracted from the input to recover task-relevant representations.
a7sisyAuRA.key_idea: Combines fixed terminal range projection with input-conditioned multi-scale context in a post-trained module while keeping the backbone and head frozen.
a7sisyAuRA.evidence: Evaluated across three datasets (primarily CIFAR-10) and three model architectures under injected bit-flip fault rates up to 10^-5, with ablations and overhead measurements.
a7sisyAuRA.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest mean top-1 accuracy in all nine dataset-backbone settings at a 10^-5 fault rate.
a7sisyAuRA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that operating with a frozen backbone and head without fault-location knowledge addresses a practical deployment constraint.
a7sisyAuRA.main_concern: Evaluation relies heavily on small datasets like CIFAR-10 rather than ImageNet or large models, and high-fault accuracy may rely mostly on the input bypass pathway.

gwKbYJF6ui.one_liner: Concentrates predictive information into leading latent coordinates of a JEPA world model via learned prefix selection and MixSIGReg.
gwKbYJF6ui.problem: Standard anti-collapse regularizers in JEPA world models spread variance across all latent coordinates without ordering them by predictive importance for compact planning.
gwKbYJF6ui.method: ALeWM learns a sequence-conditioned distribution over prefix lengths, trains the predictor to reconstruct full next embeddings from masked prefixes, and applies MixSIGReg to regularize masked embeddings toward a prior-weighted mixture.
gwKbYJF6ui.key_idea: Trains a JEPA predictor from sampled prefix lengths regularized by MixSIGReg so predictive information concentrates in early latent coordinates.
gwKbYJF6ui.evidence: Evaluated on a controlled dynamical system and four goal-conditioned visual control tasks across three backbone sizes against tuned fixed-width LeWM.
gwKbYJF6ui.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that concentrating predictive information into short prefixes improves planning success over fixed-width LeWM and that fixing LeWM's data split is valuable.
gwKbYJF6ui.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate the benefit of input-dependent capacity selection over a fixed global distribution, and comparisons omit relevant baselines like LpWM and DINO-WM.

Nf4txiO1l3.one_liner: Groups MARL agents to share policy backbones with group-wise sequential updates and private agent-specific action-replacement modules.
Nf4txiO1l3.problem: MAPPO's full parameter sharing enforces homogeneous policies, whereas HAPPO's per-agent sequential updates incur high parameter counts and long update chains.
Nf4txiO1l3.method: GHAPPO extends multi-agent advantage decomposition to agent groups that share a backbone and update sequentially by group, while adding lightweight agent-specific action-replacement modules for intra-group heterogeneity.
Nf4txiO1l3.key_idea: Balances parameter sharing and sequential updates by grouping agents with shared backbones and adding lightweight agent-specific action-replacement modules.
Nf4txiO1l3.evidence: Analyzes grouping granularity theoretically under a bounded-ratio assumption and evaluates on MARL benchmarks (including 3s5z and 8m vs 9m).
Nf4txiO1l3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that balancing MAPPO's parameter sharing and HAPPO's sequential updates via grouping and action replacement is clearly motivated.
Nf4txiO1l3.main_concern: End-to-end training speedups over HAPPO are not achieved, action replacement is not isolated from extra parameters, and the theoretical proxy objective relies on strong assumptions.

mfghYpy0ZN.one_liner: Adds a splat-region cross-attention bias to align learnable Gaussian tokens with their projected 2D image patches.
mfghYpy0ZN.problem: In token-based feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting, 31.2% of tokens attend outside the 2D image regions where their predicted Gaussians project.
mfghYpy0ZN.method: Gaussian Splat Attention Bias (GSAB) performs an intermediate decoding of existing Gaussian tokens to locate their 2D splat regions and adds an attention bias restricting cross-attention to patches inside those regions. It integrates into token-based feed-forward models without extra forward passes.
mfghYpy0ZN.key_idea: Intermediate token decoding locates each Gaussian's 2D splat region and adds a cross-attention bias to aggregate features from within that projection.
mfghYpy0ZN.evidence: Experiments evaluate GSAB on a 2K-Gaussian pose-free model (C3G) and a 262K-Gaussian posed model (TokenGS), plus misalignment diagnostics and ablations.
mfghYpy0ZN.claimed_gains: Improves PSNR by up to 0.71 dB on the pose-free model (and 0.46-0.80 dB over matched TokenGS reproductions).
mfghYpy0ZN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that token-splat misalignment is an intuitive, well-diagnosed observation and that GSAB is a minimal intervention that reduces misalignment.
mfghYpy0ZN.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains over published TokenGS checkpoints are tiny because the authors' reproductions underperform, and ablations do not isolate splat geometry from generic spatial priors.

P5SFMmkU5Q.one_liner: Introduces MainLogic, a benchmark of matched claim-evidence interventions testing whether long-context LLMs update judgments from read evidence.
P5SFMmkU5Q.problem: High accuracy on natural scientific claims does not show whether long-context LLMs rely on supplied documents or on memorized priors.
P5SFMmkU5Q.method: The authors construct MainLogic from human-verified scientific citations, creating matched claim families that pair opposing claims with original, reversed, and insufficient evidence plus irrelevant-text deletion controls, and evaluate ten frontier LLMs.
P5SFMmkU5Q.key_idea: Testing matched families of original, reversed, and insufficient evidence variations isolates evidence-grounded reasoning from parametric priors and answer bias.
P5SFMmkU5Q.evidence: Evaluations of ten frontier LLMs on MainLogic claim families and prior-elicitation controls.
P5SFMmkU5Q.claimed_gains: Models exceeding 90% accuracy on original claims solve at most 32.4% of complete evidence-intervention families, and prior-conflicting evidence drops accuracy by 6-51 points.
P5SFMmkU5Q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the matched-family intervention design for rigorously separating evidence-grounded reasoning from claim familiarity and prior bias.
P5SFMmkU5Q.main_concern: Reviewers question label validity in the automatically edited counterfactual and insufficient-evidence variants, noting the small human audit (48 rows from 40 of 108 anchors) found defects in 6 groups.

RT78MFtfKQ.one_liner: Decouples AI scientist evaluation into reference-conditioned idea reconstruction, code implementation, and controlled reporting over 753 aligned paper quadruplets.
RT78MFtfKQ.problem: Existing AI scientist benchmarks focus on isolated tasks or final manuscripts, leaving the fidelity of intermediate scientific artifacts unexamined.
RT78MFtfKQ.method: AIS-Bench constructs 753 aligned quadruplets of context, idea, executable code, and paper from 3,174 ML papers, scoring idea reconstruction, code implementation, and controlled reporting independently with phase-specific metrics.
RT78MFtfKQ.key_idea: Supplying reference inputs at each downstream phase isolates idea, implementation, and reporting failures without upstream error propagation.
RT78MFtfKQ.evidence: Evaluates 13 prompting strategies, specialized systems, and end-to-end agents on 753 executable quadruplets with judge components validated against human judgments.
RT78MFtfKQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the 753 aligned quadruplets and controlled three-phase evaluation design provide useful diagnostic separation of research failures.
RT78MFtfKQ.main_concern: Reviewers note that the central implementation-bottleneck claim lacks reported scoring criteria, sample sizes, and confidence intervals for the human-validity comparison.

pD4CdKsQoc.one_liner: Introduces a 270K-observation metric BEV benchmark for single-view indoor floormap completion comparing deterministic and generative models.
pD4CdKsQoc.problem: Single egocentric images capture limited floor area, and standard IoU metrics reward predicting floor everywhere rather than modeling spatial ambiguity.
pD4CdKsQoc.method: FlatLands unifies 270,575 observations from 17,656 scenes across six 3D datasets into aligned BEV observation, visibility, validity, and ground-truth maps, evaluating eleven deterministic, ensemble, and generative models on geometry and RGB tracks.
pD4CdKsQoc.key_idea: Standardizes single-view BEV floormap completion across six 3D datasets and evaluates multi-sample generative predictions with proper scoring rules and planning.
pD4CdKsQoc.evidence: Benchmark evaluations of eleven models across in-distribution, out-of-distribution (ScanNet++), and end-to-end RGB tracks plus risk-weighted planning.
pD4CdKsQoc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the large unified benchmark, OOD and RGB evaluation tracks, and demonstration that IoU favors trivial All-Floor baselines.
pD4CdKsQoc.main_concern: Reviewers cite confounded planning comparisons (different traversal costs for generative vs. U-Net planners), single-seed training, and limited evidence of diverse layout recovery.

9eRKjmjObm.one_liner: Scales tabular augmentation perturbations inversely with sample Shapley contribution and feature SHAP importance alongside dynamic domain correction.
9eRKjmjObm.problem: Augmenting small, imbalanced, constrained tabular datasets risks violating cross-feature constraints or distorting informative samples.
9eRKjmjObm.method: DIDA computes sample-level Shapley contributions and feature-level SHAP importance to allocate perturbation magnitudes—perturbing high-contribution samples and key features less—derived from constrained diversity maximization. It applies dynamic domain correction and constraint-guided categorical sampling to preserve valid feature combinations.
9eRKjmjObm.key_idea: Scales tabular feature perturbations inversely with sample Shapley value and feature SHAP importance under dynamic domain and categorical constraints.
9eRKjmjObm.evidence: Evaluated across six public tabular datasets, six augmentation baselines, and ten downstream classifiers on AUC-ROC, AUC-PR, F1, JS divergence, and Wasserstein metrics.
9eRKjmjObm.claimed_gains: Improves average AUC-ROC, AUC-PR, and F1 by 1.94, 2.30, and 4.30 percentage points over the strongest competing baseline.
9eRKjmjObm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree adapting perturbation strength to sample and feature importance is intuitive and improves performance across tabular datasets.
9eRKjmjObm.main_concern: Reviewers spot a mathematical inconsistency between Theorem 1 (1/sqrt(b'_j)) and Appendix Eq. 31 (1/b'_j) plus an ad-hoc practical function, missing runtime comparisons, and business-rule domain expansion risks.

ovf02gwAM4.one_liner: Generalizes signed-network polarized community detection via a one-parameter quasi-arithmetic mean objective and marginal peeling.
ovf02gwAM4.problem: The standard 2-Polarized-Communities objective uses an arithmetic mean of node balances, missing core-like or hub-driven polarized structures.
ovf02gwAM4.method: The authors formulate a one-parameter quasi-arithmetic exponential mean objective controlled by p, analyze its complexity across p regimes, and design a generalized peeling algorithm based on exact marginal objective changes.
ovf02gwAM4.key_idea: Interpolate between core-like and hub-driven polarized communities with an exponential quasi-arithmetic mean objective and peel nodes by exact marginal objective change.
ovf02gwAM4.evidence: Theoretical complexity proofs (NP-hardness and polynomial-time cases) and experiments on synthetic and real-world signed graphs support the method.
ovf02gwAM4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that generalizing polarity via the exponential mean captures distinct community structures and that the complexity results are useful.
ovf02gwAM4.main_concern: Reviewers question the incremental algorithmic novelty over standard peeling and note missing real-network comparisons against ordinary peeling selected by the same objective.

yEYioJFZPK.one_liner: Optimizes red-teaming jailbreaks over a surrogate ensemble that explicitly varies both model weights and system policies.
yEYioJFZPK.problem: Automated red-teaming transfer frameworks overlook how system policies alongside model weights affect jailbreak transfer to unseen deployments.
yEYioJFZPK.method: CAST combines strategy-conditioned candidate generation, ensemble-averaged guard scores, and explicit control over surrogate system policies, guided by a localized discrepancy transfer bound.
yEYioJFZPK.key_idea: Treat the system prompt policy as an explicit coordinate alongside model weights in a strategy-conditioned surrogate ensemble for transfer red-teaming.
yEYioJFZPK.evidence: Evaluations span 300 HarmBench behaviors and 34 deployment configurations across open and hardened targets, plus theoretical bounds and ablations.
yEYioJFZPK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical insight that system policies reshape model vulnerability profiles and value the 34-configuration transfer evaluation.
yEYioJFZPK.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty over TextGrad ensemble attacks, reliance on a single guard model, and unclear presentation connecting the theory to the method.

mt8WzlqNfi.one_liner: Compiles agent trajectories into dense long-context mid-training tasks targeting evidence grounding, aggregation, and state tracking.
mt8WzlqNfi.problem: How to organize raw agent interaction trajectories into effective mid-training supervision for long-context and agent capabilities remains underexplored.
mt8WzlqNfi.method: TrajLong converts agent trajectories into dense long-context supervision tasks targeting evidence grounding, cross-evidence aggregation, and temporal state maintenance, applied before supervised fine-tuning.
mt8WzlqNfi.key_idea: Compile agent trajectories into validated QA and state-tracking supervision tasks targeting three atomic long-context capabilities during mid-training.
mt8WzlqNfi.evidence: Experiments mid-train Qwen3-14B-Base and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base and evaluate on 6 long-context and 12 agent benchmarks.
mt8WzlqNfi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear motivation linking long-context and agentic supervision and the broad evaluation across 18 benchmarks.
mt8WzlqNfi.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains over unmasked raw-trajectory mid-training are small and may be confounded by teacher-generated reasoning present only in TrajLong.

mqftaOFSQ1.one_liner: Estimates time-series source dataset transferability by regressing target future changes on representation changes across adjacent windows.
mqftaOFSQ1.problem: Existing time-series transferability estimators score individual windows independently and miss local temporal evolution between overlapping windows.
mqftaOFSQ1.method: CWRE decomposes series into trend and seasonal components, evaluates frozen source-pretrained encoders on target data using closed-form ridge regression over both instance-wise and cross-window trend differences.
mqftaOFSQ1.key_idea: Score source transferability via closed-form ridge regression measuring how representation changes across adjacent windows predict future trend changes.
mqftaOFSQ1.evidence: Experiments evaluate source selection across three target datasets, six candidate sources per target, cross-architecture settings, and missing-observation regimes.
mqftaOFSQ1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that cross-window representation-change correspondence is an interesting signal and appreciate the cross-architecture evaluation.
mqftaOFSQ1.main_concern: Reviewers point out asymmetric hyperparameter grid-search tuning favoring CWRE over untuned baselines and limited dataset scale (only three target datasets).

DSfrvWGdUU.one_liner: Pretrains wireless channel transformers via sparse multipath reconstruction using a complex-valued gated decoder.
DSfrvWGdUU.problem: Existing self-supervised learning methods for wireless channel state information ignore physical multipath sparsity priors.
DSfrvWGdUU.method: SpaRTran formulates unsupervised pretraining as compressed-sensing sparse multipath reconstruction on individual antenna links using a complex-valued gated decoder that separates component selection, magnitude, and phase.
DSfrvWGdUU.key_idea: Pretrain a channel transformer to reconstruct sparse multipath components per antenna link using a complex-valued gated decoder.
DSfrvWGdUU.evidence: Experiments test measured and simulated radio channels across positioning and beamforming codebook selection tasks.
DSfrvWGdUU.claimed_gains: Compared to prior baselines, SpaRTran cuts positioning error by up to 32% and increases top-1 codebook selection accuracy for beamforming by 26 percentage points.
DSfrvWGdUU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that embedding compressed-sensing sparse multipath priors into CSI pretraining is physically grounded and aids cross-system generalization.
DSfrvWGdUU.main_concern: Reviewers note weak low-data fine-tuning performance due to per-link pretraining missing inter-antenna correlations, plus mathematical concerns in the sparsity loss and proof.

TWINQu6sYD.one_liner: Allocates video token budgets by segment complexity and selects anchor tokens using a dynamism score and Facility Location.
TWINQu6sYD.problem: Training-free video LLM token compression methods typically allocate uniform budgets across frames or ignore temporal dynamics.
TWINQu6sYD.method: DynVid dynamically segments videos, allocates token budgets proportional to segment visual complexity, scores tokens by temporal dynamism and attention, and selects representative anchor tokens via Facility Location optimization.
TWINQu6sYD.key_idea: Allocates per-segment token budgets by complexity and selects anchor tokens via Facility Location over temporal dynamism and attention scores.
TWINQu6sYD.evidence: Experiments across eight video understanding benchmarks and four VLLMs including LLaVA-OneVision and Qwen2.5-VL.
TWINQu6sYD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that training-free, dynamism-aware adaptive token compression is practical and tested across broad video benchmarks.
TWINQu6sYD.main_concern: Novelty over FastVID, FlashVID, and prior spectral/Facility Location methods is limited, gains are modest without significance tests, and key hyperparameters vary per model and benchmark.

dEw3MgAbZJ.one_liner: Splits scene graph generation into visual-spatial and semantic-context branches coordinated by adaptive routing and tail cue augmentation.
dEw3MgAbZJ.problem: Scene graph generation suffers from semantic ambiguity, poor generalization to unseen triplets, and long-tailed predicate distributions.
dEw3MgAbZJ.method: DCRM models visual-spatial and pretrained-encoder semantic-context cues in separate branches fused by a predicate-adaptive router, while Synthetic Cue Augmentation (SCA) transfers local variations from head to tail predicates.
dEw3MgAbZJ.key_idea: Processes visual-spatial and semantic-context cues in separate branches fused by an adaptive router, with head-to-tail variation transfer in cue space.
dEw3MgAbZJ.evidence: Experiments and ablations on VG150, OIV6, and GQA200 across PredCls, SGCls, and SGDet settings.
dEw3MgAbZJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical dual-cue design, informative ablations, and improved long-tail recall from SCA.
dEw3MgAbZJ.main_concern: Performance gains over baselines may stem from pretrained BLIP features and differing branch losses (CE vs. WCE) rather than the dual-cue architecture itself.

nGMvpOJr2S.one_liner: Routes public tokens separately and perturbs compressed private hidden-state residuals with Gaussian noise for differentially private LLM inference.
nGMvpOJr2S.problem: Language-model APIs can leak both private fine-tuning data and sensitive query-time context through generated output transcripts.
nGMvpOJr2S.method: DP-LAIR uses a DP-trained router to send public-context tokens along a public path while compressing private-context hidden-state residuals into a clipped, Gaussian-perturbed latent space decoded back to output. Training-time privacy is enforced via DP training of the router and decoder, while runtime privacy uses data-dependent leave-one-out sensitivity accounting.
nGMvpOJr2S.key_idea: Splits token generation via a DP-trained router and clips and noises compressed private-to-public hidden-state residuals with leave-one-out runtime privacy accounting.
nGMvpOJr2S.evidence: Experiments across two datasets and four model configurations measure utility, leakage, membership inference, and ablations against a joint baseline.
nGMvpOJr2S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly protecting training-time and inference-time privacy in an API-only setting is practical and well-motivated.
nGMvpOJr2S.main_concern: Reviewers identify a gap in the training-data privacy proof because the encoder, covariance, and private backbone use private data without DP.

BKbzQiXL4Z.one_liner: Introduces Identity-Centric Emotion Tracking over unsegmented multi-party videos and a 21-hour bilingual dataset EmoTrack.
BKbzQiXL4Z.problem: Existing multimodal emotion benchmarks assume pre-segmented utterances and evaluate only the active speaker, ignoring continuous conversations and non-speaker reactions.
BKbzQiXL4Z.method: Identity-Centric Emotion Tracking (ICET) couples three sub-tasks—Utterance Segmentation, Identity-Consistent Emotion Classification, and Emotion-Cause Extraction—across both speakers and non-speakers. To support it, the authors annotate EmoTrack, a Chinese-English dataset with 22,585 utterance-level emotion-cause labels over 21 hours of conversational video.
BKbzQiXL4Z.key_idea: Removes pre-segmentation and speaker-only assumptions by tracking utterance boundaries, identity-consistent emotions, and causes for all participants in continuous video.
BKbzQiXL4Z.evidence: Benchmarks MLLMs (with and without speech-aligned transcripts and RL) on the 21-hour, 22,585-annotation bilingual EmoTrack dataset.
