BKbzQiXL4Z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note EmoTrack's scale and bilingual annotation protocol address pre-segmentation and speaker-centrism gaps (second review; first review text is off-topic).
BKbzQiXL4Z.main_concern: Reviewers note ICET still requires a designated target face image as input rather than discovering salient participants and omits non-MLLM baselines.

Z9hxnowPnT.one_liner: Adapts constraint penalty weights in LLM-guided evolutionary search using signed violations and the evolving feasible frontier.
Z9hxnowPnT.problem: LLM-guided evolutionary search typically discards infeasible programs or relies on brittle, task-specific fixed penalty weights.
Z9hxnowPnT.method: CAP retains infeasible programs and adapts constraint penalties via a quadratic program based on normalized signed violations and the best feasible frontier, integrated with AdaEvolve in CAP-Evolve.
Z9hxnowPnT.key_idea: Retains infeasible programs and updates constraint penalty weights via a QP over normalized violations relative to the evolving feasible frontier.
Z9hxnowPnT.evidence: Convergence proof under idealized oracle assumptions plus experiments on four constrained program-optimization tasks (seven configurations) using AdaEvolve.
Z9hxnowPnT.claimed_gains: CAP-Evolve attains the best mean result in six of seven task configurations.
Z9hxnowPnT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical and that CAP integrates cleanly into scalar-fitness LLM evolutionary search.
Z9hxnowPnT.main_concern: Reviewers point out a missing scalar fixed-penalty baseline for multi-constraint (K>1) tasks, gains mostly within noise (n=5), and a gap between idealized theory and finite-budget LLM search.

M9mXkYx3cO.one_liner: Benchmarks federated continual graph learning across node and link tasks while isolating client allocation and task-order effects.
M9mXkYx3cO.problem: Evaluating federated continual graph learning is confounded because client graph partitioning alters both local connectivity and label distributions alongside task ordering.
M9mXkYx3cO.method: GECKO defines seven matched evaluation scenarios across node classification, link classification, and link prediction under Task-, Class-, and Domain-IL, varying client allocation and task order one factor at a time.
M9mXkYx3cO.key_idea: Varies client graph partitioning and task ordering independently under matched seeds with diagnostics for cross-client support, acquisition, and forgetting.
M9mXkYx3cO.evidence: Evaluated across four datasets (mainly OGBN-Arxiv, Bitcoin-OTC, and GEMSEC Facebook) with full-grid runs on three of seven scenarios.
M9mXkYx3cO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the matched-comparison design that isolates client allocation from task order and extends beyond node classification.
M9mXkYx3cO.main_concern: Reviewers find benchmark coverage too thin, with full-grid learner evaluations in only three of seven scenarios, no learner results on NC-Domain, and FCGL-specific baselines absent from link tasks.

juE3eTe2BN.one_liner: Analyzes how contrastive projection-head critics impose distributional biases on retained encoder representations.
juE3eTe2BN.problem: Discarded projection heads strongly influence contrastive encoder representations, yet the mechanism linking critic expressiveness to downstream usability is poorly understood.
juE3eTe2BN.method: The authors analyze the critic induced by the projection head and similarity function, showing restricted separable critics impose distributional biases that yield better downstream linear-probe accuracy despite lower InfoNCE estimates.
juE3eTe2BN.key_idea: Shows that restricted separable projection-head critics constrain realizable encoder output distributions, trading off lower InfoNCE bounds for stronger downstream linear separability.
juE3eTe2BN.evidence: Information-theoretic lemmas and experiments on CIFAR-10 (six seeds) and a seven-class ImageNet subset comparing separable versus MLP and fixed critics.
juE3eTe2BN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question of how discarded projection-head critics shape retained representations interesting and appreciate the InfoNCE-vs-accuracy evidence.
juE3eTe2BN.main_concern: Reviewers identify a false equality in the NWJ part of Lemma 5.1, question Proposition 5.2's distribution-matching claim, and note small-scale datasets and missing experimental details.

t258GGlEhL.one_liner: Adapts rectified-flow probabilistic time-series forecasters online under delayed feedback using nearest-residual source assignment and replay.
t258GGlEhL.problem: Existing online time-series forecasters only update point predictions, while generative probabilistic forecasters remain fixed after offline training.
t258GGlEhL.method: OnART uses offline re-flow to straighten conditional transport for one-step residual generation. At deployment, when delayed feedback arrives, it pairs the new residual endpoint with the Gaussian source of the nearest cached forecast-time residual (minimizing target shift) and updates the velocity model alongside generated replay.
t258GGlEhL.key_idea: Straightens transport via offline re-flow and adapts online under delayed feedback by pairing new residuals with the nearest cached residual's Gaussian source.
t258GGlEhL.evidence: Evaluated on multivariate time-series datasets (including ETTh2) comparing CRPS-sum and MSE against offline probabilistic and online point baselines.
t258GGlEhL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree online probabilistic adaptation under delayed feedback is an under-explored problem and proximity source assignment with one-step re-flow is intuitive.
t258GGlEhL.main_concern: Reviewers note that the model is channel-separable despite using multivariate CRPS-sum as the headline metric, and find gains over point-only online updates modest.

a28MwJjOcz.one_liner: Verifies world-action model residual candidates against stage-wise physical task-state references before execution.
a28MwJjOcz.problem: World action models can drift from stage-critical object poses, contacts, and spatial relations during closed-loop long-horizon robotic manipulation.
a28MwJjOcz.method: TraceWAM maintains stage-wise physical references and a recurrent progress memory, predicting object-centric alignment deviations and uncertainty for base and residual action chunks. Trained on branched simulator rollouts, it accepts a residual candidate only when predicted risk and progress margins improve over the base action.
a28MwJjOcz.key_idea: Evaluates base and residual action chunks against stage-wise physical references in an object-centric task-state space before selecting actions.
a28MwJjOcz.evidence: Evaluated on RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, and RMBench against Fast-WAM and matched-context verifier baselines.
a28MwJjOcz.claimed_gains: Achieves average success rates of 93.0% on RoboTwin 2.0 and 98.1% on LIBERO, outperforming Fast-WAM by 1.6 and 1.4 percentage points.
a28MwJjOcz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree modeling object-centric task-state alignment drift is well-motivated and yields consistent empirical gains across manipulation benchmarks.
a28MwJjOcz.main_concern: Reviewers highlight heavy reliance on underspecified external components (task-state reader, schema library, pose prototypes) and missing comparisons to related verifiers like EV-WM.

HntDkhSU6J.one_liner: Optimizes per-tensor cubic models over exact block Hessians matrix-free using Lanczos Krylov subspaces and an exponential subsolver.
HntDkhSU6J.problem: Dense cubic Newton methods fail to scale past ~15k parameters, while scalable variants approximate Hessians and lose exact block curvature.
HntDkhSU6J.method: ARC-block minimizes a per-tensor cubic model over the true block Hessian using a matrix-free Lanczos Krylov subsolver (CubicKrylov) or a trust-controlled exponential relaxation step (ARC-phi1) with per-block adaptive cubic constants and monotone full-loss guards.
HntDkhSU6J.key_idea: Solves per-tensor cubic regularization models over true block Hessians matrix-free in a Lanczos Krylov subspace with monotone full-loss acceptance.
HntDkhSU6J.evidence: Theoretical sweep complexity bounds plus experiments on FINER INR fitting and a 91.4M-parameter ViSIR model.
HntDkhSU6J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree scaling curvature-based cubic regularization to 91.4M parameters and achieving strong FINER training PSNR gains are impressive.
HntDkhSU6J.main_concern: Reviewers point out a disconnect between the sweep theorem (requiring fresh gradients and certified residuals) and the practical algorithm, plus limited test-set generalization gains.

AMOf1NpBaK.one_liner: Investigates why frozen single-table tabular foundation models with parameter-free relational encoders perform well on relational databases.
AMOf1NpBaK.problem: It is poorly understood why single-table tabular foundation models without relational pretraining compete with specialized relational foundation models on relational databases.
AMOf1NpBaK.method: The authors benchmark tabular foundation model pipelines (e.g., RDBLearn, TabPFN-Rel) against relational foundation models across diverse RDB benchmarks, and propose explanations based on parameter-free encoders mapping relational effects into distributions resembling single-table data, locality, and convergent posterior predictive distributions.
AMOf1NpBaK.key_idea: Explains single-table FM success on relational data via parameter-free encoders producing single-table-like embeddings that preserve in-context posterior predictive convergence.
AMOf1NpBaK.evidence: Empirical comparisons across six relational database benchmark groups and single-table-induced RDBs.
AMOf1NpBaK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the broad multi-benchmark comparison showing TFM pipelines rivaling specialized relational FMs is valuable.
AMOf1NpBaK.main_concern: Reviewers find the theoretical explanations disconnected from the experiments, noting that proposed mechanisms (e.g., continuum parameter tau, context sampling) are not directly tested.

2k6d72Tdzs.one_liner: Trains an attention-pointer scheduling policy via behavioral cloning of a clairvoyant expert for non-clairvoyant job scheduling.
2k6d72Tdzs.problem: Learning-augmented schedulers collapse job information into a single predicted processing-time scalar, making ordering brittle to prediction errors.
2k6d72Tdzs.method: The authors train a behavioral cloning policy with an attention-based pointer mechanism that scores an arbitrary number of pending jobs directly at each decision step by imitating a clairvoyant expert, supporting both single-machine and parallel-machine scheduling.
2k6d72Tdzs.key_idea: Replaces predict-then-schedule scalar estimators with an attention-pointer policy trained via behavioral cloning of a clairvoyant expert.
2k6d72Tdzs.evidence: Evaluated on two production workload traces (ATLAS and the newly constructed 463,279-job ASTRA GPU trace) measuring completion time, maximum stretch, and makespan.
2k6d72Tdzs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree bypassing scalar size prediction via an attention-pointer policy over variable pending job sets is clean and evaluated on a large production trace.
2k6d72Tdzs.main_concern: Reviewers note thin single-run evidence (~1% gain on total completion time), limited novelty in combining BC with pointer networks, and unaddressed order-prediction baselines.

hZfZlf7fhc.one_liner: Models prospective actions as evolving target-linked lifecycle states updated by events and no-event intervals in MTPPs.
hZfZlf7fhc.problem: Standard marked temporal point processes treat prospective actions (like cart additions) as static history items rather than tracking whether they remain pending or expire.
hZfZlf7fhc.method: PAL-MTPP represents each prospective action as a latent target-linked lifecycle state updated continuously during event-free intervals and upon observed events while preserving realization uncertainty. For multi-target events, it adds pairwise target interactions to refine set-valued predictions.
hZfZlf7fhc.key_idea: Tracks prospective actions as evolving latent lifecycle states updated by both realized events and no-event intervals, plus pairwise target interactions.
hZfZlf7fhc.evidence: Evaluated on real-world mobility and e-commerce datasets and synthetic intensity-recovery experiments against action-aware MTPP baselines.
hZfZlf7fhc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree distinguishing prospective actions from realized events via evolving lifecycle states is practically relevant for event forecasting.
hZfZlf7fhc.main_concern: Reviewers point out imprecise notation and missing mathematical definitions for the event-arrival lifecycle update, parameterizations, and simpler time-decay baselines.

2z48ECWKiZ.one_liner: Constructs positive-definite hyperbolic kernels whose canonical feature maps preserve the intrinsic Riemannian metric of the Poincare manifold.
2z48ECWKiZ.problem: Existing hyperbolic kernels enforce only metric-space isometry, causing a mismatch between practical kernel-induced similarities and intrinsic geodesic distances.
2z48ECWKiZ.method: Starting from the Riemannian isometry condition on the Poincare model, the authors derive sufficient conditions and construct four positive-definite Riemannian isometric kernels (RILog, RIBin, RIExp, RIInt) whose induced distances are monotonic in geodesic distance.
2z48ECWKiZ.key_idea: Designs positive-definite hyperbolic kernels whose canonical RKHS feature maps induce a metric matching the Poincare manifold's intrinsic Riemannian metric.
2z48ECWKiZ.evidence: Supported by mathematical proofs, geometric stress analysis on CIFAR-FS, and experiments on zero-shot learning, few-shot learning, graph node classification, and semantic textual tasks.
2z48ECWKiZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Riemannian isometry formulation is mathematically clean and well proven, with broad evaluation across geometric distortion and four downstream tasks.
2z48ECWKiZ.main_concern: Reviewers note modest practical gains without multi-seed variance (since monotonic kernels yield identical inference rankings to hyperbolic distance), unclear restriction to the Poincare model, and shrunken table fonts.

lxemNMmtMC.one_liner: Establishes Markovian nonconvex ADMM convergence for tabular RL using discounted Bellman-resolvent stability instead of a smooth block.
lxemNMmtMC.problem: Classical nonconvex ADMM convergence proofs rely on a designated smooth block with fixed linear constraints, which does not hold for policy-dependent Bellman constraints under Markovian sampling.
lxemNMmtMC.method: The authors show that invertibility of the discounted Bellman resolvent (I - gamma P_pi)^{-1} provides dual-multiplier stability and analyze an empirical Bellman surrogate under Markovian sampling where mixing, drift, and noise enter as a single operator perturbation.
lxemNMmtMC.key_idea: Uses stability of the discounted Bellman resolvent (I - gamma P_pi)^{-1} to control ADMM multiplier updates under Markovian sampling without a smooth block or double sampling.
lxemNMmtMC.evidence: Supported by almost-sure KKT convergence, finite-time iteration/sample complexity, global policy-optimality bounds for tabular MDPs, and small MDP experiments.
lxemNMmtMC.claimed_gains: Establishes O(epsilon^-1) iteration complexity and O(epsilon^-2) sample complexity for squared KKT accuracy epsilon, with global suboptimality J* - J(pi) = O(sqrt(G)) under occupancy coverage.
lxemNMmtMC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree using Bellman-resolvent invertibility to secure ADMM multiplier stability is a coherent and reusable theoretical viewpoint bridging optimization and RL.
lxemNMmtMC.main_concern: Reviewers note the main complexity rates are restricted to tabular MDPs in terms of KKT residuals, experiments test only small MDPs against ADMM variants without showing RL benefits, and presentation obscures the core advance.

Nwnl0KI1bu.one_liner: Jointly searches ordered discrete sensor acquisition settings and neural architectures using adjacent-level loss finite differences and a conditioned hypernetwork.
Nwnl0KI1bu.problem: Standard NAS fixes sensor acquisition parameters because discrete pre-acquisition choices alter inputs non-differentiably, while black-box joint search is prohibitively expensive.
Nwnl0KI1bu.method: SPANAS estimates within-interval selector gradients via finite loss differences between adjacent measured sensor levels under shared weights, while conditioning an architecture hypernetwork on a structured representation of the sensor configuration.
Nwnl0KI1bu.key_idea: Uses finite loss differences between adjacent ordered sensor-acquisition levels to estimate selector gradients while conditioning a shared-weight architecture hypernetwork on the acquisition configuration.
Nwnl0KI1bu.evidence: Supported by joint accuracy–storage Pareto-front evaluations on FMCW-radar marshalling recognition, a wearable inertial (IMU) benchmark, and speech commands.
Nwnl0KI1bu.claimed_gains: Raises mean hypervolume by 11% on radar and 7% on IMU over the strongest 100-evaluation black-box campaign.
Nwnl0KI1bu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the joint sensor-acquisition and NAS pipeline is clearly presented, respects discrete ordinal geometry, and outperforms architecture-only tuning across sensing domains.
Nwnl0KI1bu.main_concern: Reviewers view the adjacent-level finite-difference gradient and hypernetwork combination as incremental, note missing data-aware NAS baselines and low diversity along the argmax-derived Pareto front, and question unexplained qNEHVI variance.

zGrJlClKC6.one_liner: Trains separate low-rank adapter branches for endpoint and bidirectional semantic transition alignment, then merges them for zero-shot CIR.
zGrJlClKC6.problem: Projection-based zero-shot composed image retrieval methods suffer from semantic transition bottlenecks and gradient conflicts when endpoint and transition supervision share one text adapter.
zGrJlClKC6.method: DeCIR constructs paired forward and reverse edit tuples from image-caption pairs, trains dedicated low-rank text adapter branches for endpoint alignment and semantic transition alignment, and merges them via Low-Rank Directional Merge (LRDM) into a single inference-time adapter.
zGrJlClKC6.key_idea: Decouple endpoint alignment and paired forward/reverse semantic transition supervision into separate low-rank text adapter branches and merge them via LRDM into one lightweight adapter.
zGrJlClKC6.evidence: Experiments evaluate DeCIR on CIRR, CIRCO, FashionIQ, and GeneCIS across two backbones and integrations with Pic2Word, SEARLE, and LinCIR.
zGrJlClKC6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling endpoint and transition supervision while keeping single-path, LLM-free inference is well motivated and delivers consistent gains across four benchmarks.
zGrJlClKC6.main_concern: Reviewers note that LRDM's contribution is not isolated from shared-basis branch training (where coefficient averaging equals weight-update averaging), gains are not disentangled from synthetic LLM training supervision, and prior work like DistillCIR is insufficiently differentiated.

KeHyHmww83.one_liner: Estimates semantic entropy under a noisy pairwise judge by counting agreements and shared-answer pairs without clustering responses.
KeHyHmww83.problem: Standard semantic entropy estimation clusters LLM answers using a pairwise judge, which fails when judge noise prevents accurate individual answer grouping.
KeHyHmww83.method: Under a noisy pairwise channel model with at most three meanings, the authors estimate Shannon entropy directly from agreement counts and squared-degree statistics (pairs of agreements sharing an answer) without clustering, and derive matching minimax rates.
KeHyHmww83.key_idea: Count pairwise judge agreements and shared-answer agreement pairs to estimate semantic entropy directly without clustering answers, achieving consistency even below the cluster-recovery threshold.
KeHyHmww83.evidence: Non-asymptotic minimax upper and lower bounds are established theoretically alongside synthetic channel-model experiments.
KeHyHmww83.claimed_gains: With at most three meanings and small n*Delta^2, the estimator attains minimax MSE order min{1, (n^3 * Delta^4)^(-1/2)}, with uniform consistency when n^3 * Delta^4 -> infinity (error vanishing for Delta = n^(-gamma) with 1/2 < gamma < 3/4).
KeHyHmww83.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that challenging the necessity of explicit clustering for semantic entropy estimation via a simple count-based estimator with minimax bounds is an interesting theoretical contribution.
KeHyHmww83.main_concern: Reviewers point out the highly restrictive scope (at most K=3 meanings, uniform pairwise error channel, known channel parameters), lack of real LLM/NLI judge experiments, and dense presentation.

xaumPxgms3.one_liner: Benchmarks automated presentation generation with 2,191 task-specific verification items separating instruction following, content quality, and visual defects.
xaumPxgms3.problem: Aggregate quality scores for automated presentation generation hide blocking failures such as instruction violations, missing mandatory content, or slide cropping and occlusion.
xaumPxgms3.method: SlideGate introduces 40 presentation-generation tasks across seven scenarios and five input forms with 2,191 task-specific verification items, evaluating instruction following, content quality, and visual presentation separately and flagging decks with blocking failures.
xaumPxgms3.key_idea: Decompose slide-deck evaluation into task-specific binary verification items across instruction following, content coverage, and visual defects to detect blocking failures masked by overall scores.
xaumPxgms3.evidence: SlideGate is applied to 240 outputs from six commercial slide-generation systems and validated against two independent blinded human annotators.
xaumPxgms3.claimed_gains: Binary content-item judgments agree with two blinded annotators at 80.7% and 85.6%, visual rankings correlate with human preference at Spearman rho = 0.829, and SlideGate detects 124 decks with blocking failures (all audited flagged decks confirmed by annotators).
xaumPxgms3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating instruction fulfillment and blocking defects from visual polish addresses a practical gap in evaluating presentation-generation systems.
xaumPxgms3.main_concern: Reviewers note limited differentiation from prior slide benchmarks (PresentBench, PPTBench, SlideAudit), reliance on LM evaluators over only six commercial systems, and incomplete validation of the blocking-failure aggregation rule.

FpslcUkTz5.one_liner: Parametrizes synthetic time-series pretraining data by structure, dimensionality, and distribution shape to match model input pipelines.
FpslcUkTz5.problem: It is unclear which statistical properties make synthetic time-series pretraining corpora transferable across models with different input preprocessing pipelines.
FpslcUkTz5.method: The authors propose the Transfer-Invariance Principle—arguing that a model's input transform decides which corpus properties govern transfer—and build TransferForge, a synthetic generator with explicit controls for structure, dimensionality, and value distribution shape.
FpslcUkTz5.key_idea: Generate synthetic pretraining corpora with explicit controls for structure, dimensionality, and distribution shape tailored to whether the target model's input pipeline normalizes windows.
FpslcUkTz5.evidence: Experiments test TransferForge on PatchTST (UCR classification), forecasting, and POYO+ (unnormalized calcium neural decoding), including an input-normalization flip ablation.
FpslcUkTz5.claimed_gains: On POYO+, TransferForge's Gaussian and calcium-shaped corpora transfer within 2% of each other (neither differing significantly from real pretraining), and flipping only input normalization on time series changes the effect of a shape manipulation by 5.8x.
FpslcUkTz5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question of how model input pipelines govern synthetic pretraining transferability interesting and appreciate the multi-domain empirical tests.
FpslcUkTz5.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the lack of theoretical backing for the Transfer-Invariance Principle, note that the normalization experiment confounds distribution shape with window scale (while z-scoring still preserves higher moments), and cite missing comparisons to CauKer.

tXMv00VV7W.one_liner: Tracks per-step gradient spectral energy concentration to adaptively project LLM RLVR updates onto a low-rank subspace.
tXMv00VV7W.problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) uses optimizers inherited from teacher-forcing SFT despite exhibiting shrinking effective gradient dimensionality over training.
tXMv00VV7W.method: Ares (Adaptive Rank-Effective Spectral Optimization) estimates the effective update rank from each 2D gradient's spectral energy distribution using approximate SVD, tracks its evolution, and restricts the gradient driving each update to that low-rank subspace.
tXMv00VV7W.key_idea: Estimate effective gradient rank from spectral energy concentration at each step and project RLVR gradient updates onto the resulting adaptive low-rank subspace.
tXMv00VV7W.evidence: Spectral analyses compare RLVR against SFT and random-reward controls, and optimization experiments evaluate Ares against AdamW across LLM scales and RLVR algorithms.
tXMv00VV7W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the spectral analysis of RLVR gradients well motivated and note consistent empirical improvements over AdamW across model scales and RLVR algorithms.
tXMv00VV7W.main_concern: Reviewers highlight heavy per-step compute overhead from 20-iteration approximate SVDs without wall-clock comparisons, weak evidence that adaptive rank beats fixed low-rank filtering, and tension with Figure 2 showing higher SFT spectral concentration.

d29zdOjAi7.one_liner: Orchestrates an occlusion-aware 3D generator's active voxel coordinates with a detail-rich generator and metric-scale pose calibration.
d29zdOjAi7.problem: Single-image 3D scene generators trade off occlusion completion, fine local geometry/texture, and metric-scale layout accuracy due to scarce jointly annotated training data.
d29zdOjAi7.method: The training-free pipeline extracts active voxel coordinates from an occlusion-aware 3D generator (SAM3D), infuses them into a detail-rich generator (TRELLIS.2) alongside inpainted visual conditioning, and calibrates metric-scale object pose using visible-region boundaries and visible depth.
d29zdOjAi7.key_idea: Condition a detail-rich 3D generator on active voxel coordinates from an occlusion-aware generator and fit metric scale and translation to visible boundaries and depth.
d29zdOjAi7.evidence: Evaluations test the training-free orchestration and metric-scale calibration across multiple 3D generators on single-image 3D scene generation.
d29zdOjAi7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that orchestrating complementary pretrained 3D models without training is intuitive and improves over base generators.
d29zdOjAi7.main_concern: Reviewers view methodological novelty as limited (combining SAM3D, TRELLIS.2, and a closed commercial 2D inpainter), question whether occlusion gains come from the inpainter rather than voxel handoff, and note that rotation is left uncalibrated.

9wUe4gLzDm.one_liner: Co-evolves an adversarial task-generating attacker and a tool-using defender via RL weighted by within-task defender-reward variability.
9wUe4gLzDm.problem: Existing adversarial co-evolution for LLM safety focuses on language-level prompts or fixed web tasks rather than multi-turn tool-using agents facing diverse environment attacks.
9wUe4gLzDm.method: AgentSafeEvo runs an attacker-defender RL game where the attacker constructs adversarial agent tasks and tool environments to induce unsafe tool use while the defender learns safe completion, using learnability-guided weighting based on within-task defender-reward variance to weight GRPO updates.
9wUe4gLzDm.key_idea: Co-evolve an attacker that synthesizes adversarial agent tasks/environments against a defender using GRPO updates weighted by within-task defender-reward variability.
9wUe4gLzDm.evidence: Experiments train on Qwen3-8B and evaluate across multiple agent safety benchmarks, general agent capability benchmarks, and cross-model attack transfer.
9wUe4gLzDm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that letting an attacker construct full adversarial agent tasks and tool environments is a meaningful extension of adversarial co-evolution with strong empirical gains.
9wUe4gLzDm.main_concern: Reviewers warn that the attacker reward could incentivize infeasible tasks without validity checks, note overlap with variance-based curriculum weighting (VCRL) without baseline comparisons, and observe training is limited to Qwen models.

7BiJjnbdM6.one_liner: Optimizes a sequence of latents for a frozen Behavior Foundation Model at test time using simulator feedback for motion tracking.
7BiJjnbdM6.problem: Behavior Foundation Models map single tasks to stationary latents, while look-ahead averaging heuristics fail to track highly dynamic time-varying motions.
7BiJjnbdM6.method: BFMTrack keeps a pre-trained BFM frozen and runs test-time optimization over a sequence of latent codes using simulator feedback to track reference motions, including sparse references.
7BiJjnbdM6.key_idea: Refine a time-varying sequence of latent codes for a frozen Behavior Foundation Model via test-time simulator-feedback optimization.
7BiJjnbdM6.evidence: Evaluations test BFMTrack on 990 motion clips against zero-shot BFM inference, generalist and specialist trackers, disturbance robustness tests, sparse references, and real humanoid deployment.
7BiJjnbdM6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that optimizing latent sequences without retraining the BFM delivers clear tracking gains (e.g., reducing MPJPE to 2.51 cm) and strong real-humanoid results across extensive clips.
7BiJjnbdM6.main_concern: Reviewers note narrow methodological novelty over prior frozen-BFM latent optimizers (BFM-Zero, LoLA, Sikchi et al.), question the mathematical handling of temporally correlated perturbations, and note missing evaluations on non-tracking BFM tasks.

FO8nfRhCrE.one_liner: Extracts training-free VLM lineage vectors via random projection of CLIP image-response outer-product matrices.
FO8nfRhCrE.problem: Black-box VLM identification and lineage tracing via text-only response embeddings ignores how generated answers align with visual inputs.
FO8nfRhCrE.method: DNAExtract probes VLMs with a shared set of image-question pairs, encodes images and responses with frozen CLIP encoders, forms outer-product interaction matrices, and applies sparse random projection to yield compact distance-preserving VLM DNA vectors.
FO8nfRhCrE.key_idea: Computes sparse random projections of frozen CLIP image-response outer-product matrices over shared VQA probes as black-box VLM identity vectors.
FO8nfRhCrE.evidence: Evaluated on 39 open-source VLMs from seven families across relation detection, one-to-one verification, and one-to-many base-model identification.
FO8nfRhCrE.claimed_gains: Achieves 0.929 AUC for relation detection, 0.923 AUC for one-to-one verification, and 89.38% rank-1 accuracy for base-model identification.
FO8nfRhCrE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the black-box VLM lineage-tracing problem is practical and that the training-free extraction pipeline is simple and clearly presented.
FO8nfRhCrE.main_concern: Reviewers note limited methodological novelty over LLM DNA, observe that normalized shared image embeddings reduce outer-product distance to text-only distance, and criticize closed-set parent assumptions and missing text-only baselines on verification/identification.

lzxkk1ynai.one_liner: Selects multimodal label-error encoders and detectors adaptively from task prototypes and estimated noise levels.
lzxkk1ynai.problem: Multimodal annotation-error detectors and VLM judges vary in effectiveness across tasks and noise regimes, making a single fixed diagnostic strategy suboptimal.
lzxkk1ynai.method: After systematically benchmarking encoders, representation-based detectors, and VLM judges under controlled answer errors, the authors propose Task-conditioned Adaptive Diagnosis (TAG). TAG identifies the task, estimates noise conditions, and selects and combines diagnostic strategies with confidence-based fallback to a shared strategy.
lzxkk1ynai.key_idea: Identifies task identity and estimates noise levels to select encoder-detector combinations with confidence-based fallback to a shared strategy.
lzxkk1ynai.evidence: Evaluated via five-fold cross-validation across eight encoders and eleven detectors on AVA-Bench, ScienceQA, and MMMU under controlled synthetic answer errors.
lzxkk1ynai.claimed_gains: Exceeds the training-selected shared strategy in mean AUROC by 1.24 percentage points on AVA-Bench, 0.16 on ScienceQA, and 0.17 on MMMU.
lzxkk1ynai.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the systematic common-protocol comparison of encoders, detectors, and VLM judges across tasks and noise levels.
lzxkk1ynai.main_concern: Reviewers criticize marginal gains on ScienceQA and MMMU (where direct VLM judgment outperforms TAG), synthetic-only multiple-choice label corruptions without downstream training validation, and incremental algorithm-selection novelty.

NpSPNIkO5s.one_liner: Benchmarks five-way safety policy-to-action routing with counterfactual splits and Latin-square binding diagnostics.
NpSPNIkO5s.problem: Binary refuse-or-comply safety evaluations miss fine-grained policy routing errors where models pick the wrong action even when refusal polarity or rule citations are right.
NpSPNIkO5s.method: PolicyGround formalizes single-turn safety compliance as five-way next-action routing (unrestricted help, bounded assistance, clarification, refusal, escalation) across 2,400 controlled counterfactual and 1,026 diverse instances. It adds request-only, policy-only, and Latin-square crossed diagnostics to separate lexical cues from request-policy binding, plus a family-disjoint SFT-LoRA mitigation.
NpSPNIkO5s.key_idea: Evaluates five-way safety action routing with request-only, policy-only, and Latin-square crossed diagnostics that isolate request-policy binding from lexical shortcuts.
NpSPNIkO5s.evidence: Evaluated five open-weight models, Gemini-3.8-Flash, TF-IDF baselines, and family-disjoint SFT-LoRA on PolicyGround's Controlled, Diverse, and Crossed splits.
NpSPNIkO5s.claimed_gains: Models achieve 0.880–0.991 coarse refusal accuracy on Controlled yet pick the wrong fine-grained action on 12.5–32.8% of coarse-correct outputs and 5.0–34.3% of exact-citation outputs, while reaching 0.788–1.000 on Crossed versus chance for TF-IDF.
NpSPNIkO5s.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value moving beyond binary refusal metrics to five-way action diagnostics, conditional citation-error analyses, and statistical audits.
NpSPNIkO5s.main_concern: Reviewers note high policy-only lexical predictability (>0.97 TF-IDF on Controlled), saturation of the simplified Crossed split, non-blind gold verification, and no check that generated responses match chosen action labels.

pdkz1Ozx7W.one_liner: Synthesizes text-rich tables via frozen-LLM structured candidate generation and reliability-gated adversarial dataset-level selection.
pdkz1Ozx7W.problem: Existing tabular synthesis methods optimize individual record quality without preserving dataset-level predictive relationships between structured attributes and long text columns.
pdkz1Ozx7W.method: CAST keeps the text generator frozen and uses Structure-Aware Semantic Generation (SSG) to produce multiple narrative-role candidates from a shared semantic plan. Conditional Adversarial Selection (CAS) and Reliability-Guided Conservative Selection (RCS) then select candidates using task-feature matching, a fixed domain discriminator, and validation-gated reweighting.
pdkz1Ozx7W.key_idea: Generates multi-role text candidates from a frozen LLM under shared semantic plans and selects table records via validation-gated task and discriminator feedback.
pdkz1Ozx7W.evidence: Evaluated across three tabular datasets with text columns (Kickstarter, Cloth, Wine Reviews) spanning classification, regression, multiple generator backbones, and fusion strategies.
pdkz1Ozx7W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate separating record-level candidate construction from dataset-level utility selection without fine-tuning the generator.
pdkz1Ozx7W.main_concern: Reviewers note that evaluated texts are relatively short (19.5–60.3 words on average), warn about overfitting to proxy predictor signals, and note limited validation of record-level semantic fidelity.

vpahOt8lBU.one_liner: Uses repeated extraction-pass disagreement to diagnose agent memory failure regimes and route voting, retrieval, and answering.
vpahOt8lBU.problem: LLM agent memory consolidation suffers from both recoverable stochastic extraction drops and irreducible low-rank backbone compression, which aggregate accuracy conflates.
vpahOt8lBU.method: Regime-Routed Construction (RRC) runs multiple consolidation passes on the same history and measures extraction-pass disagreement alongside backbone capability. High disagreement triggers more extraction passes merged by majority vote, whereas low disagreement deepens retrieval above a capability threshold or declines unsupported queries below it, supported by a Fano-type irreducibility argument.
vpahOt8lBU.key_idea: Measures disagreement across repeated memory-extraction passes to distinguish stochastic noise from irreducible compression and route vote budgets, retrieval depth, and abstention.
vpahOt8lBU.evidence: Evaluated on two long-term memory benchmarks (LoCoMo and LongMemEval) across backbones from 1.5B to frontier API models, plus theoretical Fano-type analysis.
vpahOt8lBU.claimed_gains: Improves on the strongest published LoCoMo result by +4.7 F1.
vpahOt8lBU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the distinction between recoverable stochastic extraction noise and irreducible capability loss conceptually clean and appreciate the training-free design and candid negative results.
vpahOt8lBU.main_concern: Reviewers show that switching the answer policy from declining (gentle) to non-declining (plain) accounts for most reported LoCoMo gains, and flag cross-backbone baseline comparisons.

AUkvPP5mxS.one_liner: Studies fine-grained credit assignment and decaying process rewards for multimodal RL agents in a movie-trailer video-editing testbed.
AUkvPP5mxS.problem: It is unclear when fine-grained credit assignment helps multimodal RL agents and why fixed process rewards induce reward hacking over long horizons.
AUkvPP5mxS.method: The authors construct four stagewise movie-trailer editing tasks (Content Selection, Narrative Sequencing, Rough Cut, Fine Cut) spanning 30 to over 60 turns, and compare outcome-only GRPO, GRPO with fixed or decaying LLM-judge process rewards, and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD).
AUkvPP5mxS.key_idea: Decays LLM-judge process-reward weights to zero during GRPO training to curb long-horizon reward hacking while evaluating credit granularity across multi-stage video editing.
AUkvPP5mxS.evidence: Evaluated on film-disjoint splits of four video-editing task types comparing GRPO, GRPO+PRM (fixed and decayed), and OPSD.
AUkvPP5mxS.claimed_gains: Yields a 45.4% relative gain over outcome-only GRPO on Fine Cut tasks averaging over 60 turns, versus at most a 10.4% relative gain on simpler 30–40 turn tasks.
AUkvPP5mxS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the realistic, inspectable video-editing testbed with film-disjoint splits and transparent reporting of fixed-PRM reward hacking and negative results.
AUkvPP5mxS.main_concern: Reviewers note that Fine Cut confounds horizon length with unique audio/LLM-judge scoring, that methods use single training seeds without matched sampling budgets, and that LLM-judge outcome gains lack human validation.

fixmx7WK8m.one_liner: Pairs an LSTM with Gumbel-Softmax single-slot overwriting memory and Rune-Mazes benchmarks for POMDP experience rewriting.
fixmx7WK8m.problem: Partially observable RL memory architectures and benchmarks mostly test static retention rather than overwriting obsolete cues or fusing sequential update rules.
fixmx7WK8m.method: ALER combines an LSTM with an explicit slot memory that performs independently addressed Gumbel-Softmax single-slot writes and gated fusion of retrieved memory with the recurrent state. The authors also introduce Rune-Mazes, three environments with exact required memory-state counts testing cue inversion, cancellation, reset, and repetition.
fixmx7WK8m.key_idea: Augments an LSTM with Gumbel-Softmax single-slot memory overwriting and gated recurrent-memory fusion for experience rewriting in POMDPs.
fixmx7WK8m.evidence: Evaluated against seven memory baselines on Endless T-Maze (16 configurations), Rune T-Maze (five compositions), and Multi-Corridor under vector and pixel observations.
fixmx7WK8m.claimed_gains: Reaches a success rate of at least 0.82 across all 16 Endless T-Maze configurations and at least 0.99 across all five Rune T-Maze compositions.
fixmx7WK8m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate testing memory beyond retention and value the exact state-count analysis and specification of the Rune-Mazes diagnostic environments.
fixmx7WK8m.main_concern: Reviewers point out that ALER does not clearly outperform S5 or PPO-LSTM across settings, flag checkpoint selection on reported test episodes and numerical inconsistencies, and note unclear causal evidence that memory slots outperform the LSTM state.

WQVfUbjLtk.one_liner: Calibrates RL search-agent over-searching by reshaping step advantages with self-distilled hindsight likelihood discrepancies.
WQVfUbjLtk.problem: Outcome-based RL amplifies over-searching in search agents, while existing process-aware fixes rely on rigid predefined penalties or advantage-rescaling rules.
WQVfUbjLtk.method: SOCAL probes sampled trajectories to diagnose knowledge sufficiency and build step-specific hindsight. It then contrasts the policy's likelihood for each diagnosed search step with and without hindsight conditioning, using this discrepancy as a self-distilled signal to adaptively reshape local RL credit.
WQVfUbjLtk.key_idea: Contrasts policy step likelihoods with and without knowledge-probed hindsight to generate adaptive self-distilled signals for local RL credit reshaping.
WQVfUbjLtk.evidence: Evaluated on search-agent benchmarks at 3B and 7B scales against GRPO/Search-R1 and HiPRAG, including training dynamics and over-search rate analyses.
WQVfUbjLtk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear calibration-over-suppression framing, training-dynamics analysis, and empirical improvements over HiPRAG.
WQVfUbjLtk.main_concern: Reviewers note no constant-strength attenuation control to validate per-step adaptivity, limited methodological novelty beyond HiPRAG and privileged self-distillation, and question whether over-search is a primary issue in modern LLMs.

hD2wlFVVmn.one_liner: Computes Goldstein second-order stationary points for nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problems using first-order smoothed cubic Newton.
hD2wlFVVmn.problem: Second-order stationarity guarantees for nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax problems typically require twice differentiability or higher-order smoothness.
hD2wlFVVmn.method: Smoothed Minimax Cubic Newton (SMCN) uses randomized smoothing and inexact inner maximization within a cubic-regularized Newton framework using only first-order oracle calls. It targets epsilon-Goldstein approximate second-order stationary points of the primal function under Lipschitz-continuous gradients.
hD2wlFVVmn.key_idea: Combines randomized smoothing of the primal function with inexact inner maximization and cubic regularization to achieve Goldstein second-order stationarity via first-order oracles.
hD2wlFVVmn.evidence: Provides high-probability iteration and first-order oracle complexity proofs alongside synthetic numerical experiments.
hD2wlFVVmn.claimed_gains: Requires at most O~(kappa^4 l^4 n epsilon^{-5}) outer iterations and O~(kappa^{8.5} l^8 n^2 epsilon^{-9} + kappa^{6.5} l^6 n^3 epsilon^{-7}) first-order oracle calls with high probability.
hD2wlFVVmn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize relaxing twice-differentiability to Lipschitz gradients for second-order minimax stationarity as a meaningful theoretical gap.
hD2wlFVVmn.main_concern: Reviewers view the algorithm and bounds as a direct incremental extension of Guan and So (2026a), cite steep epsilon^{-9} complexity and non-implementable theoretical parameters, and find the synthetic experiments weak.

DZHfRt7ko8.one_liner: Controls multi-agent LLM communication topologies via joint reliability beliefs, counterfactual rollouts, and RL policy optimization.
DZHfRt7ko8.problem: Unrestricted information sharing in LLM multi-agent systems propagates unreliable reasoning, amplifying errors and false consensus.
DZHfRt7ko8.method: TrustFlow estimates a joint reliability belief over agents from interaction histories, evaluates candidate information-flow topologies via counterfactual rollouts, and trains a GRPO-optimized controller to choose interventions such as preserving reasoning, peer verification, or independent rethinking.
DZHfRt7ko8.key_idea: Estimates joint agent reliability beliefs and uses counterfactual topology rollouts to train an outcome-aware controller over communication interventions.
DZHfRt7ko8.evidence: Evaluated across four reasoning benchmarks with component ablations, robustness, recovery, and token-efficiency analyses, plus theoretical error bounds.
DZHfRt7ko8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the recovery-oriented intervention framing, joint reliability perspective on correlated errors, and multi-benchmark empirical evaluation.
DZHfRt7ko8.main_concern: Reviewers highlight a gap between rollout-based theoretical guarantees and the deployed GRPO controller, missing rollout-budget and controller implementation details, and ablations that do not isolate joint versus independent reliability.

vpl7e1Jkze.one_liner: Reweights RLVR token advantages using linearized Fused Gromov-Wasserstein distance from outcome-conditioned rollout barycenters.
vpl7e1Jkze.problem: Group-based RLVR methods like GRPO assign uniform advantages to all tokens within same-outcome rollouts, ignoring global semantic novelty relative to the current policy.
vpl7e1Jkze.method: HarA models each rollout as a distribution over token hidden states and positions, computes outcome-conditioned Fused Gromov-Wasserstein (FGW) barycenters, and measures semantic novelty by each element's contribution to FGW distance. An anchor-guided linearization converts FGW into a Sinkhorn-solvable Wasserstein problem to reweight token-level RLVR advantages.
vpl7e1Jkze.key_idea: Computes anchor-linearized Fused Gromov-Wasserstein distances from outcome-conditioned rollout barycenters to reweight RLVR token advantages by semantic novelty.
vpl7e1Jkze.evidence: Evaluated on LLM reasoning benchmarks (including Qwen3-8B-Base) against GRPO with barycenter-stage alignment analyses and training-overhead comparisons.
vpl7e1Jkze.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the distribution-level FGW barycenter framing for semantic novelty and the practical anchor-guided Sinkhorn linearization.
vpl7e1Jkze.main_concern: Reviewers question whether FGW outlier distance reflects useful exploration rather than noise, note unanalyzed gradient bias from weighting inside clipping, call 'hierarchical' overstated, and flag missing comparisons to SHEAR and response-length confounds.

UK937HbLDh.one_liner: Combines a mixed Mamba encoder-decoder with batched DPO and training-only local search for efficient neural combinatorial optimization.
UK937HbLDh.problem: Neural combinatorial optimization methods tightly couple policy updates with costly on-policy rollouts and incur high memory overhead on long sequences.
UK937HbLDh.method: ECO decouples trajectory generation from updates via supervised warm-up followed by iterative batched Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) on policy-generated candidates widened with training-only local-search bootstrapping. It pairs this pipeline with a mixed Mamba encoder-decoder that lowers encoder memory and recurrent decoding-state cost.
UK937HbLDh.key_idea: Pairs a mixed Mamba encoder-decoder with decoupled batched DPO and training-only local-search preference bootstrapping for neural combinatorial optimization.
UK937HbLDh.evidence: Evaluated on uniformly random TSP (up to TSP5000, memory at 10K) and CVRP (up to CVRP1000) against neural NCO baselines and classical solvers (Concorde, HGS).
UK937HbLDh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate treating NCO efficiency as a primary objective and note controlled evidence that batched DPO matches PPO at much lower training time.
UK937HbLDh.main_concern: Reviewers flag discrepancies in reported baseline numbers (e.g., LEHD), narrow uniform-distribution evaluation missing TSPLIB/CVRPLIB and strong baselines, modest inference speedups, and widening gaps to classical solvers.

5ozvmt4xYa.one_liner: Analyzes how small transformers implement context-invariant Bayesian evidence accumulation for latent common causes.
5ozvmt4xYa.problem: It remains poorly understood whether and how transformers develop generalizable internal mechanisms for Bayesian inference of latent common causes across novel contexts.
5ozvmt4xYa.method: The authors design a tractable toy fork-structure causal setting disentangling model mechanisms from the data-generating process and analyze attention and LayerNorm circuits in small transformers. They identify low-level representations that incrementally track Bayesian evidence about a latent common cause and generalize across contexts.
5ozvmt4xYa.key_idea: Probes attention and LayerNorm representations in small transformers on controlled fork-graph tasks to isolate context-invariant incremental Bayesian evidence tracking.
5ozvmt4xYa.evidence: Mechanistic interpretability experiments and visualizations on small transformers trained on synthetic fork-structure latent common-cause tasks.
5ozvmt4xYa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the latent common-cause setting relevant to world modeling and appreciate the controlled fork-graph analysis of attention mechanisms.
5ozvmt4xYa.main_concern: Reviewers criticize restriction to a single binary fork graph without testing colliders or denser graphs, unclear terminology and hard-to-read figures, and weak motivation or baselines.

nGGJmBLLaV.one_liner: Models structured conditional densities as location-wise marginals of a shared deconvolutional stochastic generator.
nGGJmBLLaV.problem: Structure-aware conditional density estimation under sparse domain coverage typically relies on fixed analytic kernels or covariances that restrict cross-condition interactions.
nGGJmBLLaV.method: Joint-domain Implicit Conditional Density Estimation (JICDE) represents the family of conditional distributions over an ordered or gridded domain as location-wise marginals of a single joint stochastic generator. Shared learnable local deconvolutional transformations encode domain geometry while adapting cross-condition sharing across smooth, sharp, and multimodal regimes.
nGGJmBLLaV.key_idea: Represents conditional distributions over a gridded domain as location-wise marginals of a joint deconvolutional stochastic generator with shared local filters.
nGGJmBLLaV.evidence: Evaluated across ordered and gridded structured conditional density estimation benchmarks against CDE and structured probabilistic baselines.
nGGJmBLLaV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value addressing sparse-coverage conditional density estimation via adaptive learned local cross-condition sharing without prespecified kernels.
nGGJmBLLaV.main_concern: Reviewers note a mismatch between fixed-grid transductive interpolation and general continuous i.i.d. CDE (inability to query off-grid coordinates) and limited novelty relative to convolutional neural processes.

WMB5WGQbwE.one_liner: Adapts decentralized STORM stepsizes and momentum via local direction energy, two-sample noise proxies, and neighbor max-envelopes.
WMB5WGQbwE.problem: Decentralized stochastic optimization faces unknown smoothness constants and trajectory-varying gradient noise that fixed-hyperparameter methods cannot adapt to.
WMB5WGQbwE.method: Noise-Adaptive Decentralized STORM combines locally accumulated direction energy, a two-sample noise proxy, and neighbor max-envelope communication to jointly adapt stepsizes and STORM refresh coefficients with fixed horizon-independent hyperparameters.
WMB5WGQbwE.key_idea: Jointly adapts decentralized STORM stepsizes and refresh coefficients using local direction energy, a two-sample noise proxy, and neighbor max-envelopes without knowing smoothness.
WMB5WGQbwE.evidence: Provides nonconvex convergence proofs under mean-square smoothness and synchronous networks, plus matched-budget experiments across noise regimes, networks, and classification tasks.
WMB5WGQbwE.claimed_gains: Achieves O~(T^{-1/2} + sqrt(sigma) T^{-1/4}) under uniform variance sigma^2, improving to O(T^{-1/2}) under bounded cumulative variance with the same hyperparameters.
WMB5WGQbwE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate addressing unknown smoothness and varying noise in decentralized optimization via neighbor-coordinated local adaptive scales and transparent cost accounting.
WMB5WGQbwE.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the bounded-variance rate degrades to plain SGD/AdaGrad-Norm (losing STORM's O(epsilon^{-3}) advantage), relies on strict uniform noise assumptions, and has dense presentation.

XeX8dYh4m8.one_liner: Decouples cost-map and spatial-guidance feature spaces and adaptively composes diverse dense representations per scene for open-vocabulary segmentation.
XeX8dYh4m8.problem: Reusing one dense visual feature for both cost-map construction and spatial guidance causes interference between semantic discrimination and spatial coherence in open-vocabulary semantic segmentation.
XeX8dYh4m8.method: CoDR applies Cost Spatial Decoupling to separate cost-map and spatial-guidance representation spaces, builds multiple complementary representations in each space via Representation Diversification, and hierarchically combines them per input image with Scene-Adaptive Representation Composition.
XeX8dYh4m8.key_idea: Assign cost construction and spatial guidance to separate multi-branch representation spaces and weight branches adaptively for each input scene.
XeX8dYh4m8.evidence: Evaluated on five standard open-vocabulary semantic segmentation benchmarks, with gradient-conflict diagnostics, component ablations using EVA02-CLIP and DINOv3, and inference-overhead measurements.
XeX8dYh4m8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the conflict between semantic matching and spatial guidance is clearly diagnosed and supported by structured ablations and strong benchmark results.
XeX8dYh4m8.main_concern: Reviewers question incremental overlap with PCA-Seg, lack of fair comparisons controlling for DINOv3 versus DINOv2 backbones, and insufficient analysis of whether diversified branches capture distinct cues.

3GOVSbRHVB.one_liner: Encodes seven physics-guided degradation priors into prompts that route low-light infrared-visible fusion into frequency-specific operations.
3GOVSbRHVB.problem: Low-light infrared-visible image fusion suffers from heterogeneous degradations across modalities, spatial regions, and frequency bands that uniform feature aggregation fails to handle.
3GOVSbRHVB.method: PDD-Fusion organizes seven imaging-inspired priors into exposure, high-frequency reliability, and infrared thermal groups encoded as spatial and global degradation prompts. These prompts guide high-frequency reliability modulation, low-frequency exposure-aware fusion, and gated infrared residual compensation alongside direct modality reconstruction paths.
3GOVSbRHVB.key_idea: Group seven imaging priors into spatial and global degradation prompts that dispatch high-frequency modulation, exposure-aware low-frequency fusion, and gated infrared residual compensation.
3GOVSbRHVB.evidence: Trained on LLVIP and evaluated for quantitative fusion metrics and zero-shot generalization on M3FD and MSRS.
3GOVSbRHVB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decomposing low-light fusion by frequency and mapping physics-inspired degradation cues to specialized operations is coherent, interpretable, and empirically strong.
3GOVSbRHVB.main_concern: Reviewers find the novelty incremental over existing prior-guided and frequency-based fusion methods, and note empirically chosen priors, many hyperparameters, and limited ablations.
